item.title: ACS Nano: Side-Chain Engineering Stabilizes Long-Lived Photosensitizer Radical-Ion Pairs for Hypoxic Photodynamic Therapy
item.description:
Mingxuan Jia, Yuqing Tian, Ping He, Yonghui Pan, Ruizhe Chen, Haolin Zhang, Linfang Yang, Quli Fan, et al.
Photosensitizer radical-ion pairs (PS+•/PS–•) can drive self-oxygen-supplying photoredox cascades for hypoxia-tolerant photodynamic therapy (PDT), but their rapid recombination limits photoredox efficiency. Here, we demonstrate that cationic side chains can regulate molecular packing in zwitterionic photosensitizer nanoclusters to modulate PS+•/PS–• formation and recombination dynamics, enabling self-oxygen-supplying photoredox cascades for hypoxia-tolerant PDT. Mechanistic studies reveal that triphenylphosphonium side chains favor compact cross-arranged molecular packing in photosensitizer (C3TPH) nanoclusters through their combined electrostatic and steric effects. Compared with its face-to-face-packed counterpart C3PH, C3TPH preserves comparable electronic coupling for charge separation (69 vs 82 meV) while substantially reducing charge-recombination coupling (45 vs 133 meV), thereby prolonging the PS+•/PS–• pair lifetime from hundreds of picoseconds to 21.6 ns. The resulting PS+• oxidizes water to produce O2, which serves as the starting substrate for a PS–•-mediated photoreduction cascade that ultimately yields •OH. This cascade enables C3TPH to achieve a 4.1-fold higher •OH generation than the commercial photosensitizer TMPyP4 under hypoxia. Accordingly, C3TPH achieves a more than 10-fold enhancement in antibacterial efficacy relative to vancomycin. This work establishes side-chain engineering as a design principle for regulating radical-ion-pair dynamics to enhance photoredox reactivity for hypoxia-tolerant PDT.

item.title: JACS: Micelle-Driven MOF Degradation for Enhanced Cargo Release in Micromotors
item.description:
Enrique Solano-Rodríguez, Jaime Fernández de Córdoba, Martin Pumera, Beatriz Jurado-Sánchez, Alberto Escarpa
Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored as cargo-delivery platforms, yet efficient release of the encapsulated cargo remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that anionic surfactant micelles actively destabilize the HKUST-1 MOF framework through Cu2+ extraction, converting a typically undesired degradation process into a mechanism for enhanced cargo release. Complementary mechanistic studies reveal that this process depends on surfactant self-assembly and on the accessibility and coordination environment of the metal nodes. The resulting framework destabilization greatly enhances the release of different cargos from HKUST-1. This mechanistic concept is subsequently translated into tubular MOF-based micromotors by confining SDS within an agarose matrix inside the micromotor cavity. Local surfactant release generates a micelle-rich microenvironment that promotes MOF degradation and cargo release while limiting bulk surfactant exposure and reducing the cytotoxic effects associated with free surfactant under the tested conditions. The resulting platform integrates micelle-mediated MOF disassembly with spatially confined micromotor delivery, providing a strategy for localized and enhanced cargo release from MOF-based dynamic systems.

item.title: Nano Letters: Localized Bond Polarization Stabilizes Site-Selective Zn Intercalation in Orthorhombic Nb2O5
item.description:
Ren Xu, Junsen Zhong, Tengyu Yao, Yao Zhang, Zhenming Xu, Laifa Shen, Mengsha Li, Yi Wang
Orthorhombic Nb2O5 enables rapid ion storage within a rigid, open framework. However, the intercalation sites and stabilization mechanism of multivalent ions, i.e., Zn2+, in their lattice remain poorly understood at the atomic scale. Here we provide direct atomic-scale evidence that Zn2+ occupies 4g interlayer sites, which fall into two classes: bridge-oxygen-coordinated sites and non-bridge-oxygen sites within Nb tetragonal rings. Density functional calculations reveal that site stability is governed not by geometric accommodation alone but by localized polarization of Zn–O bonding coupled to Nb-centered charge compensation. The most stable sites exhibit localized charge accumulation along Zn–O bonds, whereas a subset of bridge-oxygen sites shows partial electron delocalization toward adjacent Nb atoms. These results establish an electronic-structure origin of site-selective Zn stabilization in orthorhombic Nb2O5, providing design principles for multivalent-ion intercalation hosts and an atomic-scale basis for designing high-rate Zn storage materials to overcome the intrinsic kinetic barriers.

item.title: JACS: Large 77Se NMR Signal Enhancements in Solutions by Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization at 9.4 T for Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
item.description:
Yu Rao, Luming Yang, Maik Reinhard, Igor Tkach, Marina Bennati
77Se nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a key method to probe selenium functional centers in biology and materials science, yet its practical application is severely hindered by its intrinsically low sensitivity due to the low gyromagnetic ratio (19% of 1H) and natural abundance (7.6%). Overhauser effect dynamic nuclear polarization (OE-DNP) has recently emerged as a promising method for generating steady-state signal enhancement in high-field liquid NMR at room temperature. However, its application to 77Se has remained unexplored to date. Here, we present liquid-state OE-DNP as a route for 77Se NMR. At 9.4 T, we report 102 to 103 fold signal enhancements for organoselenium compounds, including the drug candidate ebselen, with polarization buildup within seconds. The large enhancements are the result of efficient electron-to-nuclear polarization transfer with OE-DNP coupling factors of ≳|0.4|, the highest reported so far at high magnetic fields (≥3 T) for NMR-active nuclei. The replenishable signal enhancements allow reaction monitoring by NMR on timescales longer than nuclear T1. As a proof of concept, we monitor a diselenide metathesis reaction over 48 h, capturing species evolution for kinetic studies. This effect can be further expanded to the heavier chalcogen, tellurium, as demonstrated by 123Te OE-DNP with similar efficiency.

item.title: JACS: Cross-Linked Halide Networks for Lithium Superionic Conduction
item.description:
Shuaika Liang, Feilong Wang, Wen Tang, Fiaz Hussain, Jo-chi Tseng, Zhepu Shi, Fucheng Ren, Jiuwei Lei, et al.
All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) hold great promise for next-generation energy storage owing to their high safety and energy density, yet their performance critically depends on solid electrolytes (SEs) with high ionic conductivity and structural robustness. Mixed-anion chemistry, exemplified by the Cl/O system, has emerged as an effective approach for designing halide-based superionic conductors, where partial oxygen incorporation distorts the regular halide framework and enhances Li+ mobility. However, we herein show that uncontrolled oxygen incorporation is prone to generate nonbridging oxygens (NBOs), which can hinder Li+ migration via Coulombic interactions. To address this, we develop a polyanion-assisted cross-linking strategy that promotes more bridging-oxygen (BOs) coordination and less formation of NBOs. This yields a highly disordered, frustrated energy landscape conducive to efficient Li+ percolation and rapid ion migration. As an example, PO43– polyanion cross-linked ZrClx halide networks (ZrCl4-xLi3PO4) are developed and exhibit ionic conductivities up to 2.8 × 10–3 S cm–1 at 30 °C, competitive with state-of-the-art rare-metal halides, while maintaining >10–3 S cm–1 after humid exposure (5% RH, 12 h). ASSBs incorporating these electrolytes demonstrate stable cycling not only under elevated temperatures (55 °C) but also under high voltages (4.6 V). These findings identify NBO environments as potential transport inhibitors and establish inorganic cross-linking topochemistry as a structural design principle for robust, high-performance, halide solid electrolytes.

item.title: Nano Letters: Charge Trapping and Synaptic Plasticity at an Individual Fe3O4 Nanoparticle in a MoS2 van der Waals Heterostructure
item.description:
Jeongwon Lee, Hyeongyu Choi, Taewoong Kim, Taekyeong Kim
Channel-averaged transistor measurements mask the contributions of individual charge-storage sites. Here, we directly resolve memory and synaptic functions at individually selected oleic acid-capped Fe3O4 nanoparticles embedded beneath MoS2 in a graphite/hBN/Fe3O4 nanoparticle/MoS2 heterostructure. Conductive atomic force microscopy reveals pronounced gate-voltage hysteresis above the nanoparticle but substantially weaker hysteresis in adjacent MoS2-only regions. Gate-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy confirms localized contact potential hysteresis, supporting charge trapping and detrapping in nanoparticle-associated states. Programmed and erased states remain distinguishable for at least 1000 s and across 1000 cycles. Gate pulses produce excitatory postsynaptic responses, paired-pulse facilitation, spike-timing-dependent plasticity, and gradual bidirectional conductance modulation at selected nanoparticle sites. Neural network simulations incorporating the measured conductance-update characteristics support their applicability to pattern recognition. By directly correlating local transport, electrostatic charging, and synaptic plasticity at one nanoparticle, this work establishes a particle-resolved approach for identifying how single charge-storage nodes govern memory and neuromorphic behavior in two-dimensional electronics.

item.title: JACS: Photoinduced Eosin Y Self-Disproportionation Enables Reactivity beyond Direct Excited-State Electron Transfer
item.description:
T. Rittner, C. Lucht, N. Rascón, A. Abramov, L. Hetzel, N. P. Ramirez, A. Sester, R. J. Kutta, et al.
Photoredox catalysis is commonly governed by the redox properties of the initially excited photocatalyst, which can limit the activation of difficult-to-oxidize alkenes. Here, we identify photoinduced self-disproportionation of neutral eosin Y (EH2) as an alternative activation pathway. In fluorinated-alcohol media, specific hydrogen-bonding interactions stabilize a minor population of the visible-light-absorbing EH2_acid tautomer. Following excitation and intersystem crossing, triplet EH2 undergoes intermolecular hydrogen-atom transfer with ground-state EH2 to generate the complementary radicals EH• and EH3•. Time-resolved spectroscopy shows that the alkene substrate does not measurably intercept excited EH2 but instead reacts with the secondary radical EH•, thereby separating photon absorption from substrate activation. Fluorinated alcohols further couple this radical-pair chemistry to productive C–C bond formation, as illustrated by highly selective polyene cyclizations. These findings establish photocatalyst self-disproportionation as a distinct mechanistic pathway that generates secondary reactive species whose reactivity is not accessible via direct excited-state electron transfer.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nonvolatile Multistate 2D Nanoelectromechanical Memories toward In-Memory Computing
item.description:
Pengcheng Zhang, Yueyang Jia, Shuai Yuan, Yuzhuo Liu, Maosong Xie, Zuheng Liu, Jiankai Zhu, Sheng Shen, et al.
Nanoelectromechanical systems (NEMS) are promising for post-Moore-era memory and computing paradigms, thanks to the low power consumption, high reconfigurability, and high-temperature compatibility enabled by the mechanical degree of freedom. In particular, NEMS based on two-dimensional (2D) materials demonstrate record-high frequency tunability, making them ideal for realizing frequency-shift-based computing. However, such frequency shifts are volatile, which seriously limits the applications of nanomechanical memory and in-memory computing. Here, we address this challenge by embedding hafnium-oxide-based nonvolatile resistive random-access memories (RRAMs) inside 2D NEMS resonators. By leveraging the ultrahigh frequency tunability of 2D NEMS resonators, we create frequency-shift-based multistate nanomechanical memories. We achieve nonvolatile coding and discernment of 32 resonant states, which can be further extended. We further show that in-memory mechanical computing circuits using such 2D NEMS memories as weights of artificial neural networks can achieve high-accuracy (>99%) and robust (both with and without considering device variation) inference operations. These results demonstrate nonvolatile multistate nanomechanical memory and its high potential for in-memory computing applications.

item.title: ACS Nano: Formation of Dynamic Nanoporous Shells on Bimetallic Particles During Carbon Dioxide Hydrogenation
item.description:
Yifan Chen, Andreas Weilhard, Louise R. Smith, William J. Cull, Demie Kepaptsoglou, Michael W. Fay, Paul D. Brown, Gazi N. Aliev, et al.
The hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol relies on dynamic interactions between metal nanoparticles and oxide supports, yet a comprehensive, particle-resolved understanding of catalyst restructuring during activation and reaction remains difficult to obtain via conventional ensemble-averaged or post-reaction characterization. Here, identical-location high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (IL-HRTEM) has been used to track the same PdCu nanoparticles on ZnO, from the as-prepared state, through H2 activation, to subsequent CO2 hydrogenation. The most pronounced restructuring occurred under H2 conditions used for catalyst activation, when the number of observable nanoparticles decreased by a factor of 2, their average size increased, and crystalline lattice features became more readily identifiable. Particle-by-particle tracking directly distinguished migration and coalescence processes from Ostwald ripening, demonstrating that both mechanisms contribute concurrently to particle coarsening. Support-derived atomically thin ZnOx overlayers start to grow over PdCu nanoparticles under H2 and continue during CO2 hydrogenation, concurrent with a slowing of nanoparticle coarsening. The ZnOx shells are dynamic, opening and closing subnanometre pores during reaction. Identical-location single-particle analysis showed that ZnOx shells restrict nanoparticle migration and coalescence while still allowing sub-nm dynamics to readjust particle shape, mediating optimized admission of gas molecules to the metal for catalysis. Our findings reveal the mechanisms by which a morphologically uniform PdCu/ZnO material evolves into a complex PdCu–ZnOx interface governed by coupled interparticle and metal–support dynamics. Importantly, the PdCu–ZnOx form correlates with high methanol productivity, linking catalytic function to the atomic dynamics of the PdCu–ZnOx interface resolved by IL-HRTEM. More broadly, self-assembled porous oxide shells may provide a powerful general strategy for stabilizing supported metal catalysts while preserving access to active interfacial sites.

item.title: Nano Letters: Interface-Modified Second-Harmonic Generation under Electric and Magnetic Fields in WSe2/CuCrP2S6 Heterostructures
item.description:
Xian Zhang, Zimeng He, Shikun Hou, Siyu Zhang, Junying Chen, Yixuan Chen, Jun He, Hongfei Liu, et al.
Multiferroic van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures provide a promising platform for tailoring the nonlinear optical responses of two-dimensional semiconductors through interfacial interactions. However, how electric and magnetic fields independently modulate second-harmonic generation (SHG) within the same heterostructure remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate electric- and magnetic-field modulation of SHG in monolayer WSe2 interfaced with multiferroic CuCrP2S6 (CCPS). Out of plane magnetic fields reconfigure the SHG intensity and principal polarization axis in Au-grating-supported WSe2/CCPS heterostructures below the Néel temperature of CCPS. Electrical bias modulates the SHG intensity and polarization anisotropy within the same WSe2/CCPS heterostructure. First-principles calculations reveal changes in the interfacial electronic structure of WSe2 between different CCPS polar configurations. These results highlight the potential of multiferroic vdW heterostructures for electric- and magnetic-field modulation of nonlinear optical responses, with implications for tunable frequency conversion and polarization control.

item.title: Nano Letters: Lossless and Controlled-Enthalpy-Driven Coassembly of a Nanosubstrate/Analyte for High-Performance SERS Sensing
item.description:
Qi Zhang, Shenglin Cai, Yangteng Ou, Daqing Li, Pengcheng Shi, Shikuan Yang, Qi Liu, Qingbian Ma, et al.
Concentrating analyte molecules in liquid solutions and delivering them to the sensitive areas of nanosensors are common challenges for all kinds of nanosensors. In this work, we developed a microfluidic–acoustic levitation integrated system that simultaneously enriches analytes and transports them into surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) hot spots, greatly improving SERS detection. The levitation system allows us to monitor in situ the relationship between SERS performance and Ag nanoparticle assembly during solvent evaporation. We discovered a second-level transient SERS state during the liquid-to-solid transition of acoustically levitated droplets, where spontaneous formation of a 3D hot spot matrix generated exceptional SERS enhancement through a decrease in enthalpy. By optimizing parameters such as the concentration of the molecule/nanoparticle, we made this state applicable to practical SERS sensing applications. This method exhibits notable advancements in on-site detection performance and practical utility for detecting multiple trace molecules in liquids.

item.title: Nano Letters: Friction-Driven 2D InSe Phase Transition
item.description:
Kexin Ren, Hongli Li, Zhenbin Gong, Zhao Liu, Youzhuan Zhu, Wenchao Wu, Xinchen Gao, Qingkai Zheng, et al.
Despite persistent challenges in achieving adjustable friction in conventional two-dimensional (2D) materials, this study identifies γ-InSe as a transformative solution. The atomic force microscopy (AFM) tip induces over 50% friction reduction of γ-InSe, with adjustment precisely controllable via scanning cycles. The inherent plasticity of γ-InSe enables tip-triggered γ-to-ε phase transition, which is verified by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) characterizations. The friction-tuning performance of γ-InSe exhibits exceptional stability across diverse environments, scan rates, and tip loadings, with structural integrity maintained through hundreds of cyclic scans. This work provides a solution for precise friction optimization and paves the way for customizable friction engineering, with promising applications in micro–nano manipulation, low-power electronics, and adaptive lubrication systems.

item.title: Nano Letters: Stateful Nanopore Sensing through Particle-Written Interfacial Memory
item.description:
Md Sifat Islam, Tomoko Nakada, Apoorv Umang Toppo, Yuki Komoto, Ryuichiro Abe, Makusu Tsutsui, Masateru Taniguchi
Biological ion channels couple molecular recognition and ion transport, enabling their response to depend on preceding events. By contrast, solid-state nanopore sensors are generally treated as passive conduits whose sensing environment remains unchanged between analytes. Here we report a stateful solid-state nanopore in which single-particle sensing and physical memory are intrinsically coupled. Nanoparticle trapping and release reversibly switch an alkanethiol-functionalized Au nanopore between two conductance states, and the retained state subsequently reshapes both the ionic-current signature and motion of the next particle. Finite-element simulations suggest a deformable vapor-associated interface, with an electrically equivalent radial thickness of approximately 24 nm, as the physical origin of the stored state. This interface retards particle motion, exhibiting longer and more asymmetric resistive pulses. The retained state also suppresses clogging by approximately 3-fold. These results establish a solid-state analogue of history-dependent biological transduction, integrating memory, sensing, and operational stability within a single nanoscale interface.

item.title: Nano Letters: Helicity-Resolved Photocurrent with Distinct Dominant Mechanisms at Electrode-Contact Boundaries in Few-Layer MoS2 and WTe2
item.description:
Xiaonan Zhang, Zhihao Zhang, Ao He, Xiang Li, Lingxiu Chen, Shixuan Wang, Xiaolan Xue, Chuanlei Jia, et al.
Helicity-dependent photocurrents provide an electrical probe of spin-valley-coupled transport in two-dimensional materials. However, polarization modulation can displace the focused spot and produce photocurrent or photothermoelectric signals at the same frequency, mimicking spin-related responses and complicating assignment of the underlying mechanism. We distinguish these contributions near electrode contacts in few-layer MoS2 and WTe2 devices by examining their dependence on phase retardation, sample azimuth, and focal-spot size. In MoS2, the circular polarized photocurrent (CPC) peaks near the quarter-wave condition and varies little with sample rotation, consistent with a dominant contribution from spin-to-charge conversion via the inverse spin Hall effect. In WTe2, the CPC varies nearly monotonically with phase retardation and depends strongly on sample rotation and spot size, indicating that beam shift dominates, although a weaker periodic component cannot be excluded. Thus, neither the amplitude nor the spatial pattern of a helicity-modulated photocurrent is sufficient to identify the dominant mechanism.

item.title: ACS Nano: Four-Dimensional Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy Nanoscale Phase Mapping of the Lithium-Metal Surface Passivation Layer
item.description:
Yiming Xu, Jinseok Ryu, Ben Jagger, Junyi Zhao, Mauro Pasta, Christopher S. Allen
Mapping microstructural features is vital to developing next-generation materials in renewable energy applications. However, the nanometer-scale dimensions, chemical heterogeneity, and beam sensitivity of these materials make their structural characterization exceptionally challenging. Here, we present a data acquisition and analysis workflow for four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) applied to a beam-sensitive lithium-metal filament sample with a surface passivation layer. By combining data dimensionality reduction with unsupervised machine-learning approaches, we perform real-space clustering to enhance signal-to-noise ratios across large data sets. Automated Bragg reflection analysis was then used to identify distinct crystallographic phases within the surface passivation layer. This approach enables nanoscale phase mapping of dominant species across large fields of view with nanometer-level lateral resolution. We identify lithium oxide and lithium hydroxide as the predominant crystalline phases in the lithium-metal surface passivation layer.

item.title: Nano Letters: Symmetric Molecule, Asymmetric Coupling: Insights from Blinking in Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
item.description:
Kanji Homma, Koushik Ranjan Das, Sudipta Dutta, Katsunori Wakabayashi, Tomoaki Nishino, Kazuhito Tsukagoshi, Satoshi Kaneko
Electronic asymmetry at metal–molecule interfaces is central to current rectification in nanoscale devices, yet its atomic-scale origin remains difficult to identify in individual single-molecule junctions. Here, we combine surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectroscopy with current–voltage (I–V) measurements to probe junction geometry and electron transport in a symmetric naphthalene derivative. Continuous SERS measurements reveal blinking, during which high-intensity SERS states coincide with asymmetric I–V characteristics, identifying a distinct blinking-on state associated with enhanced Raman signals. Vibrational analysis and transport simulations based on density functional theory and tight-binding theory are consistent with an asymmetric contact geometry that produces unequal molecule–electrode coupling and rectification. These results suggest that SERS blinking can serve as a spectroscopic signature of transient asymmetric contacts and provide a route to probing transient atomic configurations that govern single-molecule electron transport.

item.title: ACS Nano: Contactless Nanoscale Temperature Mapping Using a Luminescent Nanoparticle Attached to a Sharp Glass Tip
item.description:
Rachid Houssaini, Dawid Jankowski, Aleksandra Pilch-Wróbel, Catarina C. Haase, Luiz Gustavo Cançado, Artur Bednarkiewicz, Dawid Piątkowski, Sebastian Maćkowski, et al.
Temperature mapping of surfaces and surface structures at the nanoscale is of key importance in a variety of fields including nanoelectronics, optoelectronics, and biology. To meet this need, a range of scanning thermal microscopy techniques have been developed that utilize various sensing principles and probes. Because the temperature-sensing probe is operated in a contact or near-contact range with the sample to provide efficient thermal coupling, the probe’s heat conductance and heat capacity need to be considered in quantitative temperature measurements. This work demonstrates an isolated single luminescent NaYF4:Yb3+/Er3+ core@shell nanoparticle attached to a sharp glass tip as a nanoscale luminescent temperature probe operated in a noncontact atomic force microscope setup. We found that, in contrast to gold tips, glass tips, due to their lower thermal conductivity, do not measurably alter the detected temperature within the measurement accuracy of 1 °C. The thermal coupling efficiency between the heated surface and the temperature-sensing nanoparticle attached to the glass tip is sufficient to establish thermal equilibrium. Nanoscale temperature maps of an optically heated gold nanoparticle at varying heating intensities and of laser-heated monolayers of transition-metal dichalcogenides on glass illustrate the spatial and temperature resolution of the approach together with its broad applicability.

item.title: JACS: An Allosteric CLR N-Terminal Swing-Out Mechanism for RAMP-Mediated Adrenomedullin Receptor Selectivity
item.description:
Katie M. Babin, Ceren Kilinc, Samik Bose, Sandra E. Gostynska, Alex Dickson, Augen A. Pioszak
Three receptor activity-modifying proteins (RAMP1–3) form heterodimers with the calcitonin (CTR) and calcitonin-like (CLR) G protein-coupled receptors and determine their selectivity for six CGRP family peptide agonists. These ligand–receptor systems are drug targets for migraine headache, diabetes and obesity, and circulatory system disorders. Here, we used molecular dynamics simulations and pharmacological assays of receptor chimeras and point mutants to identify a crucial allosteric component of the mechanism by which RAMP2 and RAMP3 modulate CLR to confer selectivity for two adrenomedullin (AM) peptides. We found that the extracellular domain (ECD) of RAMP2 and RAMP3, but not RAMP1, stabilized a partially unwound “swing-out” conformation of the CLR ECD N-terminal α-helix to accommodate the unique binding mode of the midregion of the AM peptides. The inability of the CTR N-terminus to adopt the swing-out conformation contributed to the distinct peptide selectivity profile of the three CTR-RAMP amylin receptors. By exploiting the CLR swing-out conformation, we engineered AM antagonist peptide variants with enhanced affinity and selectivity for CLR-RAMP2 and -RAMP3. Our results reveal the long-sought mechanism of RAMP-altered CLR ligand selectivity and have significant implications for drug development targeting the CLR- and CTR-RAMP complexes.

item.title: JACS: Enantioconvergent N -Alkylation of Indoles with Alcohols Promoted by an Axially Chiral Iridacycle
item.description:
Gang Liao, Ran Tao, Yu Zhao
Achieving chemo- and enantioselective N-substitution of indoles presents significant challenges for catalytic method development. Herein, we report an enantioconvergent N-substitution of indoles with racemic secondary alcohols enabled by a newly developed axially chiral biaryl-supported iridacycle and chiral phosphoric acid. This borrowing-hydrogen process proceeds through an intriguing sequence involving transfer hydrogenation of indole, enantioselective reductive amination of an indoline intermediate, and subsequent rearomatization. Controlled reaction temperatures also enable selective access to the N-substituted indolines prior to rearomatization. The catalytic process accommodates diverse indoles and unactivated secondary alcohols without additional stoichiometric reagents, providing a direct and atom-economical approach to enantioenriched N-substituted indoles, including analogs of established drug candidates.

item.title: ACS Nano: Molecularly Woven Quasi-3D Covalent Organic Frameworks Enable Piezocatalytic PANoptosis for Potent Cancer Immunotherapy
item.description:
Xuan Cheng, Shuning Liu, Yujun Lu, Heng Ma, Yiqi Jin, Run Zhang, Qi Xu, Xingguang Li, et al.
Metastatic breast cancer remains refractory to current immunotherapies due to insufficient immunogenic cell death and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Here, we engineer a piezocatalytic quasi-3D covalent organic framework (COF) nanoplatform (PPyrr-COF NPs) through a molecular weaving strategy, in which aligned polypyrrole (PPyrr) chains are covalently integrated into the COF scaffold, enabling efficient piezocatalysis-driven immunotherapy. Theoretical and experimental analyses demonstrate that the covalent linkage between the PPyrr chains and the COF skeleton creates z-axis-oriented electron-transport pathways, increases charge density, and narrows the bandgap, thereby substantially augmenting piezocatalytic oxidation activity. Under ultrasound irradiation, PPyrr-COF NPs generate abundant reactive oxygen species, which trigger a distinct PANoptotic cell death pathway and robust immunogenic cell death, characterized by the release of damage-associated molecular patterns. In murine 4T1 breast cancer models, PPyrr-COF NPs combined with ultrasound irradiation not only suppress primary tumor growth but also inhibit distant tumors and prevent lung metastasis. These effects are mediated by systemic antitumor immunity, including dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, supported by transcriptomic analysis revealing regulation of PANoptosis and immune-related pathways. This work establishes a strategy for designing high-performance organic piezocatalysts and presents a noninvasive synergistic approach for cancer immunotherapy.

item.title: Nano Letters: Experimental In-Memory Neural Network Training in a 2T0C DRAM Array
item.description:
Junchi Cheng, Zenghui Chang, Quanyi Tu, Wenjuan Zhou, Renhao Xue, Ruizhan Yan, Mansun Chan, Xiwen Liu
Two-transistor zero-capacitor dynamic random-access memory (2T0C DRAM) is promising for neural network (NN) training owing to its fast, durable charge-based updates and nondestructive readout. Yet experimental 2T0C DRAM computing has remained limited to memory and inference because transposed multiply–accumulate (MAC) and incremental weight updating have not been jointly realized. Here, we report the first experimental demonstration of NN training using a fabricated 2T0C DRAM array with physical weight updates. Bidirectional access through the source/drain-symmetric read transistor enables forward and transposed MAC using the same physical weight matrix, with error standard deviations below 2.6%. Finite charge transfer programming further enables state-dependent bidirectional incremental updates, providing 64 states with linearity of R2 > 0.997. Combining these operations, experimental training on the array achieves 92.25% test accuracy for EMNIST recognition. These results extend 2T0C DRAM from inference-oriented in-memory computing toward training-oriented hardware.

item.title: Nano Letters: Understanding Texture Evolution Dynamics in the Electrodeposition of Copper Current Collectors for Lithium-Metal Batteries via Differential in Situ XRD
item.description:
Jakub Pepas, Yifan Ma, Guangxing Zhang, Zhantao Liu, Tianyi Li, Wenqian Xu, Jianming Bai, Hui Zhong, et al.
The texture of copper current collectors (CCs) strongly influences the lithium nucleation and growth in lithium-metal batteries, but evaluating the relationship between deposition conditions and texture is time-consuming due to the complex deposition process. In this study, we quantitatively analyze the texture evolution through in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) at various current densities and chloride concentrations. Time-resolved relative texture coefficient (RTC) analysis reveals that high current density and low chloride concentration induce the strongest {1 1 0} texture formation. Furthermore, we introduce a differential XRD analysis method that quantifies the texture of newly deposited material. This surface-sensitive approach reveals that strong surface texture emerges earlier than suggested by conventional RTC analysis. The strongly textured CCs exhibit lower voltage hysteresis and greater cycling stability than randomly oriented films. These findings reveal the dynamic relationship between deposition conditions and texture evolution while introducing an in situ methodology for rapid optimization of textured CCs.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nanofibrous Catalysts for Local Prodrug Activation through Bioorthogonal Uncaging Reactions
item.description:
Shadab Bagheri-Khoulenjani, Catherine Adam, Muhammed H. Rahaman, Guillermo A. Gomez, Olivia Morris Hanon, Jordan R. Hansford, Asier Unciti-Broceta, Ferry Melchels
Bioorthogonal chemistry through implant-based catalysis provides powerful strategies for site-specific drug activation, enabling therapeutic control beyond what conventional systemic dosing or local delivery depots can achieve. In oncology, this approach is particularly compelling because dose-limiting systemic toxicity often prevents therapeutic drug exposure at the tumor, limiting treatment efficacy. Despite its promise, in vivo implementation remains limited by challenges such as catalyst instability, insufficient spatial confinement, and uncontrolled diffusion of activated drugs. This Perspective focuses on recent efforts to localize and sustain bioorthogonal uncaging reactions within living systems, with a particular emphasis on heterogeneous catalytic approaches. Building on advances that employ metallic nanoparticles as bioorthogonal catalysts, we highlight both their successes and the outstanding barriers associated with biofouling, catalyst leaching, and mass-transport constraints. Here we propose nanofibrous catalytic implants as an emerging platform for localized bioorthogonal chemistry. By integrating metallic nanocatalysts within nanofibrous implants, these systems can combine high surface area, efficient reactant transport, mechanical adaptability, and prolonged catalyst retention. We discuss fabrication strategies, key biological considerations, and future design principles that may guide the development of safer and more precise implant-based drug activation technologies.

item.title: Nano Letters: Atomically Resolving Magnetic Triple- q State in Antiferromagnetic Mn Monolayer Interfaced with Bismuthene
item.description:
Yu-Tung Lin, Chia-Ju Chen, Chieh-Lin Lee, Nitin Kumar, Hung-Chin Lee, Yen-Hui Lin, Bo-Yao Wang, Stefan Blügel, et al.
Two-dimensional bismuthene with its unique honeycomb lattice and strong spin–orbit coupling (SOC) is anticipated to have an impact on monolayer (ML) noncollinear antiferromagnets. Here, we have systematically investigated the magnetic triple-q (3Q) state in bismuthene-covered (1 × 1)-Mn/Ag(111) by exploiting spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy (SP-STM) and density-functional theory (DFT). The characteristic checkerboard and stripe spin contrasts of noncollinear 3Q spin texture have been atomically resolved by SP-STM. Furthermore, the magnetic switching between magnetic checkerboard and stripe patterns and the absence of their rotational domains have been revealed in field-dependent SP-STM measurements. By considering higher-order Heisenberg exchange interactions along with SOC, the magnetic 3Q3 state turns into the lowest-energy ground state of bismuthene/(1 × 1)-Mn/Ag(111), where a uniaxial magnetic anisotropy arises from a local shift of atomic Mn spin relative to bismuthene lattice site. Our experimental and theoretical results therefore uncover the important role of bismuthene in the noncollinear antiferromagnetism of an AFM monolayer.

item.title: Nano Letters: Multilayered Gradient-Porous Piezoelectric Robotic Tactile Skins with Stress-Amplified Output
item.description:
Lei Liu, Ling Li, Shengshun Duan, Jiachen Liu, Yu-an Xiong, Xiao Wei, Meili Xia, Zhishui Chen, et al.
Flexible piezoelectric e-skins are attractive for robotic dynamic touch, yet their sensitivity often declines at higher pressures because soft architectures dissipate stress and weaken electromechanical conversion. Here, we report a structurally integrated P(VDF-TrFE) e-skin that couples gradient porosity, surface micropyramids, and three-dimensional interlayer electrodes. The symmetric microporous-macroporous-microporous multilayer assigns distinct roles to each layer, with outer microporous layers stabilizing stress transfer and the middle macroporous layer sustaining compressive deformation. This pore-size differentiation balances stress concentration and strain amplification, thereby mitigating sensitivity decay. Micropyramids intensify interfacial stress during dynamic contact at low pressures, while alternating poling and interlayer electrodes enable additive charge collection from individual layers. The e-skin achieves a maximum sensitivity of 1.71 V kPa–1 and a response time of approximately 12 ms. Integrated with robotic fingers and grippers, it enables hardness discrimination, texture-period recognition, and fabric classification.

item.title: Nano Letters: Coassembly of Membrane Proteins and Lipid Nanoparticles Enables Biomimetic RNA Delivery with Enhanced Cell-Dependent Interactions
item.description:
Anat Lyubin Haimov, Sivan Shahar, Tamar Gross Lev, Ilana Elizarov, Eden Pichotto, Rawan Mhajne, Lilac Haimovich Caspi, Assaf Zinger
Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are clinically validated platforms for RNA delivery, yet their synthetic surfaces provide limited biological functionality for cell-specific interactions. Biomimetic nanoparticles (BNPs) can improve tissue compatibility and targeting by incorporating membrane-derived components, but the two approaches have largely evolved independently. Here, we develop DUAL, a hybrid mRNA delivery platform in which neuronal membrane proteins are incorporated directly during microfluidic assembly of mRNA-loaded LNPs as a proof-of-concept model. DUAL nanoparticles were reproducibly assembled while preserving the physicochemical and structural features of conventional mRNA-LNPs. Proteomic analysis confirmed incorporation of multiple neuronal membrane proteins, including adhesion-related proteins associated with neuronal cell interactions. In vitro, DUAL particles exhibited enhanced association with neuronal cells and significantly increased mRNA expression without detectable cytotoxicity. Following intracerebral administration, DUAL supported robust and localized mRNA expression. These findings establish DUAL as a framework for cell-informed mRNA delivery combining nucleic acid delivery with biologically derived surface functionality.

item.title: JACS: A Unique Conformationally Assisted [2+2] Configuration in Cycloparaphenylenes Enables Efficient Laser Devices
item.description:
Pablo Pasqués-Gramage, Marcos Díaz-Fernández, Hikaru Kimura, Álex Farrando-Pérez, Masaya Kouno, Daniel Aranda, José M. Marín-Beloqui, Pedro G. Boj, et al.
Two π-conjugated macrocycles, namely the well-known [12]cycloparaphenylene and a newly designed macrocycle combining benzenes and rigid stilbene units, are presented for the first time as light-amplifying gain media in distributed feedback (DFB) laser devices. Both systems show good photonic functionality arising from a four-state photonic cycle comprising a [2+2] state configuration (two delocalized and two conformationally distorted localized states). The mechanism involves the generation of two optically coupled states through excited-state structural distortion induced during internal conversion, which reduces light reabsorption losses and promotes rapid population inversion. Comprehensive steady-state absorption and fluorescence and transient absorption spectroscopy studies are conducted in order to reveal the nature of the low energy lying excited states. Furthermore, amplified spontaneous emission studies of the compounds in polystyrene thin films, followed by the preparation and characterization of optically pumped DFB lasers, were performed. The results reveal new properties of these multifunctional cyclic π-conjugated molecules and unique structure-property relationships.

item.title: JACS: Chemical Programming of Stacking Order and Superconductivity Dimensionality in NbSe 2–x Te x Polytypic Heterostructures
item.description:
Xiangqi Liu, Haonan Wang, Ziguang Liu, Peihan Sun, Xiang Xu, Jing Jiang, Zhengyang Li, Ziyi Zhu, et al.
Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides exhibit electronic states highly sensitive to lattice symmetry, yet elucidating the structure–superconductivity relationship has been challenging due to the lack of a continuous structural evolution within a single material system. Here, we establish NbSe2–xTex as a model system, where Te substitution drives a sequential polytypic transition across the full composition range─from the low-Te 2H phase, through mixed 1H/1T heterostructured 4H and 6R polytypes at intermediate substitution, to ideal 1T and distorted 1T′ structures at high Te content. Combining comprehensive characterizations, we map both the structural evolution and the accompanying changes in spectral weight and orbital character near the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements reveal a striking phase-dependent superconducting dimensionality: the 4H phase (NbSe1.4Te0.6) exhibits enhanced anisotropy and an anomalous boost in the in-plane upper critical field, while the 6R phase (NbSe1.2Te0.8) shows suppressed Tc (∼2.8 K) and three-dimensional-like behavior. The combined electronic-structure and superconducting results connect the stacking sequence to effective interlayer coherence and the local spin–orbit environment. SOC band calculations resolve the distinct symmetry constraints on the 4H and 6R electronic states. These mechanisms fundamentally differ from conventional approaches by leveraging intrinsic, composition-driven polytypism to modify interlayer coupling and band structure. Thus, by establishing a definitive phase diagram that directly correlates polytypism with superconducting dimensionality, our work provides a clear roadmap for the rational design of low-dimensional superconducting devices through stacking-sequence engineering.

item.title: JACS: Entropy Engineering Accelerates High-Temperature Oxygen Evolution Reaction Rate via Spin Manipulation
item.description:
Geng Zou, Kaixin Li, Shaowei Zhang, Zijian Tan, Jingcheng Yu, Mingrun Li, Lina Yu, Xiaomin Zhang, et al.
The high-temperature oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity is closely correlated to the spin state of transition metals in perovskite anodes. However, the roles of entropy engineering in modulating the spin state and influencing high-temperature OER kinetics remain poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that entropy engineering of La0.7Sr0.3FeO3−δ to (SmNdPrLaBaSrCa)FeO3−δ (SNPLBSCF) induces a transition of B-site Fe species from high-spin to low-spin states. This transition enhances the d–p hybridization of Fe–O bonds, lowers the energy barriers for electron transfer and oxygen ion migration, and finally accelerates the high-temperature OER kinetics. Consequently, the SNPLBSCF anode in a solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) achieves a current density of 3.64 A·cm–2 at 800 °C and 1.6 V, outperforming most reported anodes. This work not only provides fundamental insights into the spin state-activity relationships of perovskite oxides but also offers a viable strategy for the rational design of highly efficient SOEC anodes through entropy engineering.

item.title: ACS Nano: Climate-Selective Dynamic Window with Temperature-Dependent Morphological Tuning of Zn Electrodeposits
item.description:
Min Seo Jo, Dong Bin Shin, Tae Hoon Ha, Hyeonbin Choi, Chi Thanh Tran, Kitae Kim, Bomi Kim, Jerome Kartham Hyun, et al.
Reversible metal electrodeposition (RME) dynamic windows are promising energy saving devices that enable dynamic modulation of incident light and radiative heat flow through windows. However, for practical application, physical robustness in diverse climate zones is necessary, especially under subzero conditions in high-latitude regions with high per-capita energy consumption. Here, we developed N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) based electrolytes for Zn RME dynamic windows operating from room-temperature (RT) to low-temperature as −30 °C (LT). The optimized device exhibits distinct optical modes in the electrodeposited state depending on temperature, with a reflective mode at RT to suppress solar heat gain and an absorptive mode at LT to enhance photothermal absorption of visible-near-infrared (VIS–NIR) light. This temperature-selective optical transition originates from modulation of Zn2+ solvation environments and diffusion-controlled growth, resulting in differences in electrodeposition behavior. In particular, a pronounced absorptive optical response is associated with void-rich porous morphology, emphasizing the importance of morphology control. In this work, unlike conventional RME dynamic windows that retain a reflective optical response regardless of temperature, we demonstrate temperature-dependent selection between reflective and absorptive optical modes in the electrodeposited state, highlighting the potential for climate-selective light and thermal management.

item.title: JACS: Nanoscale Flexibility Enables Low-Enthalpy Cooperative Water Sorption
item.description:
Audrey M. Davenport, Erik Svensson Grape, Siquan Zhang, Sahar Bayat, Kyriaki Koupepidou, Nao Horike, Kentaro Kadota, Ken-Ichi Otake, et al.
Passive, sorption-based atmospheric water harvesting technologies (AWHTs) have attracted recent interest as an alternative to energy-intensive condensation-based technologies. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer wide chemical tunability to design sorbents, but in practice, sorbents must retain moisture during humidity fluctuations, and small adsorption enthalpies are necessary for regeneration of the sorbent material. Here, we report that Cu(1,2,3-triazolate)2 nanoparticles with diameters less than 120 nm exhibit structural flexibility at the Cu2+ centers that enables a “breathing”-type cooperative water sorption. This cooperative structural phase change occurs only for nanoparticles that contain Cu2+, and not for the isomorphic magnesium triazolate. The phase change significantly decreases the onset pressures of adsorption and desorption compared to large particles and opens a practically useful hysteresis window in the isotherms, while maintaining small adsorption enthalpies (48 kJ/mol averaged over the isotherm, approaching the 44 kJ/mol latent heat of water at low RH). Mechanistic analysis indicates that adsorption initiates with weak electrostatic and dispersion interactions between water and triazolate rings brought into close proximity only by the distorted Cu2+ centers of the nanoparticles. Together, these results present a distinct water sorption mechanism and design strategy that leverages size- and metal-dependent lattice flexibility in a wide class of porous materials.

item.title: ACS Nano: Coupling O2 Activation with Proton Capture Boosts Carbon Nitride Fixed-Bed Flow Photosynthesis of Hydrogen Peroxide
item.description:
Xiaoying Peng, Zongxing Tu, Mao He, Suqin Wu, Dan Luo, Shou-Ri Sheng, Guiming Peng, Yongfa Zhu
Practical H2O2 photoproduction via the 2e ORR by polymeric carbon nitride (CN) is hindered by insufficient surface reaction kinetics, limitations in continuous reaction, and extra H2O2/catalyst separation. This work engineered fixed-bed CN networks with oxophilic Ni nanoparticles and proton-affinitive anthraquinone moieties, which enhanced the catalyst’s O2 adsorption/activation and proton capture capability. Besides, due to the electronic delocalization and extended π–π conjugation system, they imparted the catalyst with extended light absorption and improved charge separation. The as-synthesized photocatalyst demonstrated a 12.7-fold enhancement of H2O2 yield in flowing water, which reaches 3.6 mmol m–2 h–1 (1362 μmol g–1 h–1), outperforming most reported CN-based catalysts. Under natural sunlight irradiation, 581.8 μmol H2O2 was produced in 9 h using a 12 cm × 8.5 cm photocatalyst sheet. The practical application was exemplified by efficient on-site flow photo-Fenton degradation of organic contaminants with >90% degradation in 1.5 h. Electronic studies and local reactant enrichment investigation revealed that the adsorbed O2 at the Ni site and protons at AQ proceed to generate H2O2 upon participation of photogenerated electrons via the two-step 1e ORR process with high selectivity. This work demonstrates a successful surface chemistry design of fixed-bed CN networks for efficient continuous-flow photoproduction of H2O2 with facile separation.

item.title: ACS Nano: Process-Biomimetic Hydrogel with Time-Programmed Stiffening and Oxygen Delivery Orchestrates the Immune-Osteogenic Cascade for Bone Regeneration
item.description:
Shihua Mao, Pingan Lin, Yuchen Wang, Kaichen Lai, Xiaoyan Miao, Zhou Yu, Like Tang, Jintao Yang, et al.
Tissue remodeling progressively stiffens the extracellular matrix (ECM), generating stage-specific biomechanical cues that guide tissue morphogenesis. However, conventional biomaterials fail to recapitulate its spatiotemporal variation due to their inherently static and nonadaptive nature. Herein, we developed a biomimetic fracture-healing hydrogel that optimizes the osteogenic microenvironment through coupled adaptive matrix mechanics and sustained oxygen delivery. Matrix stiffening relies on the programmed, sustained release of Ca2+ from polydopamine-coated calcium peroxide particles (CaO2@PDA), which act as time-dependent ionic cross-linkers. We control Ca2+ release kinetics to achieve a stiffening trajectory from ∼20 to ∼61 kPa over 10 days, accurately recapitulating the mechanical evolution of native callus. This strategy autonomously remodels the matrix from a soft, immune-permissive state to a stiff, osteoinductive one, while simultaneously releasing O2 to mitigate hypoxia-driven necrosis and fuel angiogenesis. Moreover, RNA sequencing and complementary validation revealed that the dynamic hydrogel promotes integrin-mediated mechanotransduction into the TGF-β/Smad2/3 axis to drive osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs. In a rat distal femoral defect model, this hydrogel effectively enhanced new bone formation and neovascularization, while exerting notable immunomodulatory functions. Featuring spatiotemporally adaptive mechanics, this hydrogel provides a strategy for bone defect repair and promises to expand the biomedical potential of dynamically tunable biomaterials.

item.title: JACS: Resolving Chlorine Sites in Pharmaceuticals by Integrated Site-Resolved Zeeman-Perturbed NQR, Solid-State NMR, and Electron Diffraction Crystallography
item.description:
Alireza Nari, Jonathan Ngo-Minh Rusimovic, Patrick M. J. Szell, Mohammed Jasil, Victor Terskikh, David L. Bryce, Brijith Thomas
Many active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and high-value chemicals feature covalently bonded chlorine functionalities that influence molecular packing, stability, and bioavailability. However, site-resolved structural characterization of chlorine sites in powders remains challenging, especially in systems with multiple chemically or crystallographically nonequivalent sites, disorder, or hydration sensitivity. We report here a novel combined 35Cl nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR), 35Cl Zeeman-perturbed NQR (Zp-NQR), 35Cl solid-state NMR, and three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED/microcrystal electron diffraction) approach to characterizing powdered chlorine-bearing chemicals. Case studies of ketoconazole and chloramine-T demonstrate the utility of the approach in characterizing local structural heterogeneity and the hydration state. The role of crystal packing and noncovalent interactions on the spectroscopic observables is provided through an analysis of chlorzoxazone and five of its cocrystals, of which three are novel. Compared to ultrahigh-field NMR spectra alone, NQR and Zp-NQR spectra provide improved sensitivity to small changes in the electric field gradient and in the degree of disorder around chlorine. Experimental NQR/Zp-NQR data combined with gauge-including projector augmented-wave density functional theory (GIPAW-DFT) provide local structural constraints for a partially dehydrated chloramine-T phase. The refinement protocol does not require single crystals, and in the case of NQR experiments, intact tablets containing APIs are analyzed directly without further treatment or grinding. As a proof of principle, commercial tablets are shown to contain ketoconazole in the same crystalline form as that seen for the pure API. The general approach could be extended to other complex solids incorporating quadrupolar nuclei and is not limited to solid-form screening, polymorph identification, and differentiation of salts and cocrystals.

item.title: ACS Nano: Programmable Transistor Arrays Based on Wafer-Scale p-Type Monolayer WSe2 with Nanoscale Triboelectrification Tunability
item.description:
Ziyue Wang, Qiangqiang Wang, Tianzhao Bu, Guodong Xue, Ruifei Luan, Jie Cao, Feiling Luo, Rongwei Hu, et al.
Postfabrication customization of transistor arrays remains challenging because gate architectures and electrical functionalities are permanently defined during device fabrication. Here, we report a programmable gate strategy for transistor arrays fabricated from wafer-scale monolayer WSe2, in which nanoscale triboelectrification at the dielectric surface modulates carrier transport in the underlying semiconductor. Nanoscale triboelectric potential generated by charge transfer between the dielectric and the atomic force microscope tip enables reversible modulation between neutral and p-doped states in WSe2 with a maximum on/off ratio over 106. The programmable gating strategy allows the geometry, polarization strength, and spatial distribution of the gated regions to be arbitrarily defined and rewritten after fabrication. Using this strategy, we demonstrate programmable arrays with channel lengths down to 1 μm and an integration density of 4444/mm2, realizing NOT, NAND, NOR, AND, OR, and AOI21 logic functions. The proposed strategy extends the charge-based gating to high-density WSe2 transistor arrays with substantially improved gate modulation efficiency, while providing a versatile platform for next-generation electronic and optoelectronic systems with on-demand customization and dynamically tunable functionalities.

item.title: ACS Nano: Endometrial Micro- and Nanoplastics Exposure and Recurrent Spontaneous Abortion: Evidence from a Human Study and Computational Toxicology
item.description:
Yongyan Chen, Rui Chen, Kalbinur Kayim, Yuanyuan Wang, Xiaoyu Long, Tian Tian, Jie Qiao
Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are increasingly recognized as human environmental contaminants, but their polymer-specific relevance to uterine reproductive health remains unclear. We analyzed endometrial tissues from 82 reproductive-age women, including 43 with recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) and 39 controls, using laser direct infrared imaging, scanning electron microscopy, and pyrolysis-GC/MS. Endometrial MNPs were detected in nearly all samples, indicating widespread internal exposure at a clinically relevant reproductive site. Across Bayesian kernel machine regression, weighted quantile sum regression, and quantile g-computation, polypropylene (PP) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) showed the most consistent positive associations with RSA status, with single-polymer odds ratios of 11.48 (95% CI, 2.02–66.38) and 5.04 (95% CI, 1.08–23.19), respectively. Multiaxis integration linked these polymer-specific signals to a 210-gene program enriched in an SPP1 + macrophage-decidual stromal niche. NEAT1, PPARG, S100A8, and GSDMD were retained as mechanistic candidates supported by distinct genetic, expression, or pathway evidence. Network perturbation prioritized GSDMD-PPARG interplay, and drug-repurposing analyses nominated metformin for preclinical evaluation. These observational and computational findings suggest that PP- and PVC-associated endometrial MNP burdens may mark RSA risk through inflammatory maternal–fetal-interface programs, warranting prospective, multicenter, and additive-resolved validation. These findings prioritize polymer-specific mechanisms at the maternal–fetal interface for testing in future reproductive health research.

item.title: JACS: Catalytic Enantiodivergent Neophyl Rearrangement
item.description:
Wenxian Li, Xiangbin Bai, Penghui Gao, Xinxin Lv, Shanshan Cao, Zhiyong Jiang
The neophyl rearrangement is a long-established radical 1,2-aryl migration, yet catalytic enantioselective control of this process has remained elusive. Here we report a cooperative photoredox and chiral Brønsted acid catalytic system for the enantioselective neophyl rearrangement of tertiary alcohol-derived olefins. The reaction affords 1,5-dicarbonyl compounds bearing azaarene-substituted all-carbon quaternary stereocenters with up to 97% ee. Changing the radical precursor alters the preferred mode of catalyst recognition and reverses the absolute stereochemical outcome with the same catalyst configuration, providing access to opposite product enantiomers. The reaction also accommodates racemic olefin substrates, and experiments with the individual substrate enantiomers show that the chiral catalyst can counter their intrinsic stereochemical preferences. The results reveal how changes in catalyst–substrate recognition can alter stereochemical control during a transient radical rearrangement.

item.title: ACS Nano: Introducing Controlled Backbone Porosity and Functionality into Aerogels through Mesoporous Nanoparticle Assembly
item.description:
Linoy Dery, Elena Tervoort, Martin Kröger, Markus Niederberger
Precise control over the structural architecture of aerogels remains a central challenge, particularly in integrating well-defined nanoscale porosity within the aerogel backbone. Here, we present a nanoparticle-assembly strategy for synthesizing aerogels with controlled backbone porosity using preformed mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as building blocks. This approach decouples network formation from pore generation, enabling independent control over composition, structure, and porosity. The resulting MSNs aerogel exhibits a high specific surface area of 960 m2 g–1 and significantly enhanced adsorption performance compared with the corresponding powders, driven by improved accessibility of active sites within the hierarchical porous framework. The intrinsic surface roughness of the MSNs promotes interparticle interlocking, resulting in accelerated gelation, a lower percolation threshold, and enhanced structural stability during wetting, as supported by experiments and computational modeling. To demonstrate the versatility of this concept for sensing applications, a pH-responsive probe was incorporated into the MSN dispersion prior to assembly, yielding a solid-state pH indicator. These findings highlight the potential of nanoparticle assembly as a strategy for integrating controlled backbone porosity and tailored functionality into aerogels for applications in adsorption and sensing.

item.title: ACS Nano: Molecule Bridging Enables Integrated Design of a Hydrogen-Bond Network and Li+ Coordination Chemistry for Long-Life Solid-State Batteries
item.description:
Chaowei He, Hangjun Ying, Haonan Zheng, Fupu Liu, Lucheng Cai, Xudong Gao, Qinglong Zhao, Wei-Qiang Han
PEO-based electrolytes extensively applied in solid-state lithium metal batteries are always confronted with issues of sluggish ion transport and unfavorable interfacial stability. Although various supramolecular strategies, particularly H-bond engineering, have been attempted, their actual efficacy is fundamentally crippled by the structural lability of the H-bond cross-linking network (HBCN) and the chemical/electrochemical instability of conventional hydrogen bond donors (HBDs) at the interface. Herein, ellagic acid (EA) with abundant phenolic hydroxyl and lactone groups is identified as a valuable HBD and “molecule bridge” in the PEO-based electrolyte, together with the integrated design of a stable HBCN and favorable Li+ coordination chemistry. Through intense H-bond (C–C–O···H–O) and ion–dipole interactions (Li+···O═C–O), strong PEO–Li+ chelation is effectively weakened while enriching the Li+ solvation sheath with TFSI– and EA. Notably, the appearance of TFSI–-rich Li+ coordination and Li+–EA complex in situ generates a robust LiF-, Li3N-, and PhOLi-rich SEI, facilitating uniform lithium deposition and improved interfacial stability. Consequently, the Li|LFP batteries can achieve a stable Li stripping/plating cycle over 3500 cycles at 1C with a capacity retention of 83.8% at the 1000th. The stable operation of more than 200 cycles at 0.5C of 50 μm Li|LFP pouch batteries further confirms the practicality of the EA molecule bridge.

item.title: Nano Letters: Multichannel Three-Magnon Splitting in a BiYIG Nanodisk
item.description:
Sali Salama, Joo-Von Kim, Maryam Massouras, Jamal Ben Youssef, Abdelmadjid Anane, Jean-Paul Adam
Mode confinement in magnetic nanostructures discretizes the spin-wave spectrum and creates selective channels for nonlinear magnon scattering. We report multichannel three-magnon splitting in an in-plane magnetized, 500 nm diameter Bi-substituted yttrium iron garnet (BiYIG) disk using microfocused Brillouin light scattering. By tuning the static field, excitation frequency, and drive power, we show that a single-driven eigenmode generates up to three secondary-mode pairs with frequencies consistent with three-magnon energy conservation. Frequency- and field-resolved spectra identify the resonance windows of the decay channels, while time-resolved BLS reveals delayed secondary mode growth and different rise dynamics. An effective coupled-mode model qualitatively describes the redistribution of excitation among the channels. These results demonstrate nanoscale conversion from a single-driven mode into multiple discrete magnon channels and suggest potential applications in frequency-selective magnonic devices.

item.title: JACS: Halogenated Triazole-Based Metal–Organic Framework Achieves Ultra-Selective CO2 Capture under Humid Conditions
item.description:
Armando Rigamonti, Jacopo Perego, Charl X. Bezuidenhout, Sergio Piva, Erica Montanari, Angiolina Comotti, Silvia Bracco
Selective CO2 capture from humid, N2-rich flue gas requires adsorbents that combine extreme CO2/N2 discrimination with robustness under realistic conditions. However, only a few MOFs are able to combine ultrahigh selectivity, humidity tolerance, scalable synthesis, and structural durability. Here, we introduce CALF-20-X (X = Cl or Br) halogentriazolate–oxalate Zn-MOFs and a PVDF composite, integrating these attributes into an ultramicroporous framework. The halogenated Zn-MOFs are obtained by means of solvent-minimized liquid-assisted grinding followed by water-incubation route, producing a highly crystalline material. Halogen functionalization polarizes the triazolate C–H donor, thereby promoting directional C–H···O(CO2) contacts and enhancing electrostatic complementarity, as evidenced by an experimental isosteric heat of adsorption of 48 kJ/mol. Furthermore, this halogen substitution significantly restricts the size of the pore window inhibiting N2 uptake, and leads to the formation of perfectly CO2-fitted pockets. These combined features enabled a CO2 excellent adsorption of 2.89 mmol g–1 at 0.15 bar and 298 K, and CO2/N2 selectivity higher than 4074 for CALF-20-Cl, exceeding leading physisorbent benchmarks. The highly selective CO2 capture was confirmed by dynamic breakthrough experiments performed on a CALF-20-Cl@PVDF composite under humid conditions over numerous cycles, thus demonstrating its robust performance under flue-gas-relevant conditions. Competitive CO2/H2O breakthrough experiments, supported by GCMC simulations, demonstrate that CO2 sorption is favored at 21% relative humidity (RH), resulting in a 56% suppression of water uptake, and even remains competitive at RH > 50% and 318 K, a temperature relevant for carbon capture from point sources. These results highlight halogen-driven structural engineering for regenerable and humidity-tolerant next-generation CO2-selective MOF adsorbents with complete retention of the performance metrics.

item.title: ACS Nano: Supramolecularly Assembled Conjugated Polymer for High-Capacity, Fast, and Durable Potassium Storage
item.description:
Guangwan Zhang, Kang Han, Shuhan Jin, Zhenhang Zhong, Changyuan Guo, Ruohan Yu, Xu Xu, Xiaofan Chen, et al.
Potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) are considered promising candidates for large-scale energy storage owing to the abundance and low cost of potassium resources. Organic anodes, with their flexible molecular frameworks and abundant redox-active sites, are well suited for the reversible storage of relatively large K+. However, achieving high capacity, fast charge transfer, and long-term stability simultaneously remains challenging. Here, we report a supramolecularly assembled crystalline conjugated polymer, poly(tetraaminobenzoquinone) (pTABQ), as an anode material for PIBs. By incorporating abundant carbonyl sites into an extended C–N conjugated framework and forming an ordered layered supramolecular structure through in-plane hydrogen bonding and out-of-plane π–π stacking, pTABQ undergoes charge redistribution within the framework and local rearrangement of the stacking structure during potassiation, enabling high capacity, fast charge transfer, and long-term cycling stability. Benefiting from the synergy between its structural and electronic properties, pTABQ delivers a high reversible capacity of 460 mAh g–1 at 100 mA g–1 and an ultralong cycle life of more than 8600 cycles at 2000 mA g–1. Furthermore, a pTABQ//KMnF full cell achieves a high energy density of 284 Wh kg–1. This work provides a design strategy for high-performance organic materials for electrochemical energy storage.

item.title: ACS Nano: Inflammation-Programmed Tumor Endothelium Enables Active Nanoparticle Transport for Enhanced Cancer Therapy
item.description:
Yujie Su, Adeola Aminu, Jin Gao, Zhenjia Wang
Efficient delivery of nanotherapeutics to solid tumors remains limited by the tumor endothelial barrier, but it is unknown how tumor vasculature regulates the transport of nanotherapeutics compared to healthy vasculature. Here, we identify an inflammation-associated tumor vascular phenotype that enables nanoparticle transport across endothelium. Using intravital microscopy, we showed that inflammatory tumor microenvironments reduced the glycocalyx coverage on endothelial vasculature and exposed intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), thereby promoting active nanoparticle–endothelium interactions and transendothelial transport. Low-dose X-ray radiation to tumors at 6 Gy further amplified this vascular phenotype. Guided by these insights, we engineered high-drug-content paclitaxel nanocrystals functionalized with anti-ICAM-1 antibodies and demonstrated that combining endothelial-targeted paclitaxel nanocrystals with low-dose radiation significantly enhanced tumoral drug delivery and antitumor efficacy. This work reveals tumor endothelium as a programmable biological interface for nanotherapeutic transport and establishes vascular targeting as a strategy to overcome drug delivery barriers for cancer therapies.

item.title: Nano Letters: Nanoscale Optical Activation of Localized Metal–Insulator Switching
item.description:
Jesús López-Sánchez, Fernando Rubio-Marcos, Javier del Valle, Manuel Abuín, Fernando Ajejas, Adolfo del Campo, Jaime Dolado, Raúl Magro, et al.
Controlling phase transitions with high spatial resolution is essential for the development of next-generation electronic and photonic devices based on correlated materials. However, reversible and localized manipulation of metal–insulator transitions without direct electrical contact remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a strategy for optical activation of localized metal–insulator switching in VO2 as a model correlated oxide. Arrays of star-shaped Au nanoantennas, resonantly excited under near-infrared illumination, act as nanoscale energy concentrators that induce highly confined phase transitions through near-field electromagnetic enhancement and photothermal effects. Electromagnetic simulations reveal strong field localization at the branches and tips of the nanoantennas. Advanced in situ spatially resolved techniques, including synchrotron X-ray diffraction and confocal Raman microscopy experiments, confirm the localized phase transition. This spatially selective opto-thermal switching system provides a platform for light-addressable memory elements, neuromorphic computing, and low-power photonic devices.

item.title: JACS: Direct-to-Biology Bifunctional Screening Reveals Noncanonical Mechanisms of Targeted Protein Degradation
item.description:
Clara Gathmann, Soumya Jyoti Singha Roy, Wesley Wang, Amina Kelley, Julian Liao, Zeba Rizvi, Bo-Yang Huang, Madeleine Ghazarian, et al.
Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a powerful strategy for modulating protein function through small-molecule-induced proximity between a protein of interest (POI) and typically an E3 ubiquitin ligase to promote its proteasomal degradation. Despite significant progress, most degraders co-opt a narrow set of E3 ubiquitin ligases, motivating mechanistically agnostic strategies for discovering new routes to degradation. Here, we pursued a “degrader-first” approach using direct-to-biology (D2B) synthesis to construct and screen a 114-member library of BRD4-targeting bifunctional molecules to identify chemically tractable ligases that support TPD. Multiple compounds were found to induce Cullin-RING ligase (CRL)-dependent degradation, and two top hits were selected for mechanistic characterization. Unexpectedly, neither operates through canonical heterobifunctional E3 recruitment. Instead, one undergoes oxidative activation to generate a reactive electrophile that promotes degradation through DCAF11- or DCAF16-containing CRL4 complexes in a cell-context-dependent manner. The second acts through a bivalent bromodomain-binding mechanism that likely induces target conformational contraction and potentiates endogenous CRL3–SPOP-mediated ubiquitination. These findings highlight the capacity of D2B discovery approaches to expose noncanonical modalities of TPD while underscoring the importance of rigorous mechanistic deconvolution in interpreting screening-derived degraders.

item.title: ACS Nano: Defining a Surface ζ-Potential Window for Optimal Lymphatic Trafficking and Immunization of Liposomal Vaccines
item.description:
Ziying Yi, Xudong Li, Hongxu Li, Zhibin Xiao, Qianqian Guo, Ying Gao, Jianong Zhang, Pengcheng Zhang, et al.
How surface ζ-potential governs nanocarrier trafficking from the skin to draining lymph nodes (LNs) remains unresolved in vaccine delivery. Herein, we have constructed a library of 31 liposomal formulations spanning approximately +41 mV to −60 mV and screened the lymphatic drainage efficiency in vivo. The screen revealed a nonmonotonic relationship: LN accumulation was not monotonically linked to ζ-potential but concentrated within an optimal fitted window of −2.73 mV to −25.43 mV. Guided by this window, we designed four anionic lipids and formulated liposomes within the high-efficiency range. These formulations independently reproduced the predicted drainage window. Mechanistically, strongly negatively charged liposomes (<−30 mV) were physically trapped by the subcutaneous collagen fibers network, whereas weakly negative liposomes exploited transcellular transport mediated by lymphatic endothelial cells. Using the optimal ζ-potential, we coloaded the Axl receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor R428 with tumor antigens to develop a cancer vaccine that dramatically enhanced antigen delivery, elicited potent CD8+ T cell responses, and significantly suppressed prostate tumor growth. These findings establish surface ζ-potential as a fundamental design parameter for LN-targeted liposomal vaccines.

item.title: ACS Nano: All-Transistor Probabilistic Bits with Deterministic Clamping for Bayesian Inference and Integer Factorization
item.description:
Ho-Young Maeng, Sang-Won Lee, Jeong-A Han, Yang-Kyu Choi
Probabilistic bits (p-bits) have emerged as promising hardware primitives for solving inference and combinatorial optimization problems, while their implementations based on area-intensive CMOS circuits or emerging stochastic devices often face scalability and CMOS co-integration challenges. Here, we present Janus-type hardware for p-bits and their applications in Bayesian inference and integer factorization, composed of homotypic stochastic and deterministic transistors that share an identical structure yet operate through distinct mechanisms. The stochastic field-effect transistor (S-FET) explores the energy landscape through its intrinsic probabilistic switching behavior, whereas the deterministic field-effect transistor (D-FET) provides clamping, which is required to intentionally fix the states of selected p-bits and thereby enable the remaining p-bits to perform probabilistic computations under imposed conditions. This Janus-type architecture reduces the area overhead while decoupling stochastic switching for p-bit generation from deterministic operations for selective clamping. Using this platform, we demonstrate Bayesian network inference with local clamping for conditional probability estimations, as well as integer factorization, in which the output bits are fixed to the target integer and a subset of input bits is selectively clamped to suppress unnecessary configurations, reshape the energy landscape, and increase the probability of reaching the correct global minimum, thereby improving the factorization accuracy.

item.title: Nano Letters: Suppressing Irreversible Interlayer Migration via Enhancing Intralayer Interaction to Alleviate Voltage Hysteresis in Oxygen-Redox Na-Layered Cathode
item.description:
Bo Peng, Jing-Chang Li, Zihao Zhou, Yuxuan Xiang, Xun-Lu Li, Yu Sun, Yiwen Liu, Shaohua Guo, et al.
Oxygen redox-related Na-based layered oxides are promising cathodes to further improve the energy density of sodium-ion batteries. However, the oxygen redox-related cathodes are accompanied by ion migration during electrochemical cycling, which results in voltage hysteresis and poor electrochemical properties. Herein, taking Na0.67Zn0.28Mn0.72O2 as a model cathode, on the basis of extended X-ray absorption fine structure, Raman spectrum, and theoretical calculation, we confirm that the irreversibility of interlayer Zn migration originated from the weak Zn–O bond occurring during electrochemical cycling, which leads to large voltage hysteresis in thermodynamics. We then propose a universal local coordination environment regulation strategy by reinforcing the Zn–O bond to suppress Zn ion migration, thus reducing the voltage hysteresis and improving electrochemical properties. The representative Na0.67Zn0.13Fe0.15Mn0.72O2 cathode reduces the voltage hysteresis from 1.47 to 0.97 V and delivers an ∼1.9-fold higher capacity retention after 100 cycles compared with the baseline.

item.title: ACS Nano: Normalized Nucleic Acid Payload in Lipid Nanoparticles: A Perspective on the Harmonization of Published Data
item.description:
Erik Olsén, Bernhard R. Kirchmair, Joachim O. Rädler, Sabrina R. Leslie
Precise and consistent reporting of the nucleic acid payload per lipid nanoparticle (LNP) is important for advancing the understanding and development of nanomedicines. However, the reported number of RNA molecules ranges between ∼1–300 in recent investigations. To evaluate the RNA payload across investigations, we introduce and apply a normalized nucleic acid payload metric which accounts for differences in LNP size, nucleotides per RNA and N/P charge ratio. The normalized payload results in a similar value for siRNA- and mRNA-containing LNPs of different LNP sizes, where the average value of 73 ± 17 nucleotides/zeptoliter agrees well with the expected payload density based on molecular packing arguments. The use of normalized payload harmonizes the reported payload, complements existing payload metrics and enables comparison across samples and measurement techniques at both the single-particle and ensemble-average level.

item.title: JACS: Experimental and Computational Identification of Wide-Gap Quaternary Oxychalcogenides BaZn2OS2 and SrZn2OSe2
item.description:
Tomoya Gake, Koshiro Osuna, Kota Hanzawa, Nobuya Sato, Akira Takahashi, Hidenori Hiramatsu, Fumiyasu Oba
Oxychalcogenides have attracted attention as candidates for wide-gap p-type semiconductors in view of the energetically high and spatially spread characteristics of their valence electronic states. An appropriate choice of constituent cations would also enable n-type doping. However, reports on p-type doping have been mostly limited to Cu-based systems, which exhibit a strong p-type tendency due to hole generation and electron compensation by native Cu-vacancy acceptors. Oxychalcogenides with a practical level of n-type conductivity are yet to be developed. In this study, we focus on oxychalcogenides in the Ae–Zn–O–Ch (Ae = Ca, Sr, Ba; Ch = S, Se) quaternary system to explore new wide-gap semiconductors. Two as-yet-unreported compounds with wide band gaps, namely BaZn2OS2 and SrZn2OSe2, have been synthesized, along with four previously reported oxychalcogenides. First-principles calculations indicate that both BaZn2OS2 and SrZn2OSe2 feature direct-type band structures with low electron and hole effective masses, comparable to related compounds. Carrier compensation by native defects, however, is likely to make BaZn2OS2 insulating, whereas it can be well suppressed in SrZn2OSe2 by controlling the growth conditions. Systematic calculations of extrinsic dopants predict that bipolar doping of SrZn2OSe2 is feasible. Our results reveal the potential of non-Cu-based oxychalcogenides as a platform for the development of wide-gap, bipolar-dopable semiconductors, thereby stimulating exploration of related compounds.

item.title: Nano Letters: High-Resolution, High-Performance Quantum-Dot Light-Emitting Diodes Enabled by Intrinsic Energy Barrier Engineering
item.description:
Chengjun Li, Hao Tan, Chang Gu, Ting Tang, Kai Chen, Chaoyu Xiang, Ting Zhang
The rapid development of augmented/virtual reality drives quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs) toward higher resolution and performance. However, achieving high resolution and efficiency simultaneously remains challenging. Here, we propose an intrinsic energy barrier engineering strategy to address this bottleneck.
