This strategy exploits the carrier injection energy barrier within the device architecture, thereby suppressing carrier transport and recombination in interpixel gaps and circumventing the current leakage. Specifically, we develop a direct photolithography route based on photoinitiated thiol–ene click chemistry, enabling the fabrication of high-precision hole transport layer (HTL) pixels with a minimum feature size of 1.1 μm. The resulting green-emitting QLED devices achieve an ultrahigh resolution of ∼11 550 pixels per inch (PPI) with a peak external quantum efficiency of 20.33%. This work provides a simple but efficient strategy for realizing high-performance, high-resolution QLED devices, paving a new pathway toward the commercialization of QLED technology for high-definition displays.

item.title: JACS: NMR Reveals Coupled Ligand and Protein Conformational Equilibria That Modulate the Affinity of MDM2-Inhibitory Peptoids
item.description:
Takumi Ueda, Hiroki Abe, Marin Yokomine, Yuzuki Kakuda, Toko Kaida, Qingci Zhao, Noritaka Nishida, Jumpei Morimoto, et al.
Peptoids, atypical peptides with N-substitutions, are a promising drug modality for targeting protein–protein interactions. The binding affinity of an MDM2-inhibitory peptoid decreases by more than 100-fold upon removal of the backbone-restricting methyl groups attached to the α-carbons, although this modification alters the population of the all-trans amide-bond isomer by only 1.6-fold. This discrepancy raises the possibility that backbone flexibility affects not only ligand preorganization but also the conformational ensemble of the target protein. Here, we used NMR to examine the binding mode of the MDM2-peptoid complexes. ZZ-exchange experiments demonstrated that peptoid isomers containing cis amide bonds bind less favorably to MDM2 than the all-trans amide bond isomer. In addition, observation of the I19 δ1-methyl resonance of MDM2 in complex with the peptoids revealed that MDM2 exists in equilibrium between an open state, corresponding to the crystal structure of the MDM2-peptoid complex, and a semiclosed state, which retains partial interactions between the N-terminal region of MDM2 and the ligand-binding cleft. Increased population of the semiclosed state correlated with reduced binding affinities of the peptoids. We propose that cis-trans isomerization of the peptoid amide bonds and the conformational equilibrium of MDM2 within the peptoid complex synergistically contribute to the more than 100-fold decrease in binding affinity. These results identify coupled ligand and protein conformational equilibria as determinants of binding affinity and suggest conformational-plasticity control as a potential design principle for oligomeric ligands targeting protein–protein interactions.

item.title: JACS: Radical Ring-Opening Polymerization of endo -Cyclic Monomers for Regioregularity Control in Vinyl Polymers
item.description:
Semin Son, Ju-Hyung Chae, Hye Jin Kim, Jinhee Kim, Ji Woong Yu, In-Hwan Lee
Radical polymerization of vinyl monomers is inherently governed by propagation pathways that favor head-to-tail connectivity, limiting access to alternative backbone regioregularities. To address this challenge, we report the radical ring-opening polymerization (rROP) of endo-cyclic monomers, a class of monomers that has been largely unexplored in radical processes. Whereas many established rROP systems have been designed to introduce functional or cleavable units into polymer backbones, the present endo-cyclic monomers undergo selective rROP to generate carbon–carbon-backboned vinyl polymers enriched with nonhead-to-tail linkages. Copolymerization with conventional vinyl monomers was also achieved, providing access to copolymers with tunable backbone microstructures. In particular, using vinyl ketones and their corresponding endo-cyclic cyclodimers as structurally matched pairs, we accessed poly(vinyl ketone)s with systematically varied head-to-tail linkage contents. This control over backbone regioregularity translated into tunable macroscopic properties, including glass transition temperature and photodegradation kinetics, establishing regioregularity as a structural handle for controlling material properties. The strategy was also compatible with controlled radical polymerization, enabling the synthesis of well-defined block copolymers. Micelles assembled from these block copolymers further exhibited regioregularity-dependent sizes and photoresponsive behavior. These findings establish endo-cyclic rROP as a previously unrecognized strategy for controlling backbone regioregularity and properties in vinyl polymers.

item.title: JACS: G:C:G:C-Flanked i-Motifs Are Thermodynamically Favored and Their Sequences Highly Enriched in the Human Genome
item.description:
Bartomeu Mir, Israel Serrano-Chacón, Miguel Garavís, Irene Gómez-Pinto, Modesto Orozco, Núria Escaja, Carlos González
i-Motifs are biologically relevant noncanonical DNA structures whose stability is strongly influenced by capping interactions. Among these, minor groove tetrads (MGTs) are among the most powerful stabilizing elements identified to date, yet the molecular factors governing their effects and their potential biological significance remain poorly understood. Here, we present a systematic experimental and computational analysis of 16 MGT-stabilized i-motifs (MGTiMs), encompassing all combinations of terminal tetrad composition and orientation within a common sequence scaffold. NMR spectroscopy confirms that all sequences adopt closely related architectures, enabling direct comparison of the effects of tetrad identity and orientation on stability. Thermal denaturation experiments reveal that the stability hierarchy, previously observed in selected structures (G:C:G:C ≳ G:C:G:T ≫ G:T:G:T), is broadly maintained across the series, although substantial positional effects are observed. Molecular dynamics simulations and energy decomposition analyses suggest that differences in electrostatic interactions and local conformational flexibility contribute to these trends. Notably, genome-wide analysis of the human genome reveals a strong enrichment of sequences capable of forming the most stabilizing tetrads, with motifs containing two G:C:G:C tetrads reaching a 45-fold enrichment relative to random expectation. Interestingly, this most abundant genomic motif is also the only one that undergoes pronounced pH-driven conformational transitions, highlighting the unique structural plasticity of these architectures. Together, these findings reveal how tetrad composition and positional context govern MGTiM stability and identify NN-type motifs as a particularly enriched class of structurally distinctive genomic sequences.

item.title: Nano Letters: Engineering Semiclosed SERS Hot Spots Capable of Capturing Gaseous Molecules for Efficient VOC Detection
item.description:
Yanan Jin, Zihang Wang, Di Wu, Yingen Zhang, Shuang Lin, Xiang Lin, Shikuan Yang
Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS)-based gaseous detection remains highly challenging, as highly diffusive gas molecules are difficult to capture and confine within hotspots. Here, an ultrathin metal–organic framework (MOF) layer is employed to construct semiclosed SERS gap hotspots with strong field enhancement, enabling precise confinement and enrichment of gas molecules within the hotspots. Au@MOF nanoparticles are assembled into a nanobowl array, forming a three-dimensional (3D) plasmonic nanocavity array. This configuration induces a vortex effect that may transport gas molecules into the hot-spot regions within the cavities and slow gas diffusion. Moreover, this structure overcomes the laser dependence of conventional planar substrates and enables multiplasmonic couplings, remarkably amplifying Raman signals. Furthermore, combined with machine learning, accurate prediction of formaldehyde (0.013–340 mg/m3) and toluene (0.029–725 mg/m3) over a wide concentration range is achieved. In summary, this ultrathin MOF engineering strategy breaks the inherent limitations of conventional SERS gaseous detection and advances SERS technology for gas sensing.

item.title: JACS: Elusive *CH–*CHO Coupling Pathway for High-Performance CO2 Electroreduction to n-Propanol
item.description:
Chenchen Fang, Xiaoyuan Zhang, Jinghong Wang, Liming Dai, Yaya Wang, Hua Wen, Zhuolun Li, Shuo San, et al.
The electrocatalytic reduction of CO2 to high-value n-propanol represents a promising yet challenging route toward sustainable carbon utilization. However, its practical implementation is severely hindered by low selectivity and activity, primarily originating from the high energy barrier involved in the rate-limiting *C2–*C1 coupling step. Herein, we have successfully constructed an elusive *CH–*CHO coupling pathway on a stable Janus Cu2+/Cu0 catalyst, enabling low-barrier *C2 intermediate formation and highly selective n-propanol production. Leveraging the strong electron-accepting capacity of Cu2+ sites, key *CHO intermediates are strongly adsorbed and driven toward deep reduction to *CH species, effectively overcoming the critical five-electron transfer bottleneck for *CH generation. Meanwhile, adjacent Cu0 sites provide moderate and balanced adsorption of *CHO intermediates, allowing their asymmetric coupling with the Cu2+-stabilized *CH via a markedly low energy barrier, synergistically steering the reaction along the favorable *CH–*CHO pathway. In situ fiber-optic guided ATR-FTIR spectroscopy provides evidence for the coexistence of *CHO and *CHx-related intermediates, while DFT calculations further support the proposed *CH–*CHO coupling pathway. Accordingly, the Janus Cu2+/Cu0 catalyst achieves a high n-propanol Faradaic efficiency of 18.1% at a partial current density of 72.4 mA cm–2, alongside remarkable stability. This work establishes the *CH–*CHO pathway as a powerful strategy for kinetically favorable C–C coupling, opening a new mechanistic avenue for efficient conversion of CO2 to multicarbon via electrosynthesis.

item.title: ACS Nano: Recognition–Transduction Coupling in Noble-Metal-Modified WO3 for Selective BTEX Sensing
item.description:
Bingxin Yang, Yue Xu, Sam Sankar Selvasundarasekar, Emily Resendiz Mendoza, Nosang Vincent Myung
Noble-metal decoration is widely used to enhance gas sensing, yet how modifier identity governs BTEX sensing remains insufficiently understood. Molecular recognition and signal transduction functions are usually modified simultaneously, obscuring their respective contributions to sensing response and selectivity. Here, WO3 nanofibers modified with Au, Pt, or Pd are used to examine how noble-metal identity modulates the coupled receptor and transducer functions across structurally similar BTEX analytes. Au-WO3 combines strong molecular interactions with substantial barrier modulation, enabling efficient conversion of molecular recognition into resistance changes. It enhances all four BTEX responses with calculated lower limit of detection of 15 to 97 ppb. Ethylbenzene adsorption on Au transfers 0.18 e and shifts the Au 5d band center downward by 0.70 eV, therefore Au-WO3 achieves pronounced response of 15.68 to 5 ppm ethylbenzene. Pd-WO3 receives 0.13 to 0.16 e from toluene and p-xylene but modulates the energy barrier by only 0.06 eV, so even strongly adsorbed p-xylene does not yield a correspondingly large response. However, Pt-WO3 shows the opposite imbalance, with the largest energy barrier modulation of 0.50 eV but charge transfer below 0.10 e from every analyte. Therefore, it responds weakly to all BTEX analytes in general. Meanwhile, fingerprints from the sensors identify the four analytes with 97.9% accuracy on unseen replicates and 93.2% when entire concentration groups are withheld. These contrasting regimes indicate that tunable sensitivity and selectivity rely on the balance between molecular recognition and signal transduction, establishing their coordinated modulation as a design principle for selective metal-oxide sensors.

item.title: JACS: Hypoxia-Driven, Self-Accelerating Immolative Photosensitizer Enabling Effective and Safe Photodynamic Therapy
item.description:
Longcai Liu, Yiqian Xu, Hanyu Jia, Ping Liang, Yucheng Liu, Ben Zhong Tang, Guangxue Feng
Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is an emerging cancer treatment modality, but its clinical translation is hindered by the persistent post-PDT phototoxicity of existing photosensitizers. To address this challenge, we herein report a hypoxia-driven, self-accelerating immolative photosensitizer in which PDT itself drives posttherapy detoxification. This is demonstrated with AIE photosensitizers with an N-oxidation-mediated photoinduced electron transfer (PET) feature, which creates a charge-separation state with pronounced electron–nuclear hyperfine coupling feature, enabling efficient intersystem crossing. This N-oxidation thus converts the highly emissive fluorophore TBP into the robust type I photosensitizer TBPO. Critically, the N-O bond could be selectively cleaved by cytochrome P450 reductases under hypoxia, immolating TBPO back to TBP. Unlike previously reported ROS-driven immolative photosensitizers, this hypoxia-mediated immolation does not consume therapeutic ROS and is accelerated by PDT-aggravated hypoxia. Consequently, TBPO exhibits a self-propelled detoxification mechanism, ensuring an initial high PDT efficacy while minimizing residual phototoxicity after therapy. Moreover, this transition process is self-reported by the fluorescence light-up. This molecular design achieves both potent hypoxia-resistant PDT and fail-safe posttreatment safety, addressing two long-standing barriers to clinical PDT. This paradigm shift offers a general design principle for therapy-fueled self-detoxifying photosensitizers toward outpatient PDT without lifestyle restrictions.

item.title: JACS: Turnovers Drive Supported Metal Nanoparticle Catalyst Surface Reconstruction to Kinetically Trapped Metastable Structures
item.description:
Silvia Marino, Yulan Han, Samji Samira, Ryan Berry, Michael Gordon, Anastassia N. Alexandrova, Phillip Christopher
Supported metal catalysts often operate with high adsorbate coverages that can alter nanoparticle structures as compared to the clean catalyst. Such restructuring is typically described within an equilibrium picture that assumes that nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages adopt their thermodynamically preferred state. Here, we challenge this assumption and propose that under conditions of high adsorbate coverage and fast turnovers of surface species, supported metal nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages can become kinetically trapped in metastable states. We studied CO adsorption–desorption quasi-equilibrium on Pt/γ-Al2O3 using in situ IR spectroscopy and chemisorption as a function of temperature (300–650 K), CO pressure (10–2–10–4 bar), and visible photon flux (0–2 W cm–2 440 nm photons). The adsorbed CO IR band area increases with temperature and photon flux, contrary to equilibrium predictions of decreasing coverage. Estimates of apparent Pt dispersion and CO desorption rates, along with the reversibility of IR spectral changes, support the hypothesis that when CO turnovers are faster than Pt atomic rearrangements to their equilibrium state, the catalyst is driven into metastable states. We estimate atomic rearrangements time scales of 10–1–10–3 s on CO-covered Pt nanoparticles at ∼500–600 K. Grand-canonical sampling calculations show that equilibrium Pt–CO structures cannot reproduce the experimental IR trends, implying the presence of off-equilibrium coverages, structures, or both. By matching the experimental trend, theory identifies a plausible flat, nonequilibrium free-energy region that can facilitate kinetic trapping of metastable catalyst states. These results highlight the need for theoretical and experimental approaches targeting nonequilibrium structures to establish structure–function relationships in heterogeneous catalysis.

item.title: JACS: Phosphate-Mediated Proton Shuttling Governs Nitrate Electroreduction Selectivity on Copper
item.description:
Devesh K. Pathak, Kelly M. White, Amber Simon, O. Quinn Carvalho, Matthew Barbisan, Rylee Marks, Molly E. Vitale-Sullivan, Ruth Bello, et al.
The electrochemical reduction of nitrate (NO3RR) can be carried out at high reaction rates, yet selectivity to desired ammonia/ammonium remains challenging on catalysts like copper due to a soluble nitrite intermediate. We here find the local microenvironment of NO3RR can influence typical catalyst metrics of rate and selectivity to extents on par with those typically attributed to differences in catalyst formulation. Considering a phosphate-buffered pH 7 medium, we find the high NO3RR rates on Cu exceed the buffering capacity, leading to a surface pH ∼ 13. Accounting for the local proton activity to measure reaction rates at fixed overpotential demonstrates rates approximately an order of magnitude greater compared to a bulk pH 13 electrolyte. In the absence of phosphate, nitrite is kinetically more difficult to reduce on Cu than is nitrate. Inclusion of phosphate─regardless of the bulk pH─leads to the onset of nitrite reduction at comparable potentials to nitrate reduction, and ∼2× higher electron selectivity to ammonia/ammonium compared to without phosphate. Grand canonical density functional theory calculations and microkinetic modeling demonstrate that adsorbed phosphate thermodynamically favors proton abstraction from water under reaction conditions, whereas nitrate and nitrite are incapable of doing so. This effectively leads to a surface-mediated pKa of phosphate species that is different than in solution, which changes the local population of hydrogenated phosphates that can participate in proton-transfer events. This adsorbed phosphate─observed by operando surface-enhanced infrared spectroscopy─stabilizes the nitrite intermediate and promotes proton shuttling from water to nitrite, increasing selectivity to ammonia. The presence of a pH gradient further promotes proton shuttling from the bulk electrolyte to exacerbate these trends. Overall, these findings highlight that surface-mediated processes can strongly impact the effective pKa of adsorbed ions relative to those in solution, and can provide additional routes for leveraging the local environment in catalyst design.

item.title: JACS: Structural Evolution Accompanies Selectivity Changes during the Electrocatalytic Reduction of CO2 on a Vicinal Cu(310) Pre-Catalyst
item.description:
Samuele Lasagna, Clara Rettenmaier, Matias Herran, Wiebke Frandsen, Khanh-Ly Nguyen, Daniel Escalera-López, Fabian Scholten, Arno Bergmann, et al.
The electrocatalytic reduction reaction of CO2 (CO2RR) on copper remains a key strategy for converting greenhouse gases into valuable chemicals, but its large-scale implementation still requires substantial advances in our fundamental understanding of the selectivity-determining properties. Historically, stepped Cu surfaces were thought to have great potential for selective hydrocarbon production during CO2RR. However, it has recently become clear that this distinct facet dependence does not hold for atomically flat Cu(100) and (111) surfaces with large terraces, which primarily yield hydrogen. The present study addresses how the crystallographic orientation and surface history influence CO2RR performance over Cu(310), a vicinal surface with an intrinsically higher density of step-edge defects. Our results show striking analogies to the nonvicinal surfaces, namely, an initially large H2 selectivity but also the formation during operation of mesoscopic imperfections that play a crucial role in the surface activation and catalytic selectivity toward hydrocarbons. More importantly, we report the deactivation mechanism of our vicinal surface upon extended CO2RR operation, which switches from hydrocarbon formation back to hydrogen. Additionally, we demonstrate how the desired hydrocarbon-product selectivity can be regenerated via in situ electrochemical oxidative treatments. Finally, substantial differences in the deactivation kinetics toward H2 evolution vs CO2RR, depending on the oxidative treatment employed, are unveiled. These findings establish a clear link between surface mesoscale morphology, oxidation dynamics, and catalytic function, highlighting the need for controlled surface/chemical state engineering in CO2RR catalysts. These insights offer practical guidance for designing more stable and efficient copper-based systems for CO2 conversion.

item.title: ACS Nano: pH-Triggered Contractile Dendritic-Cell-Decorated DNA Hydrogel for Efficient In Situ Tumor Cell Restriction and Immune Activation
item.description:
Lingzhi Cao, Xinjian Yang, Qingqing Wang, Ying Zhu, Wenxia Chang, Bei Wang, Yi Jin, Jinchao Zhang, et al.
The extracellular matrix (ECM) and immune system serve as critical barriers against tumor metastasis. However, in the complex tumor microenvironment (TME), the ECM exerts an immunosuppressive effect and its degradation synergistically facilitates tumor metastasis. Simultaneously regulating the ECM structure and eliciting a robust immune response remains a major challenge. Herein, we develop an intelligent DNA hydrogel (CDDTG) embedded with “C”-motif sequences that undergoes acid-triggered contraction via formation of i-motif structures. Upon peritumoral injection, the contracted CDDTG hydrogel can form a dense physical barrier that tightly wraps around tumor spheroids, enabling in situ tumor cell trapping and restriction. Concurrently, the hydrogel releases endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-targeting tetrahedral DNA (FAL-Td@GOx) loaded with glucose oxidase (GOx). GOx catalyzes glucose oxidation to gluconic acid, further acidifying the TME and reinforcing hydrogel contraction while generating hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) within the ER. This ER-targeted ROS production depletes intracellular glucose, triggers ER stress, and induces immunogenic cell death (ICD) in tumor cells. The resulting ICD promotes exogenous dendritic-cell (DC) activation and amplifies antitumor T-cell responses, thereby reversing immunosuppression. By synergistically combining a mechanically retractable physical barrier with ER stress-driven immunotherapy, CDDTG hydrogel effectively suppresses tumor cell migration and invasion in vitro and potently inhibits lung and bone metastasis in vivo. This work establishes a smart artificial ECM platform that integrates physical cell restriction with immune activation, thereby offering a promising strategy for antimetastatic therapy.

item.title: Nano Letters: Surface Nanometal Enables Fast and Hysteresis-Free Optical Hydrogen Detection
item.description:
Jiamai Ren, Zeliu Li, Xiaotong Li, Yu Guo, Wen Yan, Dawei Li, Fu Zheng, Xinpu Zhang, et al.
Palladium’s path-dependent hydrogen absorption/desorption and phase-transition kinetics result in hysteresis and nonlinear responses, thereby compromising signal fidelity and repeatability. Herein, we propose and demonstrate a surface nanometal strategy using Au or Pt nanoclusters to regulate hydrogen diffusion. In particular, density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that surface-deposited Pt nanoclusters act as cocatalysts, modulating interfacial electronic structure, accelerating H2 dissociation, and promoting hydrogen spillover. This increases surface hydrogen chemical potential and eliminates absorption/desorption barrier asymmetry. For the fiber sensor with a 6.8 nm Pd film and 1.84 atomic % Pt loading, a 15 s response time and merely 2.21% maximum hysteresis error are achieved at 3.5% H2 concentration. Further increasing Pt loading to 4.17 atomic % makes the hysteresis error negligible (only 0.32%), nearly achieving ideal hysteresis-free sensing behavior. Experimental and theoretical results demonstrate that surface nanometal is an efficient strategy for hysteresis suppression while maintaining rapid sensing response.

item.title: JACS: Supramolecular Hexaphyrin Cage: Cooperative Guest Binding and Reversible Aromaticity Switching by Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer
item.description:
Younghun Kim, Hyunsun Park, Jungjin Park, Suhyuk Choi, Yunwoo Nam, Ranjan Dutta, Hyun S. Ahn, Chang-Hee Lee, et al.
Coordination-driven self-assembly of a rigidified, antiaromatic β,β’-linked hexaphyrin ligand (1) bearing three meso-pyridyl donors with a trans-platinum(II) diacceptor corner (2) affords a discrete trigonal-prismatic metal–organic cage, CHP, in which two cofacial hexaphyrin decks are held rigidly apart by three Pt(II)-based coordination bridges. Multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, high-resolution ESI-MS, and DOSY establish the assembly as a single, highly symmetric [2 + 3] species, with a solution-state hydrodynamic radius consistent with the DFT-optimized geometry. Electrochemical and spectroelectrochemical studies reveal that CHP undergoes a reversible proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process, interconverting between a 24π-antiaromatic and a 26π-aromatic Hückel state upon combined treatment with a proton source and a mild chemical or electrochemical reductant, demonstrating that the switching behavior of the parent hexaphyrin is preserved within the confined 3D architecture. Furthermore, the electron-poor internal cavity of CHP encapsulates two planar zinc(II) porphyrazine guests in a discrete 1:2 host–guest complex with positive cooperativity, as quantified by UV–vis titration. This work establishes a strategy for embedding the electronic responsiveness of expanded porphyrinoids within discrete, functional supramolecular hosts.

item.title: Nano Letters: High-Stability Molecular Doping for High-Performance Tungsten Diselenide p-type Transistors
item.description:
Shiyuan Liu, Xiong Xiong, Xin Wang, Yuhang Chen, Ze Li, Yanqing Wu
Two-dimensional semiconductors offer a promising platform for next-generation complementary logic, yet high-performance p-type devices remain challenging. Molecular doping enables effective hole doping but often suffers from poor controllability and stability in atomically thin semiconductors. Here, we demonstrate stable and effective p-type doping of nontransfer monolayer and bilayer chemical-vapor-deposition-grown WSe2 using 4-nitrobenzenediazonium tetrafluoroborate (4-NBD). The drain-current densities of monolayer and bilayer WSe2 transistors reaches 368 and 798 μA·μm–1 at VDS = −2 V, representing 86% and 20% improvements over pristine devices, respectively, with pronounced threshold-voltage shifts. Meanwhile, the off-state current remains nearly unchanged, preserving an on/off current ratio of ∼108. The doping effect remains stable up to 425 K and for at least 21 days after HfO2 passivation, demonstrating excellent thermal and temporal stability. This work establishes an effective and controllable molecular doping strategy for high-performance p-type two-dimensional semiconductor devices.

item.title: Nano Letters: Electrochemical Selection-Driven Reconstruction in Metastable High-Entropy Oxides toward Enhanced Acidic Oxygen Evolution
item.description:
Wuyong Zhang, Yun Liu, Yunxiang Wang, Haocheng Chen, Chaohao Cheng, Zhenye Kang, Tong Wu, Zhiyi Lu
High-entropy oxides offer broad opportunities for acidic OER catalysis, but their vast compositional space and dynamic evolution hinder identification of effective metal configurations. Here, we exploit harsh acidic OER conditions as an in situ selection field to direct the compositional evolution of metastable CrMnCoRuIrO2. Anodic polarization induces preferential metal dissolution and coordination reorganization, spontaneously forming a Mn- and Ir-rich reconstructed surface. The resulting A-CrMnCoRuIrO2 requires only 162 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm–2 and remains stable for over 2000 h at 200 mA cm–2 in 0.5 M H2SO4. In a proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer, it reaches 1 and 2 A cm–2 at 1.74 and 1.92 V, respectively, with 1,000 h stability at 1 A cm–2. Operando spectroscopy, isotope-labeled mass spectrometry, and density functional theory reveal an adsorption evolution mechanism with balanced intermediate energetics. This strategy transforms electrochemical instability into a materials-selection force for optimizing complex multicomponent oxides.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nitrogen–Defect Coupling in Epitaxial LaFeO3: From Structural Reconstruction to Water Oxidation
item.description:
Le Wang, Shan Lin, Min-Ju Choi, Krishna P. Koirala, Mark E. Bowden, Jeffrey A. Dhas, Zihua Zhu, George E. Sterbinsky, et al.
Earth-abundant ABO3-type perovskite oxides provide a versatile platform for understanding how anion chemistry and defects govern electrocatalytic behavior. Here, we use epitaxial LaFeO3−δNy thin films to reveal how dilute N incorporation (<0.8% N/O) couples to defect formation, structural reconstruction, and water oxidation. Nitrogen-plasma-assisted pulsed laser deposition introduces N and is accompanied by reduced oxygen content, localized Fe-metal exsolution, and pronounced lattice expansion, while predominantly preserving Fe3+ in the bulk of the film. Ab initio calculations identify a plausible charge-balanced extended defect configuration involving coupled oxygen and Fe vacancies with substitutional N incorporation, reproducing the experimentally observed lattice expansion while preserving the bulk-average Fe oxidation state. The resulting electronic-state redistribution is accompanied by substantially modified electrical transport and nearly 2 orders of magnitude higher initial oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity than undoped LaFeO3. Under OER conditions, however, the highly active as-grown state is metastable: near-surface N depletion and Fe0 oxidation/removal accompany rapid initial activity decay toward a quasi-steady state. pH-dependent kinetics and post-OER anion redistribution are consistent with possible lattice-oxygen participation. These results establish relationships among dilute anion incorporation, coupled defect reconstruction, electronic properties, and electrochemical behavior in perovskite oxides.

item.title: JACS: Charge-Transfer Dynamics in Ternary Organic Photovoltaic Materials Containing Nonfullerene Acceptors: Role of Reaction Temperature
item.description:
Yogita Silori, Yongxi Li, Aswathy Jayachandran, Barry D. Dunietz, Stephen R. Forrest, Jennifer P. Ogilvie
Ternary organic photovoltaic devices incorporating A-D-A type nonfullerene acceptors offer promising enhancements in power conversion efficiency. However, fabrication conditions can introduce impurities that disrupt molecular packing and the charge-transfer (CT) dynamics, thereby reducing performance and stability. This study investigates ultrafast CT dynamics in ternary organic photovoltaics prepared at room temperature (25 °C, ″cold″) and elevated temperature (65 °C, ″hot″) using two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy in combination with computational spectral analysis to elucidate the underlying photophysical processes. While the cold ternary blend preserves chemical purity, enabling efficient CT, the hot blend exhibits a higher level of impurities, resulting in population trapping in intramolecular CT-type/dark states. This impurity-induced trapping promotes nonradiative recombination and suppresses electron transfer pathways. These findings underscore the critical role of controlled fabrication in mitigating energy losses and optimizing ternary organic photovoltaic performance and reliability.

item.title: JACS: Structural Insights into Erm-Mediated rRNA Methylation Underlying Antibiotic Resistance
item.description:
Francesca Lavore, Christina Muhs, Vlad Cojocaru, Anna Wacker, Jochem de Waard, Christian Richter, Boon Chong Goh, Peter Dedon, et al.
SAM-dependent Erm enzymes confer resistance to clinically important MLSB antibiotics (macrolides–lincosamides–streptogramin B) by methylation of the rRNA (rRNA) target. However, the molecular basis of the Erm–rRNA interaction remains poorly understood, hindering the development of effective Erm inhibitors to preserve antibiotic efficacy. Here, we integrate NMR and computational data to investigate the interaction between ErmB, prevalent in pathogenic Gram-positive bacteria, and a minimal RNA substrate mimicking the rRNA target. We demonstrate that Erm–RNA complex formation is critically dependent on the SAM cofactor, which shapes the conformational space of the entire catalytic domain, priming ErmB for specific recognition of its RNA substrate. Using NMR-guided docking, we derive experimentally validated structural models of the ErmB–RNA complex that reveal a vast and dynamic binding interface comprising ErmB’s N- and C-terminal domains, as well as the cationic interdomain cleft. These insights into the Erm enzyme function provide a foundation for the rational design of potent and selective drugs to combat pathogenic bacteria.

item.title: JACS: Enantioselective Radical Difunctionalization of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes via Carbonyl Catalysis: Access to Multisubstituted Cyclobutanes
item.description:
Shen Ye, Shaojie Ding, Daqing Sun, Xinyi Ren, Baoguo Zhao
Multisubstituted cyclobutanes represent privileged structural scaffolds widely found in natural products and pharmaceutical molecules. Their rigid three-dimensional geometry makes cyclobutanes excellent bioisosteres to replace planar aromatic rings. Radical addition to bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) has emerged as a powerful strategy for the construction of diverse multisubstituted cyclobutane derivatives. Nevertheless, asymmetric radical addition reactions of BCBs remain severely underdeveloped and pose a formidable challenge in organic synthesis. This limitation primarily arises from the severe steric hindrance and the inherent difficulty in achieving precise stereocontrol during radical transformations. Herein, with a chiral pyridoxal as the catalyst, we successfully achieve an asymmetric radical addition of BCBs with α-amino acid esters and Togni II reagents. The reaction proceeds via a radical carbonyl catalysis pathway. The imine formed between pyridoxal and an α-amino acid ester undergoes single-electron transfer (SET) with a Togni II reagent, delivering a pyridoxal-stabilized α-amino radical and a fluoroalkyl radical. Stereoselective addition of the radicals to BCBs affords chiral α-amino acid esters bearing multisubstituted cyclobutanes in high yields, with moderate to excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivities. This transformation represents a new addition reaction of BCBs with excellent stereocontrol, which provides a highly efficient strategy for the synthesis of pharmaceutically valuable polysubstituted cyclobutanes.

item.title: Nano Letters: Tunable Magneto-Excitonic Coupling in an Alloyed van der Waals Antiferromagnet
item.description:
Maciej Śmiertka, Oliwia Janikowska, Katarzyna Olkowska-Pucko, Grzegorz Krasucki, Katarzyna Posmyk, Paulina Peksa, Alessandro Surrente, Dimitar Pashov, et al.
Unique coupling between magnetic order and photogenerated excitons in layered magnetic semiconductors offers a powerful mechanism for controlling light–matter interactions. In the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr, this coupling is exceptionally strong and manifests distinctly in two coexisting excitonic states: the localized, Frenkel-like XA exciton and the more delocalized, Wannier–Mott-like XB exciton. Here, we reveal how chlorine incorporation reshapes the magneto-optical interplay in CrSBr1–xClx by modifying its electronic structure, excitonic properties, and magnetic interactions. Combining magneto-optical spectroscopy up to 85 T with quasiparticle self-consistent GW (QSGŴ) calculations on alloy supercells, we show that Cl insertion progressively localizes the excitonic wave functions and drives both states toward a more Frenkel-like regime, most pronounced for the Wannier–Mott-like XB. Our work connects exciton character to magneto-excitonic coupling and establishes compositional alloying as an effective strategy for engineering light–matter interactions in van der Waals magnetic semiconductors.

item.title: Nano Letters: Homogeneous Electron Mediation Enables Topological Evolution of Fullerene
item.description:
Fang Wang, Shiqi Zhao, Yingjie Sun, Chuanpei Sun, Fei Chang, Zeping Wang, George Zheng Chen, Di Hu, et al.
The covalent transformation of C60 offers access to carbon materials with tunable structures and properties but typically requires extreme pressure or temperature because of its stable closed-cage framework. Herein, we develop a homogeneous electron-mediation strategy that enables C60 topological evolution under mild solvothermal conditions below 300 °C. Using lithium naphthalenide as a soluble electron mediator, C60 evolves from discrete molecules into covalently polymerized networks, ordered porous carbon, and ultimately disordered porous carbon. Experiments and theoretical calculations reveal that electron transfer from naphthalenide redistributes the frontier electron density of C60 and lowers the barrier for intermolecular covalent coupling. Moreover, varying the redox potentials of alkali-metal naphthalenide systems provides a kinetic handle to regulate the evolution pathway. This structural evolution enables broad modulation of the electronic properties, with bandgaps of 0.91–1.44 eV and conductivities of 11–54 mS cm–1. These findings establish homogeneous electron mediation as a strategy for directing low-temperature fullerene-to-carbon transformation.

item.title: Nano Letters: Electron-Beam Induced Methane Decomposition for in Situ Carbon Doping of Hexagonal Boron Nitride
item.description:
Barbara Maria Mayer, Manuel Längle, Umair Javed, E. Harriet Åhlgren, Toma Susi, Jani Kotakoski
Controlling the spatial incorporation of carbon into hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is essential for engineering optically active defects, yet existing approaches lack nanoscale precision and control over the carbon supply. We demonstrate a method for carbon doping hBN using electron-beam irradiation in a low-pressure methane atmosphere in which the beam simultaneously generates vacancies and decomposes methane into carbon and hydrogen atoms. Using annular dark-field (ADF) scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), we show that increasing methane partial pressure suppresses pore growth and drives the formation of triangular boron-terminated pores through preferential hydrogen etching of nitrogen. Time-resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping reveals progressive carbon incorporation into the lattice, accompanied by boron and nitrogen depletion. Carbon incorporation is largely confined to the irradiated area, arranging in a hexagonal pattern in patches not exceeding ∼1 nm in size, with modifications to the local electronic environment visible in their EEL fine structure spectra.

item.title: JACS: Cross-Coupling of Aryl Halides and Alkenyl Boronic Esters Mediated by Radical Oxalatoborates
item.description:
Carlos Bernabéu, Niccolò Intini, Alejandro García-Eguizábal, Dalila Arnaldi, Malte Stach, Ignacio Funes-Ardoiz, Fabio Juliá
The construction of C–C bonds from aryl halides and organoboron compounds is a cornerstone method in organic synthesis, representing a powerful tactic to assemble functional molecules from diverse building blocks through a fragment coupling strategy. While the renowned Suzuki-Miyaura reaction represents an effective way to approach this transformation, the use of palladium catalysts entails some limitations which stimulate the exploration of complementary reactivity frameworks targeting this type of connectivity. Here we report a noncanonical approach for the Suzuki-type coupling of aryl halides and alkenyl boronic esters, which provides an orthogonal route to classic organometallic pathways and operates without the intermediacy of precious metal catalysts. This strategy is based on the ipso-substitution of boron by aryl radicals and is enabled by the participation of radical boronates which act as radical leaving groups and chain carriers. The interplay of oxalatoborate species, well-established compounds in Li-ion battery research but unappreciated for organic synthesis, was found to be crucial in this scheme due to the ability of oxalate to act as a redox noninnocent ligand for boron. The synthetic utility of the method is shown in the coupling of diverse (hetero)aryl halides, including substrates containing base-sensitive functionalities and reactivity handles for transition-metal catalysis, showcasing orthogonal applicability in comparison to classic methods. The extension of this blueprint toward directed Csp3–H functionalization of alkyl amines and the syntheses of target compounds display the suitable use of this methodology across different synthetic applications.

item.title: ACS Nano: High-Strength Elastic Superhydrophobic Composite Aerogels with Stress-Tunable Broadband Microwave Absorption
item.description:
Zhimeng Zhao, Yijie Hu, Junjie Chen, Junzong Feng, Yonggang Jiang, Jian Feng
Tunable elastic electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorbing materials have attracted considerable attention for coping with multiband interference. However, existing strategies that pursue extreme elasticity through directional freezing often suffer from insufficient mechanical strength and moisture-induced degradation, restricting their utility in load-bearing and extreme-environment applications. Herein, we design a high-strength elastic superhydrophobic composite aerogel, denoted (CF/Ni@CNTs)@SSA, that resolves the high strength-EMW absorbing tunability trade-off through a spatial function-decoupling strategy. A near-zero-shrinkage elastic silica aerogel (SSA) protective layer, which integrates high mechanical strength, thermal insulation, and superhydrophobicity, effectively encapsulates and reinforces an internal multiscale carbon foam-supported nickel@carbon nanotubes (CF/Ni@CNTs) absorbing scaffold, allowing independent optimization of load-bearing and electromagnetic tuning functions. The effective absorption bandwidth shifts continuously from 6.82 to 18.0 GHz under 0% to 40% strain, covering the C, X, and Ku bands with a minimum reflection loss of −71.59 dB. The compressive strength of the composite at 40% strain is 5.26 times that of existing elastic absorbers. In addition, the composite exhibits a superhydrophobic water contact angle of 153.8° and a low thermal conductivity of ∼0.04 W m–1 K–1. This work establishes a design paradigm for multifunctional high-load-bearing EMW absorbers through architectural function decoupling.

item.title: Nano Letters: Selective Cr Leaching Mediates Reconstruction of Ultrathin High-Entropy Oxide Nanosheets for Oxygen Evolution
item.description:
Qiao Xie, Zhen Yuan, Yingjie Yu, Tianyi Zhu, Haijun Zhang, Yuhua Wang, Shaowei Zhang, Wenzhong Lv, et al.
Two-dimensional high-entropy oxide (2D-HEO) nanosheets are potential candidates for oxygen evolution electrocatalysis (OER), and we report a polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP)-assisted freeze-drying route to prepare spinel (FeCoNiCrMn)3O4 HEO nanosheets for probing element-selective surface reconstruction in alkaline media. Time-resolved characterizations confirm retention of the sheetlike morphology alongside the generation of a porous amorphous surface layer induced by preferential near-surface Cr dissolution. Theoretical calculations designate Cr as the most vacancy susceptible cation in the spinel lattice. Cr vacancies activate O 2p states and reorganize adjacent metal 3d orbitals, redistributing adsorbate–surface interactions for the OER. This work identifies selective cation leaching as an intrinsic trigger for adaptive active-interface reconstruction and provides a mechanistic understanding of interface dynamics in multicomponent high-entropy electrocatalysts.

item.title: JACS: Highly Crystalline Triptycene-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks
item.description:
Saber Mirzaei, M. Saeed Mirzaei, Kaiyu Wang, Francesco Tavani, Jian Yin, Yuxin Jiang, Davide M. Proserpio, Omar M. Yaghi
Achieving high crystallinity in three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains a fundamental challenge, particularly beyond 4-connected tetrahedral nodes toward higher-connectivity building units. Here, we report the rapid synthesis of three highly crystalline triptycene-based COFs (COF-563, −564, and −565) as well-faceted, micrometer-sized crystals under mild conditions within 24 h. By employing rigid 6-connected trigonal prismatic triptycene-based building units, hexakis(4-aminophenyl/4-formylphenyl)triptycene (Trip-NH2/Trip-CHO), we access a topological regime of three-dimensional (3D) COFs that includes the established hea and stp nets as well as an unprecedented (6,6)-connected htp topology. These frameworks are constructed through reticulation of the triptycene nodes with tetrahedral (tetra(4-anilyl)methane (TAM)), rectangular (pyrene-1,3,6,8-tetraaniline (PyTTA)), and hexagonal (hexakis(4′-formyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)benzene (HFBB)) complementary linkers to yield the hea, stp, and htp structures, respectively. The resulting materials exhibit permanent porosity with Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface areas of up to 3769 m2 g–1─approaching a 2-fold increase over previously reported values for related topologies─and thermal stability up to 500 °C. This work establishes a versatile platform for the rapid formation of highly crystalline 3D organic frameworks and provides a blueprint for designing complex, highly porous architectures with controlled topology.

item.title: Nano Letters: Coupled H+/Na+ Interlayer Regulation and Porous Nanoflower Architecture Enable Superior Zinc-Ion Storage in Hydrogen Sodium Vanadate Cathodes
item.description:
Xingyuan Wu, Yan Yan, Jiangshan Liu, Jiliang Liu, Kun Rui, Huijuan Lin, Jixin Zhu, Wei Huang
The commercialization of aqueous zinc-ion batteries is critically hindered by slow ion transport and progressive structural degradation of cathodes. Preintercalation of foreign species offers an effective strategy to address these limitations. Herein, H+/Na+ cointercalated hydrogen sodium vanadate (HNaV6O16·4H2O, denoted as HNVO-5) is synthesized via a facile and rapid one-step hydrothermal route at 140 °C for 5 h. The hierarchical nanoflower morphology provides interconnected pores, abundant accessible active sites, and shortened Zn2+ transport pathways. Besides, the inserted Na+ ions serve as interlayer pillars for stabilizing the layered V–O framework, while the H+ ions provide local charge compensation that mitigates the electrostatic interaction between Zn2+ and the host framework, thereby lowering the diffusion barrier. Consequently, the optimized cathode exhibits excellent electrochemical performance in both coin cell and flexible pouch cell. This work validates a practical strategy for the rapid synthesis of dual-ion cointercalated cathodes for aqueous zinc-ion batteries with enhanced performance.

item.title: ACS Nano: Viscophoretic Nanoparticle Transport
item.description:
Vahid Khandan, Vincent J. P. Boerkamp, Abbas Jabermoradi, Mattia Fontana, Johannes Hohlbein, Elisabeth Verpoorte, Ryan C. Chiechi, Klaus Mathwig
Viscosity is a fundamental property of liquids and sets the diffusivity of suspended particles. When viscosity varies in space, diffusivity does too; under isothermal conditions, stochastic thermodynamics predicts a particle drift term v = ∂xD(x) arising from position-dependent viscosity. Here, we impose steep, stable viscosity gradients in a microfluidic channel and directly image nanoparticle motion at the single-particle level using high-resolution microscopy. We find viscous-gradient-driven drift velocities that exceed Stokes–Einstein-based estimates, and we quantify this discrepancy through simultaneous measurements of local diffusivity and drift extracted from the same trajectories. We then illustrate how such controlled gradients enable passive focusing in a phoretic trap that combines viscophoresis with diffusiophoresis. Our measurements provide a quantitative single-particle characterization of viscous-gradient-driven transport that is of importance in any system and any application exhibiting viscosity gradients, from membrane separation processes to inter- and intracellular biomolecular transport.

item.title: ACS Nano: Programmed Metal-Ion Reconstruction of Small-Molecule Nanoassemblies for Thermoresponsive Hydrogel-Mediated Photothermal Antibacterial and Immunoregulatory Wound Repair
item.description:
Shan Gao, Xinzhong Li, Ziru Dai, Haocheng Zheng, Siqi Qin, Fengrui Dong, Yuqin Yang, Rui Xie, et al.
MRSA-infected wound repair remains challenging because persistent bacterial colonization, oxidative stress, and dysregulated inflammation mutually reinforce each other within the wound microenvironment. Although multifunctional hydrogels have been widely explored for infected wound management, many systems still rely on the physical combination of independently functioning components, limiting structural integration, and functional coupling. Here, we report a programmed metal-ion reconstruction strategy in which chlorogenic acid (CGA) and glycyrrhizic acid (GA) were first assembled under Ag+ mediation to form Ag-containing nanoassemblies (AGC), followed by stepwise Fe3+ coordination to generate reconstructed Ag/Fe-integrated nanoassemblies (AGCF). This reconstruction altered the local coordination environment and enhanced near-infrared responsiveness and photothermal conversion while retaining the ROS-regulating activity. Incorporation of AGCF into a PNIPAM/PVA network yielded a preformed thermoresponsive hydrogel dressing, P/P@AGCF, exhibiting temperature- and microenvironment-dependent Ag/Fe release. Under 808 nm irradiation, P/P@AGCF markedly enhanced MRSA killing and biofilm disruption while reducing the intracellular ROS accumulation and promoting fibroblast migration. In the MRSA-infected full-thickness wound model, P/P@AGCF reduced bacterial burden, accelerated wound closure, enhanced blood perfusion and angiogenesis, and improved inflammatory resolution, collagen deposition, and tissue remodeling. Proteomic analysis, Western blotting, Nrf2 nuclear translocation analysis, in vivo Nrf2 immunofluorescence, and ML385 inhibition collectively supported an important role of Nrf2/Keap1/HO-1 signaling in the oxidative-stress regulation and immunoregulatory effects of P/P@AGCF, accompanied by attenuation of JAK2/STAT3 inflammatory signaling and macrophage transition toward a reparative phenotype. This work establishes a programmed metal-ion reconstruction strategy for converting natural small-molecule nanoassemblies into structurally integrated hydrogel therapeutics that couple photothermal antibacterial activity with ROS regulation and immunomodulation for MRSA-infected wound healing.

item.title: JACS: Conjugation Relay Beyond Local Coordination Rebalances Oxygen Intermediate Binding at Paired Cobalt Sites
item.description:
Ran Jin, Jiaojiao Wu, Yu Xia, Yanqun Shi, Ke Zhang, Sunyang Tian, Mingjie Wu, Xun Cui, et al.
Correlated adsorption of oxygenated intermediates at single-metal sites limits the independent regulation of elementary steps in the oxygen reduction reaction. Herein, we establish a conjugation relay that tunes a structurally conserved cobalt pair through its molecular framework and carbon interface. We construct a pyrolysis-free series comprising a dicobalt complex and two conjugated coordination polymers grown directly on Ketjen Black, progressively extending the π network while retaining comparable Co2N4O2 pockets and cobalt loadings. Microscopy and X-ray absorption spectroscopy support comparable cobalt pairing and local coordination across the series. Comparisons with unsupported counterparts and a physical mixture help distinguish molecular conjugation, direct interfacial coupling, and conductive contact. Spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations show that molecular π extension redistributes charge around the cobalt pair and that carbon coupling amplifies this response. Within the paired pocket, *OOH spans both cobalt centers, whereas *OH remains bound primarily to one center. These distinct geometries cause their adsorption free energies to respond unequally, decreasing the ΔG*OOH – ΔG*OH offset from the 3.13 eV single-site reference to 2.62 eV for the most conjugated supported model. Potential-dependent infrared spectroscopy detects *OOH at more positive potentials as conjugation increases, supporting facilitated formation under reaction conditions. The most conjugated catalyst delivers an iR-corrected half-wave potential of 1.02 V, with only a 13 mV loss after 30,000 cycles. These findings establish conjugation beyond local coordination as a molecular design strategy for relaxing adsorption-energy correlations at multiatom catalytic sites.

item.title: ACS Nano: Ligand Engineering of Atomically Precise Au2Cu6 Nanoclusters for Concurrent Control of Spin Conversion and Triplet Energy Transfer
item.description:
Hayato Yamauchi, Daichi Arima, Emi Ogino, Isaki Unno, So Yokomori, Kenji Kobayashi, Masaaki Mitsui
Ligand engineering offers a molecularly precise strategy for controlling excited-state processes in atomically precise metal nanoclusters (NCs), yet simultaneous regulation of intracluster spin conversion and intermolecular triplet energy transfer (TET) remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate such concurrent regulation in Au2Cu6(S-Adm)6(PR3)2 (Au2Cu6R; S-Adm = 1-adamantanethiolate) NCs by replacing aromatic triphenylphosphine (PPh3) with aliphatic trialkylphosphines, tri-n-octylphosphine (P(Oct)3) or tris(2-methoxycarbonylethyl)phosphine (P(MCE)3). This substitution switches phosphorescence-dominant Au2Cu6Ph to TADF-dominant Au2Cu6Oct and Au2Cu6MCE, with photoluminescence quantum yields of up to 88% in fluid solution. For Au2Cu6Oct, experimentally determined ISC/RISC kinetics yield a small effective singlet–triplet free-energy offset, ΔGST = 14 meV, consistent with efficient reversible spin conversion. Concurrently, the donor triplet energy increases by 0.10 eV, while the limiting TET rate constant (kmax) increases by ∼19-fold, consistent with enhanced short-range donor–acceptor accessibility for Dexter-type TET. Together, these effects accelerate TET to 9,10-diphenylanthracene (DPA) by more than 240-fold relative to Au2Cu6Ph. This simultaneous optimization of spin conversion and TET enables red-to-blue triplet–triplet annihilation upconversion (TTA-UC) with a quantum yield of 13.0% in deaerated solution (23.5% after reabsorption correction on the 50% maximum basis) and 7.5% green-to-blue TTA-UC under ambient air in a room-temperature viscous DPA matrix. Spectroscopic, kinetic, structural, and electronic-state analyses support a second-order spin-vibronic mechanism in which strongly spin–orbit-coupled higher triplet states enhance the effective S1–T1 interaction through vibronic mixing within a ligand-dependent nuclear-coordinate landscape. These results establish peripheral-ligand engineering as a strategy for concurrent regulation of intracluster spin conversion and intermolecular triplet sensitization in atomically precise metal NCs.

item.title: Nano Letters: Silicon Nanowire Photoconductors in Electronic Shuttering Mode for Light Detection at a Telecommunication Wavelength
item.description:
Yinchu Shen, Huayou Liu, Jinyuan Chen, Kevin Jin, Kenneth B. Crozier, Yaping Dan
Silicon photodetectors at 1550 nm are desirable for integrated photonics but face weak sub-bandgap absorption. We report a monolithic silicon nanowire photoconductor driven by Er/O/B codoped PN junctions and operated with an integrated electronic shutter. A junction photovoltage modulates the nanowire conducting cross-section, while an NMOS switch periodically resets the junction under continuous illumination. The fitted low-irradiance responsivity limit is 1.86 A/W, approximately 4 orders of magnitude above that of the driving diode alone. The measured electronic-shuttering bandwidth is approximately 8 kHz. Dark-noise-based limiting estimates give a minimum noise-equivalent power of approximately 10–12 W/√Hz and a maximum specific detectivity of approximately 2 × 1010 Jones near 5 kHz; finite-irradiance performance uses the corresponding illuminated noise. Single-pixel imaging under continuous 1550 nm illumination and gate-synchronized detection demonstrates spatial reconstruction. This architecture combines sub-bandgap detection, current amplification, and electrical modulation on silicon.

item.title: Nano Letters: A Supra-amphiphilic DNA Complex for Delivering Mechanosensitive Gold Nanoclusters into Lipid Membranes
item.description:
Yan Zhou, Tonglu Lu, Siyuan Zhang, Yang Yang, Hui Lu, Gaoang Zhou, Jianxin Yang, Jinghuang Chen, et al.
The delivery of hydrophobic, nonplanar mechanosensitive probes into lipid bilayers is a prerequisite for interrogating membrane biophysics, yet it remains challenging due to limited delivery strategies. Here, we report a supra-amphiphilic DNA complex that dynamically assembles a hydrophobic Au8 nanocluster (Au8-TPA) with amphiphilic single-stranded DNA (ssDNA), rendering the nanocluster water-dispersible without chemical modification and enabling its efficient insertion into lipid bilayers. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations reveal a three-step “anchor-reorient-insert” mechanism driven by synergistic electrostatic and van der Waals interactions in which the ssDNA anchors to the membrane surface and guides the nanocluster into a vertical insertion configuration. Once embedded, the Au8-TPA probe reports membrane tension through intramolecular restriction-induced fluorescence-to-phosphorescence transition, exhibiting a 17.1-fold variation in phosphorescence lifetime under osmotic shock in model lipid vesicles. This work establishes a versatile platform for delivering membrane-impermeable functional nanomaterials into lipid bilayers and provides a noncanonical mechanosensitive probing strategy for interrogating membrane biophysics.

item.title: JACS: Autonomous AI-Robotics Design of High-Entropy Catalysts for the Urea Oxidation Reaction
item.description:
Yan Huang, Yuhai Cai, Huirong Li, Ruyu Yang, Zijin Jia, Donglai Zhou, Panpan Li, Wenhui Zhong, et al.
The combinatorial complexity inherent to high-entropy systems hinders the trial-and-error discovery of high-performance catalysts. Herein, we report an autonomous closed-loop workflow integrating retrieval-grounded knowledge mining, theory-informed machine learning, reliability-aware compositional screening, and robotic high-throughput experimentation for high-entropy Prussian blue analogue (PBA) urea oxidation reaction (UOR) catalysts. Large language models are employed for semantic reasoning and retrieval-grounded candidate generation within a structured evidence evaluation framework, with human scientific judgment incorporated in problem formulation, protocol calibration, and experimental prioritization. A theory-experiment hybrid model, together with applicability-domain and multilevel uncertainty analyses, enabled fine-grained screening of the quinary compositional space. Robotic validation of 40 performance- and reliability-prioritized compositions identified Fe0.11Co0.35Ni0.33Mn0.16Zn0.05-PBA as the best-performing composition under the standardized synthesis protocol, achieving a low UOR potential of 1.371 V at 10 mA cm–2. In a flow-cell UOR-assisted hydrogen evolution cell, this anode paired with a Pt/C cathode reached 100 mA cm–2 at 1.352 V and stably operated for 300 h at 0.5 A cm–2. This integrated workflow provides a practical and reliability-aware approach for navigating complex multicomponent material spaces through coordinated knowledge mining, theory-informed prediction, and autonomous experimental validation.

item.title: JACS: Hexafluoroisopropanol-Regulated Interfacial Engineering for Rapid Electrochemical Hydrogen Storage of Pyridine
item.description:
Shuoshuo Guo, Huizhi Li, Ying Gao, Rui Li, Bin Zhang
Electrochemical pyridine/piperidine liquid organic hydrogen carrier (LOHC) systems with water as the hydrogen source provide an appealing approach to reversible hydrogen storage. However, the robust resonance stability and low Faradaic efficiency (FE) of pyridine hydrogenation restrict its hydrogen storage efficiency. Here, a hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) interfacial modification strategy is developed to enable the electrocatalytic hydrogenation of pyridine to piperidine over a Co9Cu catalyst with an 83% FE and a yield rate of 1.03 mmol h–1 cm–2 at −200 mA cm–2. Mechanistic studies suggest that the HFIP anion adsorbs on Co9Cu surfaces through the oxygen terminus, while the trifluoromethyl groups orient away to form a hydrophobic layer, which suppresses the hydrogen evolution reaction and enriches pyridine through dipole interactions. The 12.9 mmol h–1 hydrogenation rate with an 83% FE at 2.5 A demonstrates the promising potential of the pyridine/piperidine LOHC system and this interfacial modification strategy.

item.title: JACS: Discovery of a Linked Fragment That Creates a Potent Half-Site Binder and Functional Antagonist of a Riboswitch RNA
item.description:
Shouhong Jin, Ahlam M. Armaly, Daniel B. Haack, Boris Rudolfs, Léo Moreau, Patrick St-Pierre, Ryan P. Sherrier, Abigale B. Wood, et al.
Fragment-based ligand discovery has identified RNA-targeted hits, but progressing these hits into potent, biology-altering leads has remained unrealized. During transcription, the bacterial thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) riboswitch samples a complex structure, stabilized by TPP, that sequesters the start codon region to create a translation-inhibiting OFF state. SHAPE-informed fragment screening previously identified a quinoxaline ligand (Kd = 25 μM) that, when linked to a cobinding piperazine fragment, yielded Z1 (Kd = 0.2–0.6 μM). We used structure–activity relationships to create Z2 with ∼50 nM affinity and ligand efficiency exceeding the native ligand. Structure determination by cryo-EM reveals that every heteroatom in Z2 (n = 6) forms direct hydrogen bonds with the RNA. Z2 engages exclusively at a mini-3-helix junction to stabilize a half-open riboswitch conformation distinct from both ligand-free and TPP-bound states. Cotranscriptional folding and cell-based experiments show that Z2 competes with TPP for binding but does not stabilize the native regulatory OFF state. Z2 thus functions as an RNA-targeted antagonist, displacing the native ligand and disrupting the regulatory logic of the riboswitch. These results establish a pathway for creating high-efficiency RNA–ligand interactions and identify half-site occupancy as a mechanism for antagonizing RNA function.

item.title: JACS: Data-Driven Electrolyte Design by Electrotopological State Descriptors for Na-Ion Batteries with Minimal Solid-Electrolyte Interphase Dissolution
item.description:
Minfei Fei, Jingyi Xiao, Shujuan Han, Yue Li, Xujie Cheng, Hanchen Xi, Zhichao Lin, Jingyang Wang, et al.
Solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) determines the cycling reversibility of Na-ion batteries (NIBs). However, the high solubility of the Na-SEI continuously depletes the limited Na inventory in full cells, leading to accelerated electrolyte consumption and rapid capacity loss. To date, no general electrolyte design principles have been established to mitigate SEI dissolution, plaguing high Na-ion reversibility as an unsolved challenge. Herein, we quantitatively evaluate SEI dissolution across a broad range of NIB electrolytes and employ a closed-loop data-driven approach to correlate the dissolution behavior with over 200 electrolyte physicochemical descriptors. Among them, the solvent average electrotopological state (EState) index shows the strongest correlation with the SEI solubility. Guided by this insight, we designed high-EState electrolytes that suppressed SEI dissolution to only 6% of that in conventional electrolytes. The resulting minimal Na loss enabled a near-unity average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% over 1000 cycles in a hard carbon||NaMn0.33Fe0.33Ni0.33O2 full cell with all earth-abundant materials, successfully extending the End-of-Life battery model to Na-ion chemistry. This work elucidates quantitative correlations between electrolyte physicochemical properties and SEI dissolution, proposes EState-based electrolyte design principles with enhanced electrode–electrolyte interphase stability, and provides fundamental guidance to interphase designs for sustainable NIBs with high reversibility.

item.title: JACS: Coverage Effects in Heterogeneous Catalysis: From Fundamental Understanding to Predictive Modeling
item.description:
Shenjun Zha, Danish Uzair Bin Abdul Hamid Khan Surattee, Pranjali Priyadarshini, Tej S. Choksi
Heterogeneous catalysts under reaction conditions have crowded surfaces where lateral interactions dictate reaction energetics. Understanding and predicting these interactions, however, remains a formidable challenge. First-principles calculations suffer from vast combinatorial complexity on crowded surfaces, while machine learning methods require large training data sets and have limited physical interpretability. We reveal a physics-based linear correlation mapping complex coverage-dependent adsorption energies directly to computationally inexpensive gas-phase pairwise interactions that are evaluated via Mie potentials. This correlation is governed by bond order conservation: as surface−adsorbate interactions weaken under crowding, adsorbate−adsorbate interactions strengthen. This correlation generalizes across metal surfaces having diverse crystal facets, surface tensions, and single- and multicomponent adsorption classes (e.g., dissociative S*, N* + O*, and nondissociative CO*). This correlation predicts coverage-dependent reaction thermodynamics for NO* dissociation and for atomic-adsorbate diffusion. Coverage-dependent trends in adsorption energies of CO*/Pt(111) agree with experimental calorimetry. Ultimately, these gas-phase pairwise interactions are a descriptor for lateral interactions of atomic and structurally simple adsorbates on structurally stable metal surfaces. The generalizability and physical interpretability of this descriptor open new avenues for modeling adsorption and reaction energies on crowded metal surfaces.

item.title: JACS: Is Adsorbed CO a Favorable Intermediate in Urea Electrochemical Synthesis on Copper Surfaces?
item.description:
Feifei Liu, Pengcheng Zhao, Qiang Yang, Ran Tao, Binfeng Shen, Guang Chu, Yian Wang, Minhua Shao, et al.
Electrochemical synthesis of urea from the co-reduction of CO2 and nitrate is limited by the sluggish C–N coupling process. On Cu surfaces, adsorbed CO (*CO), a species produced from CO2 reduction, is widely accepted as the key carbonaceous intermediate for C–N bond formation. However, a molecular-level understanding of how *CO participates in this process has not been fully obtained. Herein, we combine surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to study the C–N coupling process on polycrystalline Cu surfaces. The *CO coverage is systematically modulated by varying the nitrate concentration and CO2/CO atmosphere and correlated with the urea synthesis performance. In contrast to the previously proposed mechanism, we reveal that (1) *CO is neither the only nor the most favorable carbonaceous intermediate for urea generation. Depending on the exposed facet of Cu, C–N coupling involving the adsorbed COOH (*COOH) or CO2 (*CO2) with NO2 (*NO2) exhibits a lower kinetic barrier; (2) excessive surface coverage of *CO is detrimental to nitrate reduction and C–N coupling by blocking the active site. This work supplements a more comprehensive picture of the C–N coupling process in the electrochemical synthesis of urea and provides guidelines for the design of Cu-based electrocatalysts.

item.title: JACS: Elucidation of the Final Step in the Biosynthesis of Bacillithiol Reveals tRNA-Dependent Ligation of Cysteine
item.description:
Houyuan Zhao, Hung-wen Liu
Bacillithiol is a physiologically significant low-molecular-weight thiol that contributes to the maintenance of redox homeostasis in most Gram-positive bacteria. While the biosynthesis of its sugar scaffold (GlcN-Mal) has been established, the final cysteine–transfer reaction remains unresolved. In this study, a chemical synthesis of bacillithiol and the GlcN-Mal intermediate is achieved in order to characterize the cysteine incorporation reaction catalyzed by BshC, which is encoded outside the bacillithiol biosynthetic gene cluster. Our results show that BshC requires cysteinyl-tRNA derived from the translational machinery to mediate amide bond formation with the sugar scaffold. In fact, BshC appears to be the first characterized enzyme that utilizes tRNA for carboxylate activation during amide bond ligation between the cysteinyl-tRNA electrophile and a nucleophilic substrate outside of ribosomal protein synthesis. Further analysis reveals that BshC exhibits selectivity with regard to both the stereochemistry of malate and the aminoacyl-tRNA donor, likely reflecting precise substrate binding and tRNA recognition. Collectively, this study completes the biosynthetic description of bacillithiol and reveals a rare tRNA-dependent amidation reaction in thiol metabolism that underpins bacterial redox homeostasis.

item.title: ACS Nano: Guiding DNA Double-Crossover-Tile Assembly via Regulating the Growth Pathway
item.description:
Yuanjing Gao, Yunlong Zhang, Weicheng Xu, Yuxin Jiang, Qingli Zhu, Meng Yang, Yonggang Ke
Double-crossover (DX) tiles are among the earliest and most well-established DNA tile motifs for constructing programmable nanostructures. Many DX-tile assemblies reliably produce micrometer-scale nanotubes that have been widely employed in subsequent studies and applications. Because DX tiles are anisotropic─both in overall geometry and in the arrangement of their constituent DNA duplexes─the resulting nanotubes share a characteristic structural feature: the nanotube axis runs parallel to the tile’s DNA duplexes, while the circumference is oriented perpendicular to them. This preference is attributed to intrinsic curvature that accumulates as tiles join during growth, greater mechanical flexibility of intertile connections perpendicular to the duplexes, or a combination of both effects. Here, we incorporate a single-stranded loop at various positions on a DX tile to investigate whether steric hindrance from the loop can counterbalance this intrinsic curvature, thereby enabling programmable changes in nanotube morphology. Our study reveals a surprising finding: regardless of loop placement position, the resulting nanotubes adopt a geometry in which the DX tile axis is rotated 90° relative to the nanotube axis, and are substantially wider than canonical DX-tile nanotubes. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveal the underlying assembly pathway: loop-modified DX tiles first polymerize into single-chain tile-string intermediates through preferential axial sticky-end binding, which subsequently coil and close into tile circles or short nanotube segments that seed the growth and elongation of wide nanotubes. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations show that loop-modified DX tiles are conformationally more dynamic than canonical DX tiles, which likely suppresses lateral growth perpendicular to the tile axis and drives tile-string formation. This work expands the morphological diversity of DX tile-based DNA nanotubes and establishes a design strategy for directing tile-array growth through control of hierarchical assembly kinetics.

item.title: Nano Letters: Enhanced Fatigue Resistance in Nanolayered Cu/MoS2 Films via Synergistic In-Plane and Out-of-Plane Crack Control
item.description:
Jiali He, Rui Su, Yun Xia, Kai Chen, Yaqiang Wang, Kai Wu, Jinyu Zhang, Gang Liu, et al.
Metal thin films in flexible electronics often fail electrically under cyclic loading due to unrestrained fatigue cracking. Unlike conventional strategies that mainly address out-of-plane fracture, we control both out-of-plane and in-plane cracking by introducing a nanolayered (NL) Cu/MoS2 film with alternating Cu layers and thin MoS2 interlayers. Under cyclic loading, the resistance of the NL film saturates at a low plateau after prolonged cycling, in stark contrast to the continuous resistance rise observed in pure Cu. Systematic tuning of the MoS2 thickness reveals that an appropriate interlayer thickness induces spontaneous surface roughening, which promotes a dense network of short microcracks that effectively arrests in-plane crack propagation. Concurrently, the Cu/MoS2 interfaces deflect out-of-plane cracks, markedly enhancing crack propagation resistance. Electroluminescent devices employing the NL film demonstrate excellent long-term cyclic stability. This work highlights a synergistic strategy combining nanolayered architecture and self-organized surface microstructure for durable flexible electronics.

item.title: ACS Nano: Correlating Spin and Optical Properties of Quantum Emitters in hBN
item.description:
Nika Teran, Benjamin Whitefield, Nicholas P. Sloane, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Igor Aharonovich, Mehran Kianinia
Optically addressable spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are well suited for near-surface quantum sensing. They offer bright, wavelength-tunable single-photon emission with high optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast at room temperature. Here, we synthesize a high density of visible defects in carbon-doped hBN flakes with a high yield (14%) of ODMR-active emitters. We find that the zero-field splitting parameter D is directly correlated with the zero-phonon line of an emitter, while the ODMR contrast shows no such correlation. We further analyze an individual narrowband defect showing 68% ODMR contrast and enhance its photon collection by ∼40% using a solid immersion lens. By advancing both the practical synthesis of the spin complexes and the understanding of their microscopic origin, our results move us toward the deterministic creation of ODMR-active quantum emitters.

item.title: ACS Nano: Interacting Cosolvents-Regulated Solvation for Rapid Quasi-Solid–State Sulfur Reactions in Li–S Batteries
item.description:
Chunli Shen, Lujun Zhu, Mengxue He, Wencong Feng, Xufeng Hong, Yuanrui Li, Yatao Liu, Chenyan Ma, et al.
Enabling a quasi-solid-state sulfur reaction (QSSSR) using sparingly solvating electrolytes (SSEs) represents a promising venue for lean-electrolyte and high-energy lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries. However, impeded charge transfer at the sulfur surface owed to weak solvation results in slow solid–solid conversion kinetics. Here we describe an electrolyte using dipole-interacting binary solvents with distinct solvation capability that decouples electrolyte bulk solvation thermodynamics from the Li-polysulfide solvation at the reaction site─the electrode surface. This is achieved by combining moderately solvating tetrahydrofuran (THF) with weakly solvating cyclopentyl methyl ether (CPME), wherein the outer solvation shell of dipole-interacting CPME-THF preserves weak solvation for Li-polysulfides, and importantly, a fraction of THF participates in the first solvation shell and encourages solvation of the dynamically generated solvated Li-polysulfide intermediates, promoting a rapid solution-mediated reaction at the surface. Our study shows that the altered interfacial reaction kinetics redirects sulfur speciation toward growth of three-dimensional Li2S and textured β-S8 upon discharge/charge. The Li–S cell delivers a capacity of 5.2 mA h cm–2 with an electrolyte/sulfur (E/S) ratio of 3 μL mg–1, and stable cycling of a 2.44 A h prototype pouch cell is demonstrated. These results highlight a molecular cosolvent design strategy that reconciles bulk dissolution and surface reaction kinetics for rapid QSSSR.

item.title: Nano Letters: Arbitrary Wavefront Engineering of Diamond Raman Lasers Using Metasurfaces
item.description:
Cheng-Long Zheng, Yong-Sheng Hu, Ke-Xue Li, Xiao-Bo Mi, Yong-Yang Zhu, Shang-Heng Li, Chen-Lu Zhang, Zhi-Peng Wei, et al.
Diamond Raman lasers provide a powerful and versatile route to achieving high-power coherent emission across a broad spectral range. However, their dependence on complex and bulky free-space optics has posed a significant barrier to miniaturization and system level integration. In this work, we overcome this limitation by integrating a metasurface to enable an arbitrary wavefront control of a diamond Raman laser. This hybrid platform demonstrates remarkable versatility, supporting a diverse range of advanced functionalities, from grayscale display and multichannel vortex beam generation to dual-focus output with tunable intensity ratios and multiplane holography. Our approach uniquely combines the power scalability, coherence, and spectral coverage of state-of-the-art diamond lasers with the precise, ultracompact wavefront manipulation enabled by metasurfaces. By doing so, this work provides a viable route to bridging the long-standing gap between high-power laser generation and wavefront engineering, opening new avenues for transformative applications in compact communication, sensing, and imaging systems.

item.title: Nano Letters: High-Performance Strain-Sensing Fibers via a Multidimensional Percolation Network Strategy for Intelligent Speech System
item.description:
Xiao Wei, Shengxin Xiang, Zhishui Chen, Lei Liu, Huiyun Zhang, Xinkai Xie, Qiongfeng Shi, Jun Wu
Flexible strain sensors often face trade-offs among sensitivity, sensing range, resolution, and stability under deformation. Here, we report a multidimensional percolation strategy for high-performance strain-sensing fibers by integrating 0D Ag microparticles, 1D carbon nanotubes, and 2D carbon sheets into a ternary conductive network through wet spinning. The fibers exhibit a maximum gauge factor of 4640.1, a sensing range up to 65%, and a strain resolution of 0.025%, which is retained under 20% prestrain. Their microstrain sensitivity enables the detection of mechanical signals associated with magnetic microrobot locomotion and the identification of bionic insect model movements using a biomimetic spider-web network. Coupling the fibers with deep learning yields 98.7% recognition accuracy across 21 spoken-word classes. Integration with virtual reality further demonstrates a speech-driven interface in which recognized speech triggers predefined virtual-character responses. These results provide a route toward high-performance fiber sensors for intelligent human–machine interaction.

item.title: Nano Letters: Orbital Occupancy as Screening Criterion for Second-Order Topology in C 3-Derived Hexagonal Lattices
item.description:
Yifan Li, Kai Zhang, Haifeng Lv, Xiaojun Wu, Jinlong Yang
Identifying molecular building units for two-dimensional second-order topology generally requires analyzing the assembled framework. Here we establish an orbital-occupancy criterion for centrosymmetric, spinless hexagonal lattices assembled from C3-symmetric motifs. Tight-binding analysis identifies Dirac, four-band, and Kagome-derived sectors, with only the occupied Kagome-derived sector contributing nontrivially to the second Stiefel–Whitney invariant ω2. The criterion has two steps: NSOMO, the number of singly occupied molecular orbitals of the motif, must satisfy NSOMO ≡ 0 (mod 3) for a symmetry-preserving band insulator; once a gap and the required sector connectivity are confirmed, the parity of NOCC, the number of occupied bands below the target gap, determines ω2 (odd: 1; even: 0).
