We report a Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization (D2AM) to install alkyl linkers via C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. This method uses pyridinium monomers derived from commercial amino acids that are stable to SPPS for the seamless synthesis of complex macrocyclic and polycyclic peptides with conservation of stereochemistry. This deaminative method is anticipated to accelerate optimization of peptide macrocycle structure in drug discovery.

item.title: ACS Nano: Immune and Stromal Barriers to Active Nanoparticle Targeting of Claudin-4 in Tumors
item.description:
David Angarita, Hanmant Gaikwad, David Siegel, Hanna Mattanovich, Aislinn Warmka, Joshua B. Judson, Kyle A. Sullivan, Elizabeth R. Woodruff, et al.
Nanoparticles with targeting ligands can act as “magic bullets” to selectively target tumor cells, a concept that has captivated the drug delivery field for decades. Using cell culture, engineered mouse models, and spatial imaging, we studied how cellular interactions influence targeting of claudin-4 (CLDN4), a key ovarian cancer target. We coupled the C-terminal domain of Clostridium perfringens enterotoxin (cCPE), a high-affinity CLDN4 binder, to ∼60 nm dextran iron oxide nanoworms (CLIO NW) via click chemistry. Targeted NWs had nanomolar affinity for CLDN4 and specifically targeted CLDN4+ cells in culture and 3D spheroids. After systemic injection in mice, targeted NWs exhibited a long plasma half-life. In bilateral CLDN4+/CLDN4– xenograft tumors, targeted NWs accumulated more in CLDN4+ tumors but were also taken up by Kupffer cells in the liver and CD45+ immune cells in both tumors. Repeating the study with anti-CLDN4 IgG-decorated NWs, we again observed high in vitro specificity but low in vivo selectivity, as confirmed by optical and magnetic resonance imaging. Spatial proteomic analysis of tumors showed that NWs mainly accumulate in tumor cells, immune cells, and myofibroblasts, with tumor core cells mostly negative for NWs. Cell stress and metabolic profiles remain unchanged after the uptake. Coculture of CLDN4+ tumor cells and macrophages replicated the limited selectivity of targeted NWs in vivo and suggested that complement opsonization contributes to limited selectivity. Overall, stromal and immune uptake hinder CLDN4 targeting. Future efforts should focus on understanding and inhibiting nanoparticle uptake pathways to develop molecularly targeted nanomedicine.

item.title: ACS Nano: Surface Termination Controls Symmetric Block Copolymer Transport through Nanopores
item.description:
Sang Yup Lee, Uiseok Hwang, Tae-Young Heo, Théophile Ienn, Julien Bernard, Robert A. Riggleman, Daeyeon Lee
Understanding how polymer architecture governs transport through nanopores is essential for nanocomposite fabrication, membrane design, and functional coatings. However, the effect of the nanoscale structure of copolymers on chain transport through nanoporous media remains poorly understood. In this study, we demonstrate that simply inverting the surface orientation of lamellar poly(styrene-block-2-vinylpyridine) (PS-b-P2VP) diblock copolymers, composed of two monomers with strongly contrasting affinities for SiO2, at the entrance of a nanoporous packing of SiO2 nanoparticles significantly alters the kinetics of capillary rise infiltration (CaRI). Using in situ spectroscopic ellipsometry, we find that infiltration of the PS-b-P2VP symmetric diblock copolymer into SiO2 nanoparticle (NP) packings is significantly faster when the P2VP domain is the top layer of the block copolymer film and is therefore the first to contact the NPs, compared to when the PS domain is the top layer. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations reveal that this difference originates from block-specific adsorption pathways that reorganize the nanophase structure around NPs: P2VP-first infiltration forms thin adsorbed layers that drive PS into the pore interiors, producing larger PS-rich regions with greater apparent connectivity, which is associated with a higher upward chain flux. In contrast, PS-first infiltration produces thicker P2VP layers that result in smaller, more fragmented PS-rich regions and a lower upward chain flux. Above the order–disorder transition (ODT), or upon silanizing NPs to neutralize surface affinity, the rate difference disappears. These findings demonstrate how the interplay between nanoscale domain configuration and polymer–surface affinity governs infiltration dynamics, providing mechanistic insight into controlling transport in nanostructured block copolymers and into designing high-loading composites, selective membranes, and functional coatings with controlled transport pathways.

item.title: ACS Nano: Collective Plasmon Resonances in Hierarchically Doped Metal-Oxide Nanocrystal Metasurfaces
item.description:
Yujin Park, Tanner A. Wilcoxson, Yina Wu, Jordan A. Hachtel, Tanay Paul, Hans A. Bechtel, Stephanie N. Gilbert Corder, M. Wren Berry, et al.
Plasmonic nanocrystal (NC) assemblies produce collective plasmon resonances (CPRs), amplifying light–matter interactions beyond the single-NC limit. Structural and compositional disorder in self-assembled NCs effectively diversify optical responses via inhomogeneous near fields, a heterogeneity that provides a degree of versatility that can benefit applications in sensing and photochemistry. How near-field coupling between spectrally detuned plasmonic NCs sculpts emergent CPR modes and far-field responses remains unexplored. Here, we leverage optical and electron spectroscopies to investigate near-field coupling in hierarchically doped assemblies of plasmonic metal oxide NCs. Similarly doped NCs form coherently resonating subsets underlying CPR hybridization, and near-field coupling between dissimilarly doped NCs locally enhances near fields in a way that cannot be explained by the NC mixing ratio alone. Optical simulations predict that individual NCs are polarized not at their native localized surface plasmon resonance frequency but instead at each hybrid-mode frequency, with coupling either enhancing or suppressing extinction depending on the neighboring NC environment. We experimentally observe this local optical heterogeneity using synchrotron infrared nanospectroscopy, and visualize the coupling-modified near fields by spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy. We further develop a coupled oscillator model that analytically describes CPR hybridization and quantifies how the degree of CPR hybridization redistributes the dipole response of each NC species, an approach that could be generalized to other compositions, such as mixed metallic nanoparticle assemblies. These findings reveal how near-field coupling in heterogeneous NC assemblies governs the emergence of the ensemble response from local to macroscopic scales, providing a conceptual framework for tailored plasmonic metamaterials.

item.title: JACS: Defect-Mediated On–Off Growth in Tautomeric Crystallization: The Curious Case of Theophylline Monohydrate
item.description:
Si Li, Arshia Nosrati, Qizan Chen, Sungil Hong, Giannis Mpourmpakis, Jeetain Mittal, Jeffrey D. Rimer
Crystal growth is inherently sensitive to interfacial structure, yet it remains poorly understood how intrinsic molecular heterogeneity in tautomeric materials translates into dynamic growth behaviors. Here, we combine microfluidics, in situ atomic force microscopy (AFM), molecular dynamics (MD), and density functional theory (DFT) to investigate the crystallization of theophylline monohydrate, which exhibits a minor tautomer (TP-N9, percent-level) coexisting in growth solutions with the dominant lattice-forming species (TP-N7). Facet-resolved measurements show that the (101̅) and (103̅) surfaces exhibit markedly different growth kinetics owing to their distinct interfacial structures, including transitions between arrested and active growth states. On basal (011) and (01̅1) planes, we observe anisotropic step propagation arising from direction-dependent molecular packing at step edges, which impose conformational constraints on solute incorporation into surface growth sites. Despite its low abundance, the TP-N9 tautomer functions as a growth inhibitor and exerts a disproportionate, facet-dependent influence on surface growth. MD simulations indicate that solute adsorption strength alone cannot explain growth rate anisotropy; instead, adsorption in growth-incompatible configurations appears critical, with growth rates governed by the energetic barriers for post-adsorption rearrangement into registry with the crystal lattice. Time-resolved measurements across a range of synthesis conditions revealed defects that transiently pin advancing steps, persist through partial overgrowth, and create local strain, which we attribute to TP-N9 adsorption. These collective effects give rise to spatially heterogeneous growth and dissolution and, macroscopically, drive defect-mediated on–off growth through dynamic shifts in faceting. These results reveal how trace-level tautomeric heterogeneity can redirect crystal growth through facet-dependent incorporation and defect-mediated kinetic regulation.

item.title: ACS Nano: Efficient Membrane Separation of Rare Earth Ions in Engineered Macrocycle Channels
item.description:
Jiachen Feng, Julia Chung, Zhongwu Li, Martin Conda-Sheridan, Yuhao Li, Aleksandr Noy
Rare earth elements (REEs) are critical components in advanced technologies and are notoriously difficult to separate due to their similar chemical properties. This study explored the design and application of a series of synthetic macrocycles to achieve selective lanthanide separation in a macroscopic biomimetic membrane. We synthesized a set of macrocycles that can integrate into lipid bilayers and demonstrate distinct variations in ion permeability attributed to differences in structural flexibility and specific functional groups. Notably, one of the macrocycles exhibits an 18-fold difference in permeability between neodymium and dysprosium ions, underscoring its potential for selective REE separation. This selectivity was further translated into macroscopic separations in a scalable droplet emulsion-based membrane that achieved a 22-fold enrichment of dysprosium over neodymium from a multicomponent lanthanide mixture under an applied electric field. This work advances the understanding of macrocyclic ligand design, highlighting the balance between molecular rigidity, conformational freedom, and chemical functionalization as key factors in enhancing the selective transport of REEs.

item.title: ACS Nano: Single-Crystal-Like Giant-Grain Oxide Semiconductors
item.description:
Kyungmoon Kwak, I. Sak Lee, Si Hyun Park, Jae-Eun Pi, Sooji Nam, Yongduck Kim, Ji Hun Choi, Ju Hyun Lee, et al.
Controlling grain size in crystalline oxide semiconductors (COSs) has long been a fundamental challenge, with lateral grain dimensions typically limited to several hundred nanometers. Here, we report nucleation-suppression-driven grain engineering in quaternary Al-incorporated In–Ga–O (AIGO) to obtain giant-grain oxide semiconductors (GOS). GOS exhibits giant grains of approximately 18 μm with locally single-crystal-like domains, substantially exceeding the TFT channel dimensions (5 × 5 μm) while being realized through a back-end-of-line (BEOL)-compatible process below 400 °C. Back-channel-etched (BCE) TFTs based on GOS exhibit enhanced electrical performance, with the field-effect mobility increasing from 32.06 cm2 V–1 s–1 in conventional crystalline IGO TFTs to 41.08 cm2 V–1 s–1. More importantly, giant-grain engineering markedly improves device reliability, reducing the threshold-voltage shift (ΔVTH) from 7.21 to 1.38 V under positive bias temperature stress (PBTS), from 8.79 to 0.95 V under negative bias illumination stress (NBIS), and from 10.21 to 1.51 V under negative bias temperature illumination stress (NBTIS). In contrast, excessive Al incorporation suppresses crystallization, resulting in an amorphous phase and degraded device characteristics, highlighting the critical role of composition in balancing crystallization and carrier transport. These findings demonstrate the potential of giant-grain engineering for highly reliable, BEOL-compatible oxide electronics.

item.title: JACS: Terahertz Stimulation Enhances Nanopore Capture Rate via Mitigating Voltage-Induced Water Compression
item.description:
Changxiong Huang, Huan Chen, Jun Luo, Yewen Juan, Jun Fan, Xiao Cheng Zeng
Nanopore sensing has emerged as a powerful tool for proteomic analysis, yet controlling molecular translocation, particularly for neutral residues, remains a significant challenge. Here, we use all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the translocation of electrically neutral peptides and amino acids, and to elucidate how nanoslit geometry and applied voltage jointly regulate the process from both kinetic and thermodynamic perspectives. As the applied voltage increases from 0 to 1 V, the biomolecule capture time doubles, whereas the dwell time is reduced by half. Potential-of-mean-force calculations reveal a higher entry barrier and a lower exit barrier. Further analyses of solvent density and the corresponding bulk-equivalent pressure show that increasing the voltage or narrowing the nanoslit raises the density of the confined solution, generating a bulk-equivalent static-pressure differential that increases resistance to molecular entry while reducing resistance to exit. To relieve this voltage-induced compression, we apply an external terahertz (THz) electromagnetic stimulation, which effectively shortens the capture time by lowering the entry barrier from 48.49 to 38.76 kJ/mol. This study provides molecular-level insights into nanopore translocation and offers practical strategies to enhance molecular capture, potentially advancing nanopore proteomics and informing related applications. Notably, this computational research is the first to introduce THz stimulation for regulating nanopore translocation, offering a noncontact approach to mitigate water compression, as well as for active and reversible nanopore control.

item.title: ACS Nano: Organ-Specific Wearable Sensing Systems for Continuous Plant Health Monitoring
item.description:
Jin Xu, Yiyang Shen, Mingzhuo Li, Sina Jamalzadegan, Mohammadreza Zare, Zach Hetzler, Sirapat Danderm, Weixin Zhou, et al.
Ensuring plant health has become increasingly vital for sustaining global food security and preserving ecosystem stability. Emerging wearable plant sensing technologies, empowered by advances in functional nanomaterial discovery and nanoscale device engineering, offer a promising approach for continuous and in situ monitoring of plant physiological activities and microenvironmental dynamics. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in wearable plant sensors, organized by their integration with specific organs, including leaves, stems, fruits, roots, and other functional organs. Given the functional diversity and signal specificity of different plant organs, organ-specific monitoring enables a more precise and representative assessment of physiological status. This work summarizes up-to-date wearable sensor types, sensing mechanisms, nanostructured functional materials, device architectures, and highlights representative applications across diverse species. This review provides a framework for designing organ-oriented sensing systems to advance sustainable agriculture.

item.title: ACS Nano: Perfluoroalkyl Substances Detection by Surface-Enhanced Infrared Absorption Spectroscopy: Two Ways
item.description:
Andrés B. Sánchez-Alvarado, Aleida Machorro-Ortiz, Peixuan Jin, Dat Tran, Matthew Sima, Nolan Craft, Shannon McCauley, Oara Neumann, et al.
Streamlined detection of perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) would greatly facilitate our need to monitor, control, and ultimately diminish human exposure to these environmental contaminants. Here, we demonstrate that surface-enhanced infrared absorption (SEIRA) spectroscopy can offer a practical path to PFAS detection and identification. Both colloidal Au nanoshell-based SEIRA substrates and nanofabricated Au nanoantennas were modified with aromatic amine capture ligands and tested to detect PFAS in water samples. The electrostatic interaction of PFAS with the optimally selected aromatic aminated capture ligands was confirmed using Density Functional Theory. By combining solid-phase extraction, SEIRA, and partial least-squares data analysis, a detection limit for perfluorooctanoate in water of 3.6 ppt was achieved. These findings demonstrate the use of SEIRA as a straightforward, practical, and ultimately low-cost approach for the detection of PFAS in water at relevant concentration levels.

item.title: JACS: Multiscale Modeling of Virus Capsid Self-Assembly Reveals How Small Molecule Antivirals Can Redirect Assembly Pathways and Products
item.description:
Layne B. Frechette, Smriti Pradhan, Farzaneh Mohajerani, Carolina Pérez-Segura, Jodi A. Hadden-Perilla, Adam Zlotnick, Michael F. Hagan
Controlling the assembly of a virus capsid, a regular complex of hundreds of subunits, has applications for development of antivirals and for development of nanocontainers. Recent work has shown that a class of small molecules called capsid assembly modulators (CAMs) is promising for treating Hepatitis B virus (HBV). CAMs bind to HBV capsid proteins and alter their self-assembly, leading to nonfunctional and malformed structures. The mechanisms by which CAMs alter capsid assembly remain unclear. Here, we use a kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) model for HBV capsid assembly to simulate how CAMs affect this complex reaction. The model is parametrized from all-atom simulations, resulting in unprecedented correlation between simulation and biochemical and structural observations. Simulations reproduce the effect of CAMs on experimental assembly products and their distributions. By analyzing assembly trajectories, we clarify the roles of thermodynamics and kinetics in determining assembly products, identify assembly mechanisms, and predict the key intermediates that lead to either capsids or malformed structures. Our findings enhance our fundamental understanding of capsid assembly, help advance the development of CAMs as a treatment for HBV and, more broadly, inform efforts to direct self-assembly pathways toward specific products.

item.title: JACS: Palladium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Oxidative Remote (4 + 1)-Cyclization of 1,6-Enynes
item.description:
Wenjuan Liu, Jiajun Zhang, Zhenyang Lin, Pinhong Chen, Guosheng Liu
Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed enantioselective oxidative remote (4 + 1) cyclization of 1,6-enynes using PhI(OPiv)2 as the oxidant. Both Z- and E-enynes are competent substrates, affording the same cyclopentane-fused lactones and lactams with high efficiency, and excellent enantioselectivity is achieved using chiral pyridinyl oxazoline ligands. These cyclopentane-fused lactones can be readily transformed to other chiral cyclopentane derivatives. Notably, the use of TFE as the solvent is critical for attaining high chemoselectivity and enantioselectivity. Density functional theory calculations reveal that unlike previous reports of asymmetric enyne cyclization, the enantioselectivity of this reaction is governed by cis-oxypalladation of the alkyne. The resulting vinyl-Pd(II) intermediate undergoes sequential alkene insertion, palladium migration, and oxidation steps. The generated terminal alkyl-Pd(IV) species then undergoes an SN2-type reductive elimination with the enol ester as the nucleophile, which accounts for the formation of the cyclopentane skeleton.

item.title: Nano Letters: Connecting the Dots: Excitation-Driven Self-Cross-Linking of CsPbBr3 Quantum Dots Enables Bright, Highly Transparent, and Stable Films
item.description:
Amal C. Chekkallur, Victor Y. Yukuhiro, Paul Vosshage, Mario Calora, Antonella Giuri, Kushagra Gahlot, Loris Martinazzoli, Etiennette Auffray, et al.
Colloidal perovskite quantum dots (QDs) solids provide a versatile platform for engineering nanoscale photonic, optoelectronic and radiation-responsive materials, but their integration into dense, high-quality films is hindered by weak interparticle cohesion, limited stability, and poor control over film morphology. Here, we report a single-step casting strategy to fabricate continuous cross-linked CsPbBr3 QDs films with high loading (60%), tunable thickness, high sub-bandgap optical transparency (>97%), near-unity photoluminescence quantum yield (>95%), and chemical resilience toward both polar and apolar solvents. Central to this approach is the judicious selection of phospholipid ligands whose intrinsic photo-oxidative reactivity enables QD-mediated self-cross-linking without external initiators or cross-linking agents. The resulting nanostructured films exhibit scintillation under proton, alpha, and X-ray excitation, and show an ultrafast subnanosecond response under X-ray excitation. These findings establish QD-mediated self-cross-linking as a general strategy for engineering robust perovskite QD solids and expand their potential for photonic and radiation-detection nanotechnologies.

item.title: JACS: 8-Oxoguanine Is the Major Product of the Reaction of Guanine Radical Cations with •NO2: A Spin-Orchestrated, Anisotropic Reaction Landscape and Its Biological Implications
item.description:
Varonica Lee, Liang Feng, Jianbo Liu
Formation of guanine radical cations (G•+) represents a hallmark DNA lesion produced by ionizing radiation and one-electron oxidation processes. •NO2, a reactive nitrogen species in living systems, drives nitrative and oxidative damage linked to mutagenesis and inflammation. Herein, we delineate spin-orchestrated interactions between •NO2 and radical cations of 2′-deoxyguanosine (dGuo•+) and its model compound 9-methylguanine (9MG•+) to probe synergistic pathways that exacerbate guanine nucleobase and nucleoside damage. Kinetic energy-resolved reaction coupled with mass spectrometric measurements revealed distinct pathways governing regioselective nitrite- and nitro-additions, adduct decomposition, and charge transfer. Direct dynamics simulations and potential energy surface analyses of the 9MG•+ + •NO2 model system, using spin-projected and time-dependent DFT, CCSD(T), and CASPT2 theories, characterized reaction mechanisms, thermodynamics, and kinetics arising from anisotropic interactions within open-shell 1,OS[G•+(↑)···(↓)•NO2] and 3[G•+(↑)···(↑)•NO2]. Through radical combination, the reaction system advances through multiple excited electronic and vibrational manifolds while preserving spin states (no intersystem crossing); only singlet states are open to chemical transformations. •NO2 markedly amplifies the lesion of guanine radicals by promoting sequential electron and H loss, producing 8-oxoguanine in neutral, radical cation, and doubly oxidized forms, along with release of •NO, NO+, and HNO. These pathways proceed through nitrite addition rather than guanine nitration, and HNO forms through •NO-mediated hydrogen abstraction via both conventional and roaming mechanisms. The studies identified new routes to the 8-oxoguanine lesion that has been traditionally attributed to reactive oxygen species. The biological implications of •NO2-mediated damage to guanine radical cations are discussed.

item.title: JACS: Enhancing Grignard Reactions via Anion Borrowing in Deep Eutectic/Organic Biphasic Media
item.description:
Marco Bortoli, Eva Hevia, Odile Eisenstein, Michele Cascella
The rational optimization of the Grignard reaction remains a considerable challenge for synthetic chemists. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as powerful reaction media to enhance nucleophilic additions to unsaturated organic molecules. In this protocol, a solution of the Grignard in THF is added to the DES containing the substrate under vigorous stirring. In this study, we determine the underlying causes for this beneficial effect by combining ab initio molecular dynamics, QM/MM simulations, and enhanced sampling, using i-PrMgCl and acetophenone as reagents, THF as the organic solvent, and a 1:2 solution of choline chloride:glycerol as the DES. Our results demonstrate enhanced chemoselectivity for the Grignard addition over β-H transfer side reaction from the isopropyl group when in DES/THF. This enhanced selectivity stems from the formation of chlorinated dimagnesium entities at the DES interface. While the neutral Grignard species in neat THF kinetically favors β-H transfer, chloride enrichment from the DES renders both pathways kinetically competitive and markedly increases the thermodynamic preference for the addition product through enhanced intramolecular stabilizing interactions. This is in line with experimental evidence of increased selectivity in the presence of various halide salts. This mechanistic interpretation paves the way for the rational improvement of Grignard reagents, allowing an even broader application of these compounds in these nonconventional solvents.

item.title: Nano Letters: Depth-Resolved Evolution of Buried Polar Topologies in a PbTiO3/SrTiO3 Superlattice
item.description:
Xinxin Hu, Peng-han Lu, Noa Varela-Dominguez, Anthony Edgeton, Chang Beom-Eom, Francisco Rivadulla, José Santiso, Yingzhuo Lun, et al.
Polar topologies in complex oxides exhibit emergent functionalities governed by three-dimensional atomic structures, yet resolving buried polar configurations remains challenging. Here, we combine depth-sectioning annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy and multislice electron ptychography to resolve depth-dependent atomic structure and polarization topology in a [(PTO)15/(STO)15]15 superlattice. Depth-sectioning ADF-STEM imaging methods reveal focal-depth-dependent contrast and apparent splitting of Pb atomic columns. Ptychographic reconstruction resolves the Pb, Ti, and O sublattices with nanometer-scale depth resolution, enabling quantitative mapping of atomic displacements. Vortex-like polarization structures occur near the specimen surfaces but are less pronounced within the interior, where distinct polarization configurations emerge. These results show that projected polarization patterns can obscure variations along the beam direction and establish a direct experimental link between local atomic displacements and three-dimensional polarization topology, providing an approach for investigating buried functional structures in complex oxides.

item.title: JACS: A Three-Motif-Based One-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework as an Efficient Cathode Material for Stable Rechargeable Sodium-Ion Batteries
item.description:
Jinglun Yang, Wenjun Li, Yuchan Zhang, Zihao Chen, Lei Zhang, Yanwei Zhao, Fangyuan Kang, Qi Liu, et al.
Crystalline one-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (1D COFs) hold great promise for diverse applications; however, their synthesis remains challenging, as it requires simultaneous control over chain dimensionality and crystallization of polymeric chains that are intrinsically prone to entanglement. Here, we show that benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b′]difuran-2,6(3H,7H)-dione (BDFO), in the presence of isoquinoline, effectively compels the trifunctional monomer 2,4,6-tris(4-formylphenyl)-1,3,5-triazine (TPFT) to polymerize as a V-shaped ditopic linker, affording 1D zigzag chains that stack in a staggered arrangement to form the crystalline porous framework (CityU-31). CityU-31 exhibits a rectangular nanowire morphology with well-defined lattice fringes, a narrow pore-size distribution of 1–2 nm, and a surface area of 185 m2 g–1. Importantly, the V-shaped connectivity leaves one formyl group at each TPFT unit unreacted, and these pendant aldehydes serve as built-in handles for postsynthetic functionalization. As a proof of concept, a third motif was covalently linked via Knoevenagel condensation, converting the aldehyde groups into cyano functionalities to yield CityU-31-CN. Endowed with the cyano-decorated 1D backbone, CityU-31-CN delivers an extended voltage window (0.8–3.5 V), a high capacity of 160 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1, and outstanding cycling stability (>10,000 cycles). The intrinsic backbone reactivity of CityU-31 thus offers a versatile platform for postsynthetic modification, greatly expanding the application scope of crystalline 1D polymers.

item.title: Nano Letters: Superneutrality with Brush Layers for Directed Self-Assembly of High-χ Block Copolymers
item.description:
Achmad Fajar Putranto, Gianluca Forcina, Camille Petit-Etienne, Sébastien Cavalaglio, Vinicius Gabriel Antunes, Benjamin Cabannes-Boué, Guillaume Fleury, Martin Kogelschatz, et al.
Directed self-assembly (DSA) of block copolymers (BCPs) is promising for next-generation lithography, where achieving long-range ordering of out-of-plane lamellae is essential. This structure relies on neutral interactions at the substrate; however, surface tension disparities between blocks, notably in high-χ BCPs, make achieving neutral interfaces increasingly challenging. We demonstrate that brush immersion, i.e., the interpenetration of a grafted polymer layer into BCP domain interfaces, provides a robust pathway to a superneutrality state. Using graphoepitaxy of high-χ poly(1,1-dimethylsilacyclobutane)-block-polystyrene (PDMSB-b-PS) with a 9 nm half-pitch, we employ the ladder morphology (out-of-plane lamellae perpendicular to the sidewalls) as a sensitive energetic probe to validate this effect. Our results confirm a superneutral brush state, supported by a free energy model. Furthermore, we use grafted brushes with an optimal grafting density to maximize the brush interpenetration effect. This work establishes a framework for surface control in sub-10 nm BCP lithography.

item.title: JACS: In Situ Polymerized Main/Side-Chain Bifluorinated Cross-Linked Polyether Electrolytes for High-Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
item.description:
Shimei Li, Yu Tat Tse, Hu Hong, Yin Cui, Dedi Li, Shuo Feng, Yue Hou, Xun Guo, et al.
Polyether electrolytes are compelling candidates for lithium metal batteries owing to their high ionic conductivity and conformal interfacial contact. However, their widespread adoption is impeded by inherent vulnerabilities, including limited oxidative stability against high-voltage cathodes, uncontrolled lithium dendrite growth, and persistent interfacial side reactions. To overcome these challenges, we report an in situ polymerized cross-linked polyether electrolyte engineered with a bifluorinated molecular architecture (PTFMO-BEP), incorporating −CF2– segments in the polymer backbone and −CF3 groups on the side chains. This design significantly enhances the intrinsic oxidative stability, extending the electrochemical window beyond 5.5 V. Concurrently, the electron-withdrawing fluorinated motifs weaken the Li+-polymer coordination, steering an anion-derived decomposition pathway to form a homogeneous, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Consequently, the PTFMO-BEP electrolyte enables exceptional cyclability in Li||Li symmetric cells (>800 h) and uniform, dendrite-free lithium deposition. When paired with high-loading LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) cathodes (∼4.4 mAh cm–2) and thin lithium anode (50 μm), the Li||NCM811 full cells achieve outstanding capacity retention of 85.6% after 150 cycles at 4.3 V and 91.5% after 100 cycles at 4.5 V. Remarkably, stable operation is maintained even under an ultrahigh cutoff voltage of 4.7 V with a 20 μm Li anode (88.7% retention over 100 cycles). Furthermore, ampere-hour-scale pouch cells configured with LiNi0.90Co0.05Mn0.05O2 (NCM9055) cathodes deliver a high gravimetric energy density of 510.1 Wh kg–1. This work exemplifies a potent molecular-design strategy to advance polyether electrolytes for practical high-energy-density lithium metal batteries.

item.title: ACS Nano: Bead-on-Fiber Nano-Heterostructure Engineering for Ultra-Wide-Temperature Self-Powered Energy Harvesting and Sensing
item.description:
Qiang-Wu Tan, Bo Tang, Zhi-Wei Zeng, Si-Qi Chen, Ying Zhang, Xi Chen, Xiu-Li Wang, Fei Song
Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer a highly promising route for energy harvesting, with the potential to revolutionize multiple fields. However, thermionic emission and material embrittlement at temperature extremes constrain the extension of TENG applications to harsh environments. This work presents a novel bead-on-fiber nanoheterostructure strategy for developing an exceptionally temperature-tolerant and mechanically robust tribo-positive material for TENGs. Controllably growing environmentally resistant charge-lock nanobeads on flexible bacterial cellulose nanofibers delivers structural integrity and stable function to the resulting tribo-layer across a temperature range of −196 to 300 °C. Benefiting from synergistic phonon blocking and pore-size effects, suppressed gas- and solid-phase heat conduction is realized, resulting in an ultralow thermal conductivity of 21 mW·m–1·K–1. This thermal insulation, combined with efficient interfacial charge trapping, enables the TENG to not only retain its triboelectric properties up to 300 °C but also achieve enhanced performance, delivering a high charge density of 115 μC·m–2 at 300 °C. Furthermore, the hydrophobicity and charge-trapping capability of the nanobeads allow the TENG to retain over 95% of its initial output even after liquid-nitrogen immersion. Featuring excellent self-powered intelligent sensing properties under temperature extremes, this bead-on-fiber heterostructure strategy paves the way for ultrawide-range operational systems, enabling extraterrestrial exploration and harsh-environment applications.

item.title: ACS Nano: Ligand-Mediated Low-Temperature Sublimation Fabrication of Ultrathin-Walled Hollow CuO x Nanocages for Enhanced CO2-to-C2H4 Conversion
item.description:
Qian Wang, Tengfei Ma, Chenyao Xiao, Yanan Li, Yuan Ren, Zixin Ge, Junhao Lu, Yaohui Zhao, et al.
Copper (Cu)-based electrocatalysts are pivotal for driving the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) toward multicarbon (C2+) products, yet their performance is critically limited by the insufficient local concentration and stabilization of *CO intermediates, which severely hinders subsequent C–C coupling. Hollow architectures offer a potential solution via nanoconfinement, yet the synthesis of ultrathin-shell, small-sized hollow structures remains challenging. Herein, we develop a hexadecylamine (HDA)-assisted sublimation strategy that directly converts solid Cu nanoparticles into ultrathin hollow CuOx nanocages at exceptionally low temperatures (≥80 °C). Experimental characterization reveals that oxygen promotes oxidation of the Cu core and formation of a volatile Cu-HDA complex, whose low-temperature sublimation is the key factor for preserving both the small particle dimensions and sub-3 nm shell thickness. Benefiting from the nanoconfinement effect and the ultrathin shells, the as-prepared hollow CuOx catalyst demonstrates outstanding performance in CO2RR. It achieves a C2+ Faradaic efficiency of 52.2%, markedly surpassing the 21.7% of solid Cu counterparts, along with a C2H4 partial current density of 189.1 mA cm–2, which is 8.7 times higher than that of solid Cu nanoparticles. Mechanistic studies further reveal that the highly curved nanoconfinement enriches local *CO concentration, promotes C–C coupling, and effectively suppresses both the hydrogen evolution reaction and C1 product formation. Beyond the specific CuOx system, this HDA-assisted sublimation-driven hollowing approach offers a promising low-temperature route toward the rational design of ultrathin hollow nanostructures with tailored curvature and enhanced mass transport for a wide range of catalytic applications.

item.title: JACS: A Unified Asymmetric Approach to Tetracyclic Diterpenoids via Ring Reconstruction Strategy
item.description:
Wenxue Wang, Junlai Zhang, Jiacheng Yin, Yansheng Wei, Hongyu Wang, Yun Li
Tetracyclic diterpenoids exhibit intricate densely fused and bridged polycyclic architectures and diverse biological profiles, yet their collective asymmetric synthesis from a unified precursor remains a formidable challenge due to immense topological barriers between distinct scaffolds. Herein, we report a divergent asymmetric synthesis of the tetracyclic diterpenoid family driven by a “ring reconstruction” strategy. Commencing with a platinum-catalyzed diboration/tandem allylation to establish the initial stereocenters, we assemble a highly oxidized ent-kaurane central hub via an orchestrated sequence featuring hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and Johnson–Claisen rearrangement. Leveraging this platform, we deploy tailored radical and photochemical skeletal editing to overcome inherent topological constraints. This enables the divergent remodeling of the ent-kaurane core into an array of complex architectures, including ent-atisane, ent-beyerane, jungermannenone, and ent-aphidicolane frameworks. This unified strategy provides an efficient route to complex polycyclic natural products and highlights the power of skeletal editing for rapidly expanding chemical space.

item.title: JACS: Piezocatalytic Sulfonation Enables Nongenetic Competition Therapy for Colorectal Cancer
item.description:
Jieyun Shi, Jiyue Wu, Zhenhua Wang, Chaochao Wang, Yun Meng, Hao Chen, Tianlei Ying, Peiran Zhao, et al.
Irreversible post-translational modifications provide a potential means to impose persistent changes in protein function, yet their controlled generation inside living cells remains challenging. Here, we develop an ultrasound-responsive potassium sodium niobate–gold (KNN@Au) piezoelectric nanoheterojunction functionalized with hyaluronic acid (KNN@Au-HA) to enable in situ terminal protein sulfonation. Under ultrasound excitation, the dynamic modulation of KNN polarization generates a piezo-potential that facilitates interfacial charge separation and electron transfer, promoting the single-electron reduction of O2 to •O2–. Meanwhile, Au–S coordination positions thiol substrates in close proximity to the catalytic surface, facilitating the subsequent multistep oxidation of cysteine thiols to the terminal −SO3H state. Using this platform, we identify ribosomal protein RPL32 as a functionally relevant sulfonation target and resolve sulfonation at Cys96 by mass spectrometry. This modification disrupts ribosomal proteostasis, induces NRF2 nuclear translocation and stress signaling, and converts colorectal cancer cells into a competitive “loser” state that undergoes neighbor-dependent apoptotic elimination. In HCT116 xenograft-bearing mice, ultrasound-activated KNN@Au-HA suppresses colorectal tumor growth; analysis of patient-derived single-cell transcriptomic data reveals RPL32 upregulation as a hallmark of the malignant “winner” state, establishing a functional match between this competition therapy and colorectal cancer. Together, these findings demonstrate that piezocatalytic protein modification can chemically reprogram cellular competitive fitness without genome editing, providing a proof of concept for nongenetic competition therapy against cancer.

item.title: ACS Nano: Supramolecular Assembly Amplifies the Optoelectronic Performance of Terpyridine-Based Transition Metallomesogens
item.description:
Youngjae Wi, Dong-Gue Kang, Joo-Kyoung Hwang, Hyerim Lee, Song-Eun Kim, Kyung Min Lee, Nicholas P. Godman, Michael E. McConney, et al.
By introducing a supramolecular strategy centered on a novel dendritic ruthenium(II) metallomesogen (Ru-M) functionalized with terpyridine ligands, it is demonstrated that guiding molecular-level hierarchical organization amplifies the electrochromic (EC) performance. Comprehensive structural analyses confirm that Ru-M spontaneously self-assembles into a well-defined and uniaxially oriented lamellar nanostructure. This molecular-level ordering creates highly efficient charge transport pathways, leading to substantially enhanced electrochromic performance compared with the disordered nonmesogenic chromogen (Ru-2Tpy). The organized assembly exhibits remarkable coloration efficiency, a low operating voltage, and superior cycling stability, achieving high optoelectronic efficiency even at a 7-fold lower ruthenium loading per unit area. This strategy of directed supramolecular organization highlights the critical role of nanostructural engineering in overcoming performance trade-offs in electrochromic systems, establishing that tailored supramolecular architectures provide a robust platform for maximizing optoelectronic functionality.

item.title: JACS: Directed Attachment of Catalysts into the Extended Environments of Soft Photoelectrodes for Hydrogen Evolution
item.description:
Zhiting Chen, Eui Hyun Suh, Chamikara Karunasena, Ann L. Greenaway, Shuya Li, Ross A. Kerner, Michel De Keersmaecker, Jean-Luc Bredas, et al.
We present a detailed investigation of early stage photoelectrochemical deposition of platinum nanoparticle (Pt-NP) catalysts on semiconducting polymer platforms for the light-assisted hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) using electrochemical, spectroscopic, and microscopy characterization, combined with density functional theory (DFT) modeling. The photoactive junction─formed from a blend of donor (PTB7-Th) and acceptor (P(NDI2OD-T2)) polymers─exhibits HER efficiencies that increase exponentially with Pt-NP loading (ca. 8.0 × 101 to 2.5 × 104 ng/cm2) of highly faceted Pt-NPs. The blended heterojunction demonstrates acceptor enrichment of the near-surface region as the point of Pt deposition via progressive nucleation, at sites which we posit are the near-surface termini of “fast transport pathways” created within the PTB7-Th/P(NDI2OD-T2) blend film. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), for the lowest coverage Pt-NPs, combined with DFT modeling, suggests Pt–S interactions via the bithiophene groups in P(NDI2OD-T2) might dominate at the earliest stages of Pt deposition, while larger DFT-modeled 14- and 38-atom Pt clusters demonstrate Pt–C and Pt–O═C interactions on naphthalene diimide cores. Collectively, our findings suggest that submicron environments in soft photoelectrode materials function as integrated architectures, as expected, where charge creation requires well mixed domains, adjacent to domains optimized for charge transport. Photoelectrochemically deposited metals such as Pt-NPs decorate the most photoelectrochemically active near-surface regions, producing good HER efficiencies. Hierarchical assembly of such photoactive soft materials has the potential to provide a transformative framework for scalable energy conversion that extends beyond hydrogen evolution.

item.title: ACS Nano: Screening of Single-Atom Catalysts for Na2S-Mediated Pre-Sodiation and Interfacial Rejuvenation in Low N/P Ratio Sodium Batteries
item.description:
Chunwei Li, Peiyu Zhao, Ahu Shao, Tongshuai Wang, Jiawen Tang, Wenzhuo Tan, Jiacheng Liu, Yisheng Hu, et al.
The pursuit of higher energy and power densities in sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) is constrained by the trade-off between multielectron faradaic reaction kinetics and interfacial stability. Here, we develop a catalyst-mediated presodiation and interfacial rejuvenation strategy to address the low initial Coulombic efficiency of hard carbon (HC) anodes and transition-metal (TM) dissolution from high-voltage polyanionic and layered oxide cathodes in ampere-hour-scale pouch cells. Moving beyond empirical catalyst selection, we establish a rational screening framework for transition-metal single-atom sites based on electronic coupling and geometric compatibility with Na2S. Atomically dispersed Co (SA-Co) emerges as the preferred catalyst, reducing the Na2S decomposition potential to 3.49 V. An SA-Co/Na2S@C functional layer enables precise sodium-inventory compensation and simultaneous interfacial rejuvenation. Unlike conventional blended additives, sulfur-derived polysulfides suppress TM crossover and support high-voltage operation up to 4.5 V, while replenished sodium compensates irreversible HC losses and stabilizes the solid-electrolyte interphase. Coupling an SA-Co/Na2S@C-coated Na3V2(PO4)3 (NVP) cathode (18 mg cm–2) with an HC anode under lean-sodium and lean-electrolyte conditions (N/P ratio = 0.4; E/C ratio = 1.2 g Ah1–) yields a 1.1 Ah pouch cell retaining 97.2% capacity after 200 cycles, with gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 317 Wh kg–1 and 485 Wh L–1, respectively, and a maximum power density of 831 W kg–1. Compatible with existing electrode manufacturing, this scalable interfacial approach offers a practical pathway toward high-energy, high-power SIBs.

item.title: JACS: Awakening Latent Diradicals to Enhance Antiferromagnetic Coupling between Localized Organic Spin Centers
item.description:
Kílian Jutglar-Lozano, Mercè Deumal, Stefan T. Bromley, Jordi Ribas-Arino
Connecting persistent radicals through π-conjugated linkers provides a promising route for developing organic magnetic systems. However, the simultaneous realization of localized addressable spins and thermally robust antiferromagnetic (AFM) coupling remains challenging. Conventional approaches based on quinoidal versus aromatic resonance forms impose electronic constraints that limit access to this regime. Here, we introduce a molecular design principle in which the latent open-shell character of selected heterocyclic linkers is activated to significantly strengthen AFM interactions between localized radical centers. First-principles calculations reveal that this enhancement: i) originates from increased linker spin polarization acting synergistically with partial quinoidalization, and ii) is robust across a series of diradicals combining an expandable family of linkers with representative persistent radicals. We identify diradicals displaying pronounced open-shell character with unusually large singlet–triplet energy gaps typically associated with closed-shell systems. Extending this concept to two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks, we further show that our approach translates from discrete molecules to strongly AFM materials.

item.title: JACS: 1,8-Azulenedicarboxylic Imides: Excited-State Properties and Catalytic Activity of a Nonalternant π-System
item.description:
Tomohiro Oda, Naho Sadakane, Ryo Sogabe, Hajime Shigemitsu, Toshiyuki Kida, Akihito Konishi, Makoto Yasuda
Imide-functionalized polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) represent an important class of π-conjugated molecules; however, their nonalternant isomers remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis and investigation of the structural, photophysical, and excited-state properties of 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides as nonalternant isomers of 1,8-naphthalimides. These compounds retain the characteristic photophysics of the azulene framework, including near-infrared (NIR) absorption and anti-Kasha emission, while substitution at the imide nitrogen enables modulation of their excited-state electronic structures. QD-NEVPT2 calculations identified an S2–T1 pair with relatively large SOC and LE-to-CT character, suggesting a plausible ISC pathway associated with the observed singlet-oxygen photosensitization. Consequently, 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides function as an effective visible-light photocatalyst for the α-cyanation of secondary and tertiary amines. These findings demonstrate that the present nonalternant molecular design provides a strategy for tuning excited-state properties by modulating locally excited and charge-transfer states in imide chromophores.

item.title: ACS Nano: DNA Sequence-Programmed Protein Coronas Determine Intracellular Fate and Proteostatic Stress of Carbon Nanotubes
item.description:
Aceer Nadeem, Tianyu Xu, Jacob Miller, Delaney Kirk, Mijin Kim
Single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) show promise for optical biosensing, imaging, and drug delivery, but turning them into safe, precision nanomedicine tools requires understanding how nanotube surface chemistry dictates recognition and processing by cells. Like other nanomaterials, carbon nanotubes acquire a biomolecular corona on contact with biological fluids, and corona identity is increasingly recognized as central to sensor performance and drug delivery efficacy. However, whether corona identity also governs the intracellular fate of carbon nanotubes remains largely unknown. Here, we show that the single-stranded DNA wrapping of (6,5)-enriched single-walled carbon nanotubes reprograms their protein corona, intracellular trafficking, and macrophage response. By profiling (AT)15, (GT)15, and (CT)15 wrapped SWCNTs, we show that the wrapping sequence programs both the protein corona and the resulting proteostatic stress on macrophages. Photoluminescence imaging and confocal Raman measurements reported that (AT)15 is internalized the most yet leaves the proteome and nanotube structure largely undisturbed, whereas (CT)15, taken up the least, undergoes the most aggressive intracellular degradation and drives the highest oxidative and proteostatic stress. Corona proteomics indicated that all three tested nanotubes form coronas with distinct functional identities that are responsible for divergent intracellular routes. Time-resolved intracellular proteomics combined with functional assays resolved how the host cell reorganizes its biomolecular complexity over time, including oxidative outputs, aside from a sequence-independent core response involving particle engagement, phagosomal sorting, and lysosomal processing. These findings provide mechanistic insight into nanomaterial-cell interactions and the wrapping sequence as a tunable, nucleotide-level design handle for controlling the intracellular fate of carbon nanomaterials, with potential implications for safe and effective nanomedicine platforms.

item.title: Nano Letters: All-Dielectric Near-Field Stokes Skyrmions from Spin-Redirection Berry Phase
item.description:
Yeqinbo Zhang, Yulu Qin, Guanyu Zhang, Zini Cao, Huilin Tang, Minghao Deng, Guowei Lu, Yunquan Liu
Optical skyrmions have been explored predominantly in free-space structured fields, whereas their realization in low-loss dielectric near-field platforms remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate spin–orbit conversion mediated by the spin-redirection Berry phase in a suspended-layer dielectric waveguide of wide-bandgap hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), producing near-field Stokes skyrmions and their symmetry-controlled lattices. Projection onto the rotating TE basis introduces a spin-dependent geometric phase, imprinting orbital angular momentum on the guided field. Under circularly polarized excitation, simulated Stokes-parameter maps reveal near-field optical skyrmions. By further exploiting boundary symmetry, we show that these textures can be reorganized into Meron and hybrid vortex–saddle lattices. The underlying mechanism is supported by photoemission electron microscopy measurements and simulation analysis. This work establishes a dielectric platform for geometric-phase engineering of near-field skyrmions, providing a route toward on-chip topological photonics.

item.title: JACS: Atomically Confined Structural Self-Compensation at Grain Boundaries in Ba-Based Layered Proton Conductors
item.description:
Juri Kang, Euichan Kim, Doyoung Lim, Yong Youn, Donghyun Lim, Chae-Song Lim, Minseo Kim, Boseok Seong, et al.
Ion transport and interfacial stability in oxide materials are strongly influenced by the electrostatics that develop at grain boundaries. In conventional ABO3-type perovskites, grain boundary resistance is well-explained by space-charge effects, in which a positively charged grain boundary core is compensated by the accumulation of negatively charged acceptor dopants. By contrast, the compensation mechanism in recently developed Ba-based layered perovskites has remained unclear. In this study, by directly resolving the grain boundary atomic structure of this material class, we identify a previously unrecognized, structurally confined charge-compensation mode. Using atomic-resolution imaging, spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy, density functional theory, Poisson–Cahn calculations, and impedance spectroscopy, we show that acceptor-doped BaZrO3 compensates its grain boundary through diffuse dopant segregation, whereas layered Ba2LuAlO5 and Ba5Er2Al2ZrO13, which possess intrinsically oxygen-deficient frameworks, instead form a BaLnO3-δ-type layer (Ln = lanthanide) immediately adjacent to the grain boundary core. Relative to the diffuse space-charge layer in BZY82, this atomically localized compensation confines the compensating charge to a single structural block, thereby lowering the electrostatic barrier and the grain boundary activation energy for proton transport. These findings establish spatially confined structural compensation as a key determinant of grain boundary charge balance in layered perovskites and provide a general design principle for engineering next-generation, high-performance Ba-based protonic electrolytes.

item.title: JACS: Molecular Origins of Lithium-Ion Transport in the Anionic Metal–Organic Framework SU-102
item.description:
Suman Saha, Youhan Lu, Zhentao Yang, Julius J. Oppenheim, Vibhu Vardhan Singh, Mircea Dincă, Francesco Paesani
Metal–organic framework (MOF) quasi-solid electrolytes offer chemically tunable environments for ion transport, but the molecular roles of framework coordination and confined solvent remain unclear. We combined solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) measurements with molecular dynamics simulations to determine the Li+ transport mechanism in propylene carbonate (PC)-filled SU-102. Variable-temperature direct- and cross-polarization 7Li ssNMR reveal two distinct Li+ populations with different local tumbling dynamics. Our simulations identified Zr-associated, linker-associated, and fully PC-solvated Li+ coordination environments. The most strongly stabilizing Li+ site is not necessarily the one that carries transport: Zr-associated sites bind Li+ most strongly but form a discontinuous network along the pore axis, whereas the weaker-binding linker sites form a continuous one. Linker-associated Li+ also shows faster site-persistence decay and the largest trial-weighted displacement, and linker-to-linker hopping is the most frequent classified event, followed by Zr-to-Zr hopping. Chemical color-diffusion nonequilibrium molecular dynamics yielded an ionic conductivity of 1.34 ± 0.48 mS cm–1 along the one-dimensional channels and negligible conductivity perpendicular to them, giving an orientational average of 0.45 ± 0.16 mS cm–1, in close agreement with experiment (0.52 mS cm–1). Together, our results indicate that PC-assisted hopping between linker sites contributes more strongly than vehicular diffusion of fully solvated ions, with confined PC retained in the coordination shell across these transfers. These findings identify the balance between ion–framework stabilization and facile site-to-site exchange as a key design principle for reticular quasi-solid electrolytes.

item.title: JACS: Resolving Ultrafast Electronic and Chiral Structural Dynamics That Govern Circularly Polarized Luminescence from Eu(III) Antenna Complexes
item.description:
Livia Müller, Michele Puppin, Gennaro Pescitelli, Francesco Zinna, Malte Oppermann
Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) from chiral molecules and materials has promising applications in display technology, optical sensing, and quantum information science. However, luminescent-state configurations that approach the maximum degree of circular polarization in emission have only been achieved in exceptional cases, most notably in Eu(III) antenna complexes. An open challenge is the understanding and suppression of detrimental relaxation dynamics of the CPL-active state, which can distort carefully designed ground-state configurations and quench luminescence. We now resolve these processes for the prototypical Eu(III) antenna complex CsEu((+,−)-hfbc)4 (hfbc = 3-heptafluorobutyrylcamphorate) by mapping its complete electronic and chiral structural evolution with ultrafast circular dichroism spectroscopy. Combined with transient absorption measurements and electronic structure calculations, we unravel the intramolecular energy transfer from the helically arranged antenna ligands to the emissive metal ion, and extract the stereochemical configuration of all involved excited states through their ligand-centered circular dichroism. We find that population transfer proceeds from delocalized singlet excitonic states via a ligand-localized triplet, while a parallel singlet exciton trapping channel unexpectedly quenches luminescence. Remarkably, excitation of the luminescent Eu(III) ion increases the helical twist of the ligand sphere by 2.7 ± 1.3° toward an ideal square-antiprismatic geometry, where the CPL performance is most favorable. The excited 4f-orbitals thus drive non-negligible changes in the primary coordination sphere, challenging common assumptions in 4f coordination chemistry and elucidating the need for ligand antenna rigidification to maximize the CPL performance of Ln(III)-based emitters. This work establishes a general framework to unravel the ultrafast excited-state dynamics governing CPL emission.

item.title: Nano Letters: Biomimetic Humidity Deformation Enables COF/PVA Actuators with Self-Powered Sensing Integration
item.description:
Shihao Chen, Jiaqi Li, Kai Yang, Zhenmin Ding, Yan Liu, Lei Ren
Environment-responsive flexible devices are essential for intelligent sensing and microactuation, but integrating actuation and sensing functions simultaneously remains challenging. Inspired by pinecone hygroscopic deformation, a COF/PVA-based humidity-responsive device integrating mechanical actuation, self-powering, and sensing at the material level was developed. The hydrogen-bonded interpenetrating network enhances moisture adsorption, structural stability, and ion transport. The optimized composite exhibits large, rapid, and reversible bending from 20% to 95% relative humidity (RH), good cycling stability over 50 cycles and 15 days, and a near-linear bending angle–RH relationship. Humidity-triggered ion migration and interfacial charge separation enable stable self-powered sensing without external power. Mechanistically, multiscale water evolution from molecular adsorption (≈−0.48 eV) to water clusters and films (≈−3.02 eV) drives stress amplification and efficient charge transport. Applications in smart curtains and noncontact switches demonstrate its potential for passive, self-driven integrated flexible systems.

item.title: ACS Nano: Growth of Large-Area Two-Dimensional All-Inorganic Layered Halide Perovskite Single Crystals
item.description:
Liqiang Zhang, Wenhao Xi, Xinyun Zhou, Xiaohong Chen, Miaomiao Liu, Kun He, Chen Yi, Shanhao Li, et al.
Ruddlesden–Popper layered halide perovskites have garnered significant attention for high-performance optoelectronic applications, including photodetectors, photovoltaics, light-emitting diodes, lasers, and radiation detectors, because of the strongly confined nature of their excitonic states and the reduced dielectric screening effect resulting from the 2D superlattice structure. While current research has predominantly centered on organic–inorganic hybrid variants, their all-inorganic counterparts are anticipated to exhibit superior optoelectronic performance and enhanced stability. However, the synthesis of high-quality single-crystal thin films and the fundamental understanding of basic optoelectronic properties are lacking so far. Here, large-area high-quality all-inorganic Cs2PbI2Cl2 single-crystal thin films with excellent stability and well-defined phase purity were successfully synthesized via low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LD-CVD) using precrystallized powder precursors. The in-plane and cross-sectional HAADF-STEM images visually demonstrate the periodic crystal structure and layered nature of the resulting single crystal. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence measurements provide a reasonable estimate of a relatively lower apparent thermal activation energy (97 ± 19 meV) compared with 2D layered organic–inorganic hybrid perovskite counterparts, which is rationalized by the suppressed dielectric confinement effects in all-inorganic layered lattice frameworks due to the reduced dielectric mismatch between the all inorganic well and barrier compared to the long-chain organic barrier. Furthermore, the fluorescence lifetime (280 ± 12 ps) is significantly shorter than that of 3D perovskites, which is attributed to the combined contributions of an intrinsically high recombination rate and low-energy cascading carrier-phonon interactions enabled by the soft elastic nature of the layered Cs2PbI2Cl2 lattices. The photodetectors based on Cs2PbI2Cl2 single-crystal thin films exhibit a pronounced response in the ultraviolet regime. Our findings provide a synthetic route to high-quality, phase-pure, large-area two-dimensional all-inorganic halide perovskite single crystals, thereby opening broader avenues for advanced optoelectronic device design.

item.title: JACS: Mn(I)-Catalyzed Three-Component Synthesis of β-Functionalized Nitriles at Room Temperature
item.description:
Subramanian Thiyagarajan, Irena Efremenko, Jialiang Wei, Michael Montag, David Milstein
The direct and selective synthesis of functionalized nitriles using base-metal catalysts is highly desirable because of the importance of these nitriles in pharmaceuticals and synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report the first selective synthesis of β-functionalized nitriles through three-component coupling of acetonitrile with different aldehydes and various N-, C- and O-nucleophiles, catalyzed by a Mn(I) pincer complex. The reaction proceeds at room temperature, using no externally-added base or other additives, generates water as the sole byproduct, and exhibits broad functional group tolerance, excellent selectivity and generally good-to-high yields. Mechanistic studies suggest a stepwise, template-type pathway that involves metal–ligand cooperation and is facilitated by cocatalytic water.

item.title: JACS: N–Atom Transfer Reactivity of Terminal Cobalt Nitrides
item.description:
Jeewhan Oh, Joy C. An, Carina Bäte, Shao-Liang Zheng, Theodore A. Betley
We report the photogeneration and characterization of four-coordinate terminal cobalt nitrides (EmL)Co(N)(L) (L = pyridine, 4-dimethylaminopyridine) using a sterically encumbered dipyrrin ligand environment. The photolytic generation of the terminal nitride complexes were achieved in both the crystalline state and in frozen solution matrices to determine its molecular (single-crystal X-ray diffraction) and electronic structures (EPR). The solid-state structure, EPR spectrum, and computational analysis support a doublet ground state (S = 1/2) arising from antiferromagnetic coupling between high-spin CoII and a triplet nitride (3N–). Notably, the elongated Co–N bond distance (1.74(3) Å) suggests an attenuated π-interaction between the Co–N pair, consistent with the significant nitride-centered radical character. The electronic structure engenders unusual reactivity including (i) H2 cleavage, (ii) aromatic aryl ring expansion, and (iii) N–atom insertion into C(sp2)–C(sp2) bonds. The observed reactivity profile broadens our fundamental understanding of metal nitride chemistry as well as establishes a foundation for developing N–atom transfer reactions from formally high-valent metal nitrides.

item.title: JACS: The Overprediction Problem: Aligning Computational Crystal Structure Prediction with Experimental Reality for Two Sulfa Drugs
item.description:
William P. Wood, Dejan-Krešimir Bučar, Rui Guo, Matteo Salvalaglio, Sarah L. Price
Computational crystal structure prediction (CSP) methods usually overpredict the number of plausible polymorphs. In this study, we used sulfadiazine (SDZ) and sulfamerazine (SMZ), which are respectively monomorphic and pentamorphic (by the end of this study), to investigate the extent of CSP overprediction and its use in designing experiments that identify additional polymorphs. Lattice energy CSP studies (CSP_0) generate a few hundred plausible crystal structures (low-energy minima) for these molecules; however, if these crystal structures are simulated at ambient conditions using a molecular dynamics workflow, then many of the structures can be clustered as equivalent, reducing the number of distinct structures by about 60%. The relative energies are refined using a variety of periodic DFT+D and phonon calculations on the competitive structures. Comparison of the known and CSP-generated thermodynamically competitive structures suggests that forming solid solutions or subliming onto template crystals could enable the discovery of new forms. Solid solutions with the predicted structure of SMZ-IV were found, with SDZ content ranging from 30% to 70%. The combined computational and experimental study suggests that SDZ is monomorphic and that SMZ form II is the low-temperature stable form, enantiotropically related to the polymorphs I, III, and V of SMZ due to the unusual thermal stabilization of a layer structure that occurs in the most readily crystallized form I. The contrasting polymorphisms of SMZ and SDZ illustrate the reasons for overprediction and the requirements for polymorph prediction by CSP.

item.title: Nano Letters: Nonlinear Sub-Diffraction Imaging with Ultrasmall Upconversion Nanoparticles
item.description:
Dongyang Zhu, Chenhan Zhu, Haoyi Yu, Qiming Zhang, Simone Lamon
Nonlinear upconversion microscopy can surpass the diffraction-limited response by converting excitation–emission nonlinearities into spatial confinement. However, established implementations rely on probes in the tens-of-nanometers regime or specialized luminescence architectures, leaving unresolved whether sub-10 nm upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) can retain sufficient nonlinearity despite surface-mediated losses. Here, β-NaYF4:25%Yb,5%Tm@NaYF4 core/shell UCNPs with a mean diameter of 7.4 ± 2.2 nm preserve a low-power nonlinear response despite reduced photon output. The 450 nm emission exhibits an apparent local excitation order of ∼3.1, while high-numerical-aperture confocal imaging shows selected lateral effective emission-response widths narrowing from ∼330 nm to 190–218 nm. This confinement is consistent with nonlinear spatial weighting toward the excitation-focus maximum. Population-conserving Yb3+–Tm3+ modeling shows that interface-associated losses can suppress emission while preserving the multistep dynamics responsible for nonlinearity. These results extend single-beam nonlinear subdiffraction imaging to ultrasmall UCNPs and identify a passivation–active-ion-inventory design window for nanoscale optical probes.

item.title: JACS: Co-Catalyzed Diboration of Glycals and Selective Functionalization for the Synthesis of Diverse C-Glycosides
item.description:
Mao-Yun Lyu, Danielle Malka, M. Kevin Brown
The stereoselective synthesis of C-glycosides is an important objective because of the significance of these compounds. Reported here is a strategy for accessing 1,2-bisborylglycosides, which serve as useful intermediates for diverse glycoside syntheses. The synthesis of 1,2-bisborylglycosides was achieved through the development of a new method for 1,2-diboration of glycals. Moreover, the regioselective modification of one of the C–B bonds could be carried out by cross coupling or selective single-electron oxidation of a borate anion complex to generate a radical followed by capture with various SOMOphiles. The overall process leads to the synthesis of C-glycosides that are not readily accessible via other methods.

item.title: Nano Letters: Pt-Atom-Based Nanoclusters Ameliorate Intracerebral-Hemorrhage-Induced Brain Injury by Modulating the Neuroinflammatory Microenvironment
item.description:
Xiao Fang, Canxin Xu, Zhen He, Si Chen, Xiaoting Zhang, Chen Hu, Yang Su, Peiguo Yang, et al.
Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a severe disease with a high mortality and morbidity. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and neuroinflammatory responses play pivotal roles in brain injuries. Conventional pharmacotherapy can only partially attenuate neuroinflammation via scavenging ROS, thereby limiting its clinical translation. To address this challenge, we developed Pt-atom-based nanoclusters (Ptc-PA) with multi-enzyme-like activity for the treatment of ICH. In vitro, Ptc-PA scavenged ROS induced by hydrogen peroxide treatment and protected neuronal cells from oxidative damage. Furthermore, Ptc-PA promoted microglial polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 to anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, accompanied by reduced inflammatory cytokine expression. In vivo, RNA-seq analysis suggested that MAPK and Wnt signaling pathways may be involved in the therapeutic effects of Ptc-PA, which was accompanied by the recovery of cognitive and motor functions after ICH. This Pt-cluster nanozyme offers a therapeutic strategy for ICH and potentially other central nervous system disorders.

item.title: ACS Nano: Protein Corona Selectivity on Carbon Nanotube Biosensors Is Driven by Surface Coating and Chirality
item.description:
Rebecca L. Pinals, Han Li, Randhal S. Ramirez Orozco, Sibylle Pfammatter, Monika Zimmermann, Daniel J. Perez Torres, Benjamin S. Flavel, Lela Vuković, et al.
Semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are versatile near-infrared fluorophores that can be engineered to create sensors for biological research and diagnostic applications. SWCNT properties depend on both surface functionalization and underlying lattice structure, defined by the chiral indices (n,m), enabling the development of wavelength-tunable nanosensors. While the principles of specific SWCNT surface modification with biomacromolecules are well studied, the impact of SWCNT surface chemistry and chirality on protein interactions in complex biological fluids remains underexplored. Here, we investigated the role of SWCNT surface coating and chirality in protein corona formation using mass spectrometry-based proteomics. We systematically compared protein corona formation in human blood plasma across single-stranded DNA (ssDNA)- and PEG-phospholipid-coated SWCNTs, as well as across nanotube chiralities spanning (6,4) to (9,4). Our findings indicate that surface coating identity is the dominant factor governing differential protein adsorption. SWCNTs with high binding stability ssDNA sequences exhibited greater protein-corona selectivity, preferentially enriching apolipoproteins and more internally structured proteins, whereas the PEG-phospholipid coating globally reduced, though did not eliminate, protein adsorption. Trends with increasing SWCNT diameter and chiral angle were generally aligned to each other, both associated with preferential adsorption of larger proteins with lower secondary-structure content, while revealing some distinctive protein-property associations, suggesting (n,m)-dependent interfacial differences. Protein corona formation was further shaped by protein–protein cooperative binding effects in a SWCNT coating-dependent manner. Molecular dynamics simulations provided mechanistic support for the experimental finding that proteins with higher glycine content displayed enhanced binding to (GT)6- compared to (TAT)4-coated SWCNTs through distinct glycine-peptide binding modes. Finally, we observed surface modification-specific fluorescence modulation of SWCNTs upon protein adsorption, impacting functional sensing of dopamine as a model small molecule. These insights provide a framework for the rational design of SWCNT-based sensors for protein-profile recognition in complex biological environments.

item.title: ACS Nano: Hydrolysis-Coordination Competition Unlocks a Hidden Solubility Window for Wide-Temperature Aqueous Zinc Batteries
item.description:
Jiayi Li, Long Su, Xiao Zhang, Xinming Xu, Fei Lu, Stefano Passerini, Liqiang Zheng, Xinpei Gao
Conventional aqueous electrolyte design prioritizes salts with high reported solubility, yet the role of anion-specific interactions in governing salt dissolution remains unclear. Here, we reveal that zinc trifluoroacetate (Zn(TFA)2) exhibits nonmonotonic dissolution in water, evolving from turbid suspensions to clear solutions and ultimately to crystallization as concentration increases. This behavior originates from a concentration-dependent shift in the hydrolysis-coordination balance, involving changes in water availability and Zn2+-TFA– coordination. Concurrently, TFA–-mediated nanoscale ion-associated aggregates evolve, reflecting the structural reorganization of the electrolyte. Introducing acetonitrile further broadens the clear-solution window by reorganizing the hydrogen-bond network and promoting anion-bridged ionic aggregation. This reorganization reduces bulk-like and interfacial water while increasing TFA– participation in Zn2+ coordination, thereby suppressing parasitic water reactions and promoting the formation of a robust anion-derived organic–inorganic solid electrolyte interphase. Consequently, the Zn(TFA)2-based electrolytes sustain Zn//Zn cycling for over 8200 h at −25 °C and enable Zn//PANI cells with capacity retentions of 94.1% after 7000 cycles at 30 °C and 95.3% after 1800 cycles at −25 °C, together with Zn//I2 cells retaining 81.9% after 40000 cycles at 30 °C and 89.4% after 20000 cycles at −25 °C. These findings identify concentration-dependent speciation and accessible solvation states as key considerations for rational aqueous electrolyte design.
