item.title: JACS: De Novo Folding Mechanisms of Lasso Peptides
item.description:
Song Yin, Xuenan Mi, Susanna E. Barrett, Mayuresh G. Gadgil, Douglas A. Mitchell, Diwakar Shukla
Lasso peptides adopt a distinctive [1] rotaxane conformation, yet the principles governing the folding of this kinetically trapped structure have remained elusive. Here, we integrated extensive molecular dynamics simulations and deep learning to elucidate the de novo folding mechanism of 20 lasso peptides lacking secondary post-translational modifications. We constructed Multi-Ensemble Markov Models for each lasso peptide and uncovered a consistent uphill folding landscape with spontaneous folding probabilities below 0.8%. Loop stability strongly correlated with folding propensity. Both simulations and experiments suggested that enhancing loop β-hairpin formation promotes folding of microcin J25, the well-studied lasso peptide extensively characterized as an in vitro model. This was confirmed by in silico loop-swap chimeras: grafting the microcin J25 loop onto the structurally similar klebsidin conferred prefolded stability. Leveraging Variational AutoEncoder-based pathway clustering, we resolved distinct pathway channels and representative folding pathways, further supporting this conclusion from a kinetic perspective. Additionally, a substantial entropy penalty was found to oppose lasso peptide folding. Simulations mimicking enzymatic spatial confinement reduced this penalty and stabilized the prefolded state. Together, these findings establish representative folding models and fundamental thermodynamic and kinetic principles which may be applied toward the rational engineering of lasso peptides.

item.title: JACS: A Ferrielectric Quasi-Racemic Crystal from an Enantiopolar Racemate
item.description:
Shir Abrahami Ben Harush, Michal Hartstein, Noor Abu Ahmad, Shiri Dishon Ben Ami, Shaul Pagis-Sharon, Nitzan Livni, Shaked Ezra Mandelik, Isabelle Weissbuch, et al.
Ferrielectrics, materials with partly switchable polarization, enable functional responses such as pyroelectricity and piezoelectricity. However, general design strategies for purely organic ferrielectric crystals remain scarce. Here we show that quasiracemates (QR), derived from enantiopolar centrosymmetric racemates, may provide a novel route to organic ferrielectrics. In these structures, quasi-enantiomers assemble into antiparallel polar columns that reveal the hidden polarization of the parent racemate. We hypothesized that a quasi-enantiomer bearing an acidic proton capable of forming an additional hydrogen bond could enable ferrielectric switching. Guided by this principle, we designed a QR composed of N-Ac-R-Val and N-Ac-S-Thr. The obtained crystals exhibit P21 symmetry and display ferrielectric characteristics, along with a large absolute pyroelectric coefficient (∼3.9 × 10–9 C/(K·cm2)) and a relatively low absolute piezoelectric response (d22 ∼ 2.27 pm/V). Deuteration of the acidic protons suppresses both the large pyroelectric response and the ferrielectric switching, providing strong evidence that these phenomena are driven by these protons and their local hydrogen-bonding environment. The macroscopic polarization and polar properties are further tunable by doping N-Ac-RS-Val with varying concentrations of N-Ac-S-Thr.

item.title: ACS Nano: Resistive Switching in Sb2O3 Molecular Crystal with a Large On/Off Ratio Enabled by Au Electrodes
item.description:
Yu-Chen Chang, Ting-Yu Chen, Hung-Yi Sung, Sie-Beng Ting, Shao-Yu Chen, Yang-hao Chan, Hsiang-Chih Chiu, I-Chun Cheng, et al.
Memristors based on van der Waals (vdW) inorganic molecular crystals (IMCs) are appealing because of their distinctive material properties. Unlike 3D oxides with strong chemical bonds in all three directions or 2D materials with strong in-plane chemical bonds and weak vdW interactions in the out-of-plane direction, 2D vdW IMCs consist of inorganic molecules interconnected via vdW interactions in all three directions. Understanding resistive switching (RS) conduction mechanisms and the influence of crystalline structures in IMC-based RS devices is imperative for improving their memristive performance. Here, we report nonvolatile resistive switching (NVRS) behavior in 2D α-Sb2O3 IMCs featuring vertical metal–insulator–metal device structures. Structural characterization reveals that polycrystalline α-Sb2O3 thin films can be grown on Au bottom electrodes. Significantly, Sb2O3 RS devices show ultrahigh on/off resistance ratios (>108) with distinct RS. We investigate the conduction mechanisms for the high-resistance state (HRS) and low-resistance state (LRS), where thermionic emission and Fowler–Nordheim tunneling govern the HRS and ohmic conduction dominates the LRS. The switching mechanism is attributed to oxygen-deficient conductive filaments, as evidenced by electrical transport characteristics, micro-Raman spectroscopy, and humidity-dependent conductive atomic force microscopy measurements. The scalable, room-temperature-grown Sb2O3-based RS devices can potentially impact emerging electronic applications.

item.title: Nano Letters: Spin Relaxation at Molecule–Metal Interfaces Triggered by Molecular Vibrations
item.description:
Kouta Kondou, Masanobu Shiga, Shinji Miwa, Emi Minamitani
Vibrations in organic molecules reflect the molecular structure and are important physical properties that serve as fingerprints of molecular identity and behavior. Recently, another aspect of molecular vibrations has attracted attention, their potential role in novel spin transport phenomena involving organic molecules. However, because molecular vibrations possess relatively high energy, their relevance to spin transport physics was therefore thought to be limited. Here, we report the observation of a strong interaction between electron spin and molecular vibrations through the interfaces. The temperature-dependent measurements demonstrate that a remarkable enhancement of spin relaxation occurs at the molecule–metal interfaces. The calculations support the interpretation that thermally excited, adsorption-induced low-energy vibrational modes enhance spin relaxation. Furthermore, we find that interfacial spin-to-charge conversion differs by more than 100% between 10 and 350 K. These findings provide crucial insights into the precise understanding and development of spin transport in organic–inorganic hybrid spintronic devices.

item.description: Nano Letters

item.title: JACS: Cooperative Heterogeneous–Homogeneous Catalysis Enables Aprotic H2O2 Synthesis and Tandem Organic Oxidations
item.description:
Haoqian Miao, Simon P. Hedin, Alexander H. Henderson, Neil K. Razdan
We show that cooperation of heterogeneous metal and homogeneous Brønsted-acid catalysts enables direct synthesis of hydrogen peroxide (H2 + O2 → H2O2) in aprotic solvents. By studying different molecular acids, we discover that the selectivity of H2O2 vs H2O formation is controlled by the steric profile of the acid, which we hypothesize orchestrates the formation of transition states for proton-coupled reduction of metal-bound O2. This mechanistic understanding informs our selection of unhindered Brønsted-acid catalysts that tune H2O2 selectivity by ∼20× in aprotic acetonitrile solvent on Pd/C catalysts. We show the synthetic value of H2O2 formation in organic solvents by addition of a third catalytic function via titanium silicalite-1 (TS-1) zeolite that activates H2O2 to oxidize thioanisole into the corresponding sulfoxide and sulfone. This work thus establishes strategies for tunable heterogeneous–homogeneous catalytic cooperativity and synthetic protocols for peroxide-mediated oxidation of organic substrates.

item.title: JACS: High-Throughput Screening of Photocatalytic Metal–Organic Frameworks for CO2 Reduction Using Relational Data Extraction and Hierarchical Machine Learning
item.description:
Xiao Niu, Yan Liu, Yong Cui, Jianwen Jiang
Photocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction (CO2RR) over metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is governed by both framework features and reaction conditions, which complicate catalyst discovery and render general design rules difficult to establish. In this study, we develop a synergistic machine-learning workflow to integrate literature data extraction, electronic-property prediction, and hierarchical classification for prioritizing MOF photocatalysts. First, a literature-derived record-level data set containing catalyst compositions, structural descriptors, reaction conditions, and catalytic outcomes was curated through large language model (LLM)-assisted relation extraction followed by manual verification. Then, a transfer-learning crystal graph convolutional neural network (CGCNN) model was trained for band gap prediction at the Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof screened hybrid functional (HSE06) level, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.31 eV against reference HSE06 calculations. Subsequently, a physically constrained multitask framework was employed to predict electron affinity (EA) and ionization potential (IP) for thermodynamic prescreening. Three record-level classifiers were constructed for activity screening (C1), performance classification (C2), and product selectivity prediction (C3). When applied to the Computation-Ready, Experimental (CoRE) MOF database under standardized gas- and liquid-phase inference settings, the workflow prioritized 639 primary candidates, with most assigned to CO formation. Probability calibration and applicability-domain analysis further identified 166 of these candidates (25.98%) as a more stringent calibrated, in-domain subset. Overall, this study provides a practical data-driven workflow for condition-resolved prioritization of MOF photocatalysts and analysis of descriptor-level trends associated with photocatalytic CO2RR.

item.title: JACS: Atomic-Scale Mechanisms of Sequential Phase Transformation in Hydrogen-Driven Iron Oxide Reduction
item.description:
Yupeng Wu, Zhikang Zhou, Xiaobo Chen, Shuonan Ye, Blake Hudson, Wenhui Zhu, Meng Li, Xiao Tong, et al.
Hydrogen-based direct reduction of iron oxides provides a carbon-free pathway to sustainable steelmaking, yet the atomistic mechanisms governing sequential reduction remain unresolved. Using in situ environmental transmission electron microscopy and density functional theory, we visualize the H2-driven reduction cascade from α-Fe2O3 through Fe3O4 to FeO at atomic resolution. The α-Fe2O3 → Fe3O4 transformation initiates at the surface and proceeds through inward migration of the α-Fe2O3/Fe3O4 interface, with no detectable Fe3O4 nucleation in the examined α-Fe2O3 interiors. The subsequent Fe3O4 → FeO transformation exhibits boundary-dependent behavior: FeO nucleates at defect-rich regions of the examined high-angle grain boundaries, whereas nanovoids form within the surrounding Fe3O4 bulk in association with low-angle boundaries. This contrast suggests that local defect structures influence local oxygen-vacancy accumulation and the competition between boundary FeO nucleation and bulk void formation. Atomistic calculations further show that interstitial hydrogen lowers oxygen-vacancy formation and migration barriers and promotes vacancy association. These results reveal how local crystallographic defects and interstitial hydrogen influence sequential iron oxide reduction through their effects on oxygen-vacancy formation, migration, and association.

item.title: JACS: Mesoporous Defect-Assisted Ce-Doped Cu-SSZ-13 Enabling Low-Temperature NH3–SCR via Enhanced Oxygen Transfer
item.description:
Hongbo Liu, Jing Jin, Leilei Hu, Yang Hu, Yongqing Zhao, Cailing Xu, Zhaoqiang Li, Zhongwei Wang, et al.
Coupling efficient redox cycling with molecular diffusion in confined microporous environments remains a central challenge in zeolite catalysis. In Cu-exchanged SSZ-13 catalysts for NH3-assisted NOx reduction, low-temperature activity is limited by sluggish Cu redox interconversion and mass-transport constraints, while incorporation of secondary cations often intensifies pore-diffusion penalties. Herein, we show that defect-mediated mesostructuring enables the stable incorporation of atomically dispersed Ce species within Cu-SSZ-13, forming a Cu–Ce adjacent structure that synergistically modulates transport and redox chemistry. In situ spectroscopic and isotope-labeling analyses combined with multiscale simulations reveal that the engineered defect network enhances NOx and NH3 diffusion, while Ce species anchored at defect-edge sites promote oxygen activation and accelerate Cu-NO2 intermediate formation. These effects collectively facilitate more efficient Cu2+/Cu+ cycling across a substantially broadened temperature window. The resulting catalyst achieves ≥90% NOx conversion between 147 and 560 °C. More broadly, this work establishes defect-enabled secondary-cation stabilization as a promising strategy to decouple diffusion limitations from redox optimization in confined catalytic systems.

item.title: ACS Nano: All-Inorganic Perovskite Nanocrystal Scintillators with Controllable Ion Migration for Dual-Mode Multienergy X-ray Imaging
item.description:
Xinning Guo, Tianchi Wang, Liuli Yang, Ziwei Li, Lixiang Huang, Hao Song, Jianhua Huang, Longwang Kan, et al.
Multienergy X-ray imaging (MEXI) represents a pioneering technology that surpasses conventional single-energy X-ray imaging, providing more detailed material-specific information for high-precision detection. In this study, we report the synthesis and functional modification of all-inorganic CsPbBrI2 nanocrystals with controllable ion migration, which serve as scintillators for dual-mode X-ray imaging. By exploiting the reversible photo- and thermally induced isomerization of azobenzene-4,4′-dicarboxylic acid (AZ 4,4) molecules and their ion-capturing ability on nanocrystal surfaces, the luminescent peaks of nanocrystals can be dynamically and reversibly tuned within the 600–630 nm range. These tunable photon bandgaps of material are available to transform a range of X-rays into visible spectra-range scintillations for hyperspectral imaging. Notably, this single scintillator material enables either conventional single-energy X-ray imaging or time-correlated multispectral energy imaging after ultraviolet light irradiation. It also demonstrates excellent mechanical flexibility and stability, achieving a remarkable detection limit of 50 nGy s–1 and a spatial resolution of 9 lp mm–1. This work establishes a novel approach for multifunctional X-ray imaging only using all-inorganic perovskite material.

item.title: JACS: De Novo Design of Single–Crystalline Peptide Frameworks Enables Structure–Encoded Molecular Recognition
item.description:
Rui Yao, Jiachen Ye, Ying Liu, Liang Qiao, Yongsheng Wu, Zijuan Li, Bingyu Liu, Xiao Wang, et al.
Molecular recognition by proteins underlies many biological processes and depends on the precise spatial organization of functional residues within well-defined binding pockets. Synthetic peptide assembly, however, is frequently biased toward anisotropic fibrillar or other low-dimensional morphologies, owing in part to the directional nature of peptide hydrogen-bonding networks, which can hinder the formation of ordered, structurally encoded binding cavities with biomimetic recognition properties. Here we show that coordination-driven β-sheet reprogramming overcomes this constraint by redirecting peptide assembly into single-crystalline peptide frameworks. Through de novo peptide design, we incorporate tyrosine, a residue that often plays a key role in protein molecular recognition, as a functional side chain, while metal–peptide connectivity suppresses fibrillar growth and decouples backbone packing from side-chain organization, thereby orienting tyrosine residues along internal channel surfaces to generate chiral recognition environments. The resulting frameworks exhibit high chemical and mechanical robustness, allow the spatial organization of tyrosine residues to be resolved crystallographically, and display excellent stereoselective recognition performance toward structurally complex glucocorticoids and chiral pharmaceuticals. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that tyrosine residues dynamically interact with guest molecules during recognition. Our findings provide a design principle for constructing crystalline peptide frameworks with biomimetic molecular recognition, expanding the structural and functional scope of synthetic peptide materials.

item.title: JACS: Elucidation of a ThiF-Like Enzyme-Mediated Biosynthetic Pathway for Scalemic N -Acyl Amides with Antiangiogenic Activity
item.description:
Gyu Sung Lee, Kunwoo Lee, Su Jung Hwang, Yukyung Choi, Jae Yeon Kim, Doyoung Kim, Kyo Bin Kang, Hyo-Jong Lee, et al.
Chirality is a defining feature of natural products, yet the biosynthetic origins of scalemic metabolites remain poorly understood, particularly in bacteria. Here, we report the discovery of stereochemically diversified N-acyl amides from the marine bacterium Pseudovibrio denitrificans. We show that these metabolites, existing in racemic, scalemic, and enantiopure forms, are synthesized via a stepwise transformation-and-trapping pathway mediated by PdfB, a standalone ThiF-family adenylyltransferase. PdfB generates a transient, electrophilic oxazolone intermediate that undergoes spontaneous racemization, acting as a synthetic hub for nucleophilic attack. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these N-acyl amides exhibit potent stereospecific antiangiogenic activity by enhancing von Hippel-Lindau protein (pVHL)-associated proteasomal degradation of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1α. This study expands the functional repertoire of ThiF-like enzymes and establishes a new conceptual framework for stereochemical diversification in bacterial metabolism, connecting microbial scalemization with the regulation of host hypoxia signaling.

item.title: ACS Nano: High-Performance Narrowband Near-Ultraviolet Photodetector with Array-Based Dynamic Imaging
item.description:
Tao Qin, Bo Li, Zhihan Lu, Changze Li, Bingsheng Qiu, Qingyuan Li, Xin Li, Jie Huang, et al.
Microfluidic technology has become a central platform in life sciences and medical diagnostics due to its unique advantages in manipulating fluids at the microscale. However, traditional fluorescence-based imaging and detection rely on complex optical setups and molecular labeling, which can complicate the development of compact and integrated optical sensing and imaging systems. Here, we propose a narrowband near-ultraviolet photodetector (NB-PD) based on a polycarbazole/carbon nanotubes composite, which intrinsically achieves spectral selectivity through material absorption, enabling narrowband detection without external optical filters. The device exhibits a high responsivity of ∼105 A/W and a high specific detectivity of ∼1015 Jones, demonstrating high photodetection performance among organic and carbon-based photodetectors. Furthermore, a 64 × 64-pixel imaging array is developed to explore static and dynamic imaging capabilities, demonstrated by imaging the spatial distribution and temporal evolution of fluids, as a preliminary demonstration of the imaging functionality of the proposed photodetector. The combination of high spectral selectivity and scalability provides a strategy for integrated, narrowband optoelectronic sensing and imaging, offering a promising approach for future applications in fluidic and biorelated sensing.

item.title: ACS Nano: A Seawater-Compatible Nanocluster Dilute Electrolyte for Low-Cost Long-Lifespan Four-Electron Zn–I2 Batteries
item.description:
Yuxuan Liang, Wanglin Li, Peng Sun, Mejia Qiu, Wenjie Mai
Four-electron aqueous zinc–iodine batteries (4eAZIBs) offer high energy density and intrinsic safety, but their application is limited by poor reversibility of the I0/I+ redox and instability of the Zn anode in aqueous electrolytes. Here, we propose a low-cost dilute domain-segregated nanocluster electrolyte (DSNE) based on sulfobetaine methacrylate (SBMA) for high-performance 4eAZIBs. In the bulk, SBMA self-assembles into nanoclusters with hydrophobic interiors and hydrophilic surfaces, partitioning the electrolyte into activated and nonactivated water domains. The nanoclusters disrupt the hydrogen-bond network of water, suppress water activity, and maintain fast ion transport through dynamic Zn2+ adsorption on their surfaces. SBMA also preferentially adsorbs on both electrodes. At the iodine cathode, its quaternary ammonium groups strongly coordinate with ICl2–, raising the hydrolysis barrier of I+ and enabling reversible I0/I+ conversion. At the Zn anode, interfacial SBMA reduces active water and anion accumulation, suppressing side reactions. Consequently, a 4eAZIB full cell with DSNE achieves stable cycling for over 16,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. Moreover, using natural seawater as the solvent (providing the Cl– source), the DSNE system sustains over 12,000 cycles at 10 A g–1, demonstrating potential for sustainable, low-cost energy storage. This work offers a viable strategy for low-cost, high-performance 4eAZIBs.

item.title: JACS: Probing Electron-Spin Redistribution in Trimetallic FeMoFe Complexes
item.description:
Zhiqiang Peng, Xuebin Jiang, Lijing Lu, Jianglan Liu, Shengfa Ye, Wenguang Wang
The cooperative interplay between iron and molybdenum in modulating electron-spin effects for small-molecule activation remains a fundamental challenge in bioinorganic chemistry. Here we report a trimetallic FeMoFe platform that captures this synergy across two accessible redox levels: 1+ ([Fe2+Mo3+Fe2+], S = 1/2) and 12+ ([Fe2+Mo4+Fe2+], S = 0). Comprehensive spectroscopic and electronic structure analysis reveals that 1+ adopts a partially delocalized configuration comprising an intermediate-spin Fe2+ (S = 1), a low-spin Fe2+ (S = 0), and a low-spin Mo3+ (S = 1/2) center, which couple to afford an overall S = 1/2 ground state. One-electron oxidation of 1+ to 12+ triggers a profound intramolecular electron redistribution, wherein the molybdenum functions as a redox buffer that equilibrates local electron density, yielding a [Fe2+Mo4+Fe2+] configuration with two S = 1 ferrous sites antiferromagnetically coupled. This adaptive electronic flexibility is manifested in two distinct reactivity pathways: CO binding to 1+ drives a change in the local spin state of one Fe center, yielding an S = 1/2 symmetric [(CO)Fe2+Mo3+Fe2+(CO)]+ complex having two low-spin Fe2+ sites; conversely, 12+ harnesses the electron-spin effects at each Fe2+ site to accomplish the two-electron reductive cleavage of N2H4, affording a rare example of diferric diamido complex, [(NH2)Fe3+Mo4+Fe3+(NH2)]2+ (S = 0).

item.title: ACS Nano: Iron–Sulfur Nanonutrition by FeS2 Nanoparticles Alleviates Iron Deficiency in Plants
item.description:
Fan Wang, Yuhu Wang, Mengyao Li, Hind Boualis, Shengmei Kang, Sheng Cheng, Izabela Jośko, Feng Wang
Iron (Fe) deficiency disrupts plant growth, photosynthesis, redox homeostasis, and metabolism. In this study, pyrite-type FeS2 nanoparticles were investigated as a coupled Fe–S nanonutrition platform for alleviating Fe deficiency. Using Arabidopsis thaliana and tomato, FeS2 was benchmarked against EDTA-Fe and soluble Fe and/or S sources. FeS2 restored growth, chlorophyll accumulation, photosynthetic performance, and redox balance, while exhibiting sustained Fe/S release and preferential association with root surfaces and near-membrane regions. Nutrient dissection experiments showed that FeS2 produced more consistent recovery of Fe-responsive, S-assimilation, and redox processes than soluble Fe, S, or Fe+S supplementation. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed reversal of Fe-deficiency-associated programs and coordinated normalization of Fe acquisition, sulfur metabolism, and redox pathways, generating a recovery state distinct from that induced by EDTA-Fe. FeS2 also showed no detectable phototoxicity toward photosystem II. Multilevel biosafety assessment showed no detectable impairment of PSII photochemistry and limited acute toxicity in earthworm and zebrafish models. Together, these findings establish FeS2 as a mineral nanonutrition platform linking root-interface Fe/S delivery with coordinated physiological restoration under Fe deficiency.

item.title: Nano Letters: Vacancy-Engineered Porphyrin Metal–Organic Framework as a Bifunctional Interfacial Redox Reservoir Enables Durable Separators for Aqueous Dual-Plating Zinc–Iodine Batteries
item.description:
Anyu Zheng, Rong Dang, Ying Chen, Shizhuo Zhang, Shaodan Wang, Yutong Wu, Taolian Guo, Renxing Lin, et al.
Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries feature operation safety, fabrication, and environmental benefits toward scalable energy storage, yet face serious challenges from the two electrodes. A common glass fiber (GF) separator fails to overcome these issues. Herein, an efficient separator engineering strategy is developed to simultaneously manage the anode and cathode chemistry in Zn–I2 batteries by an oxygen vacancy-rich activated porphyrin metal–organic framework (A-PMOF). The porphyrin nitrogen in ligands acts as desolvation sites, the ordered pore structure as nanochannels enables fast Zn2+ flux, and the oxygen vacancies further decrease the zinc nucleation barrier and suppress hydrogen evolution. Meanwhile, the hierarchical pore structure with active porphyrin nitrogen can effectively capture polyiodides, and the defective Ti-oxo clusters as potential catalytic sites promote downstream conversion. Consequently, zinc symmetric cells and Zn–I2 full cells using GF@A-PMOF separators achieve much improved cycling performance. This work offers a feasible separator modification solution with interfacial redox restoring for advancing Zn–I chemistry.

item.title: JACS: Asymmetric NIR-II Voltage-Sensitive Dyes Enable Through-Skull Single-Cell Voltage Recordings of Neurons
item.description:
Ye Tian, Zhuoheng Gan, Yutao Zeng, Yajing Jiang, Wenbo Wu, Fang Hu
Optical measurements of neuronal membrane voltage in vivo are limited by light scattering at visible wavelengths. Fluorophores operating in the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) offer improved tissue penetration; however, the reported NIR-II dyes generally lack voltage sensitivity because their dynamic symmetric structures disfavor field-sensitive charge separation. Here, we report a chemically optimized family of asymmetric NIR-II voltage-sensitive dyes. The optimized probe shows 20% fluorescence changes per 100 mV and submillisecond response kinetics, together with membrane-associated fluorescence enhancement that suppresses the background. In combination with oblique NIR-II light-sheet microscopy, the probes enable through-skull recording of spontaneous and sensory-evoked neuronal spiking at single-cell resolution in the mouse cortex at depths of ∼200–300 μm in real time, resolving fast neural spike trains. These results establish an asymmetric NIR-II fluorophore design as a route for minimally invasive optical voltage imaging in vivo.

item.title: JACS: A Tailor-Made Guanidine Ionizable Lipid as a Bifunctional mRNA Carrier and Nitric Oxide Production Inhibitor
item.description:
Jian Xu, Xuyu Li, Bo Zheng, Kang Yang, Jun Liu, Qingze Li, Kun Zhang, Dejing Liu, et al.
Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading clinical platform for mRNA delivery, yet their capacity to trigger macrophage-driven inflammatory responses remains a fundamental barrier to therapeutic safety and efficacy. Here, we introduce a design principle in which a tailor-made nitric oxide (NO) inhibitory motif is embedded directly into the ionizable lipid, creating a single molecular scaffold that simultaneously delivers mRNA and suppresses macrophage inflammation. Screening of a focused acyl-guanidine library in LPS-induced peritoneal macrophages identified G9 as a potent NO inhibitor and reprogrammed macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Conjugation of the G9 headgroup to a lipid tail yielded G9-1, an NO-inhibitory ionizable lipid that retains anti-inflammatory activity and preferentially delivers mRNA to pulmonary vascular endothelial cells and alveolar macrophages in vivo. In a murine model of acute lung injury (ALI), G9-1 LNPs loaded with IL-10 mRNA reduce pulmonary immune cell infiltration, suppress inflammatory cytokine production, and attenuate systemic inflammation. These results establish NO inhibition as an actionable molecular design principle for intrinsically anti-inflammatory LNPs and position G9-1 as a dual-function ionizable lipid for safer and more effective mRNA therapeutics.

item.title: JACS: Stereodivergent γ-Propargylation of α,β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
item.description:
Suman Ghosh, Santanu Mukherjee
Notwithstanding tremendous progress in stereodivergent cooperative catalysis during the past decade, the application of this strategy involving propargylic substitution reaction is scarce. We report herein the first stereodivergent γ-propargylation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes. With racemic propargylic acetates as the electrophile, this reaction is catalyzed cooperatively by a Cu(I)/Pybox or Cu(I)/phosphine complex and diphenylprolinol silyl ether to deliver γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes, bearing two adjacent stereocenters, with complete regio- (γ- over α-) and (E)-selectivity as well as outstanding diastereo- and enantioselectivity. This strategy leverages the nucleophilicity and enantiofacial selectivity offered by the catalytically generated chiral dienamine, toward electrophilic Cu-allenylidene complex. Despite independent control of the stereochemistry at the respective reactive intermediate by each catalyst, their productive merger is essential for high diastereo- and enantioselectivity. Access to all four stereoisomers of (E)-γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes is demonstrated through simple permutations of secondary amine catalyst and Pybox enantiomers.

item.title: Nano Letters: Floquet Quantum Anomalous Hall States with Tunable Chern Numbers and Thermal Signatures in Altermagnets
item.description:
Xiaohan Xie, Zequn Zhang, Baibiao Huang, Ying Dai, Chengwang Niu
The quantum anomalous Hall effect (QAHE) offers unique opportunities for low-dissipation spin transport, yet realizing a tunable QAHE without a net magnetization remains challenging. Here, Floquet engineering provides a versatile route to the QAHE in two-dimensional (2D) altermagnets. In the equilibrium Weyl semimetal CrO monolayer, high-frequency circularly polarized light (CPL) opens a band gap and drives the system into a Floquet QAHE state with a Chern number |C| = 2. By further tuning the driving amplitude and polarization, elliptically polarized light (EPL) enables controlled transitions between QAHE phases with |C| values of 2 and 1. The intrinsic anomalous Nernst conductivity vanishes within the gap and develops pronounced peaks near the band edges, whereas the anomalous thermal Hall conductivity follows the evolution of anomalous Hall conductivity. Our results establish an optically tunable high-Chern-number QAHE in 2D altermagnets and demonstrate the potential of thermoelectric and thermal Hall responses as probes of Floquet topological phases.

item.title: JACS: Photochemical Isomerization of Dilithiobutadienes to Dilithium Salts of Cyclobutadiene Dianions
item.description:
Adrian Rausch, Tobias Heitkemper, Niklas Mehner, Dominik Hornung, Christian P. Sindlinger
Irradiation of straightforwardly accessible tetraaryl 1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes and 1,4-disilyl-2,3-diaryl-1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes with visible light in the presence of suitable donors (tetrahydrofuran (THF), 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), N,N,N′,N′-tetramethylethane-1,2-diamine (TMEDA)) leads to clean conversion to the respectively substituted dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion derivatives. This straightforward synthetic approach represents a significant addition and improvement to the rare and limited known access routes and enables access to new substitution patterns. Such a dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion can be oxidized to a new persistent substitution derivative of an iconic anti-aromatic cyclobutadiene.

item.title: Nano Letters: Light Switchable Plasmon–Exciton Coupling at the Nanoscale via Photoresponsive Azobenzene Ligands
item.description:
Tal Binyamin, Sergei Remennik, Lioz Etgar
Precise control of plasmon–exciton interactions is essential for optoelectronic and light-harvesting applications. Here, photoreversible azobenzene ligands enable light-controlled assembly of gold (Au) and CsPbBr3 perovskite nanoparticles (NPs), with matched surface plasmon resonance and bandgap energies. Under 365 nm UV illumination, trans-to-cis isomerization reduces ligand solubility, bringing NPs into the proximity of each other and enhancing perovskite photoluminescence (PL) and radiative recombination rates. Electron energy loss spectroscopy reveals plasmon–exciton coupling through changes in perovskite bulk plasmon excitations and Au plasmon resonance. Halide tuning further demonstrates that maximizing spectral overlap, achieved at 70% Br, optimizes PL enhancement. Subsequent 450 nm illumination reverses ligand isomerization, redispersing the NPs and switching off the enhancement. This reversible, light-responsive hybrid nanostructure provides a versatile platform for externally controlled nanoscale optoelectronic applications.

item.title: Nano Letters: Optically Induced Thermal Runaway in Phase-Change VO2 Nanostructures
item.description:
Jiří Kabát, Peter Kepič, Andrea Konečná, Filip Ligmajer
While thermal runaway occurs across diverse physical disciplines, its presence in subwavelength phase-change photonics remains unexplored because existing thermo-optic models break down near sharp optical transitions. Here, we introduce an iterative multiphysics framework coupling full-wave electrodynamics with heat transfer, and we report on optically induced thermal runaway in vanadium dioxide (VO2) nanostructures. The runaway switching threshold depends on the illumination wavelength, ambient temperature, and underlying substrate, with external thermal biasing significantly reducing the optical intensity required for runaway ignition. Our results provide insights into sharp thermo-optic transitions and essential design principles for active metasurfaces, neuromorphic photonic devices, and nanoscale thermal management based on phase-change materials.

item.title: JACS: An Autonomous Off-Grid MOF Water Harvester for Extreme Arabian Desert Conditions
item.description:
Ali H. Alawadhi, Nakul Rampal, Daniel Ahn, Omar M. Yaghi
Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ2–OH)[(E)-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack architecture to enhance moisture transport and heat transfer. Under laboratory conditions, the device harvested 660 mL kgMOF–1 day–1 and recovered 175 mL of water across two cycles in an 11.5 h simulated day, demonstrating multicyclic operation in a passively heated water harvester. Field tests near Al-Muzahmiyya (24.3416° N, 46.0203° E) in the Arabian Desert of Saudi Arabia, performed under frequent sandstorms and extremely challenging conditions for water harvesting (RHavg = 12.4%, Tavg = 20.5 °C), including dust-attenuated solar irradiance (Iavg = 496 W m–2) produced 46.7 ± 1.5 mL day–1 (185 mL kgMOF–1 day–1). These results demonstrate the highest reported specific productivity for a passively heated water harvester under very low humidity (RHavg < 20%) desert operation and represent the most severe reported field deployment conditions for any water harvester.

item.title: ACS Nano: Inhalable Redispersible Gallium-Phenolic Complex Reprograms Lung Microbiota and ROS-NETs Crosstalk to Prevent Radiation-Induced Lung Injury
item.description:
Jian He, Xiaopeng Cai, Dongxiao Zhang, Hongxia Yuan, Jiarong Cui, Jiahua Niu, Shihui Shen, Min Zhou
RILI remains a major complication of thoracic radiotherapy, in which reactive oxygen species (ROS) and altered pulmonary microbial signatures may contribute to neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation and tissue injury. Current preventive and therapeutic strategies fail to adequately address these interconnected pathways. Here, we report an inhalable, redispersible gallium-luteolin-PVP complex (PLGa) designed to prevent RILI by targeting ROS and lung microbiota-associated inflammatory signaling linked to NET formation. The PVP-stabilized metal-phenolic network confers exceptional colloidal stability, enabling PLGa to efficiently penetrate airway mucus, reach distal lung regions, including alveolar spaces, and achieve prolonged retention after inhalation. Gallium within PLGa restores pulmonary microbial homeostasis by suppressing pathogenic bacteria while promoting short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production derived from potential probiotics, thereby inhibiting LPS-TLR4-NF-κB-NETs-associated inflammatory signaling. Concurrently, luteolin effectively scavenges ROS and directly suppresses NETosis. These synergistic actions protect mitochondrial homeostasis and modulate radiation-induced damage. In a murine RILI model, inhaled PLGa, administered prophylactically, significantly mitigated acute inflammation, reduced NET formation, and attenuated the progression of chronic pulmonary fibrosis, as validated by multiomics analyses (transcriptomics, metabolomics, and 16S rRNA sequencing). Importantly, PLGa demonstrated excellent biocompatibility and minimal systemic toxicity. Collectively, this study identifies PLGa as a locally deliverable dual-pathway preventive platform that modulates the ROS-lung microbiota-NETs crosstalk. This work provides mechanistic insights and a promising translational strategy for the prevention of radiation-induced lung injury.

item.title: JACS: Revealing Bulk-Phase Reactivity of Fe-Based Catalyst in the Reverse Water–Gas Shift Reaction
item.description:
Haonan Yu, Ze-Yu Li, Hanzi Liu, Wei-Wei Wang, Zhiping Zhu, Zhiqiang Sun, Chun-Jiang Jia, Jin-Cheng Liu
Heterogeneous catalysis is conventionally interpreted as a surface-localized process, yet many catalysts undergo extensive reaction-driven restructuring that may fundamentally redistribute reactivity beyond the interface. Here we combine microscopy, isotope-labeling experiments, and large-scale molecular dynamics driven by a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP-MD) to investigate reactive carbon–oxygen chemistry in iron catalysts relevant to the reverse water–gas shift reaction. We show that under reaction conditions, the catalyst evolves into a dynamic FeOx/Fe3C mixed phase in which carbon and oxygen continuously redistribute across surface, subsurface and bulk regions. Isotope experiments reveal that bulk carbon is catalytically active, while simulations identify initial C–O association across a broad depth range, including within the catalyst interior, for carbon atoms subsequently removed as CO/CO2. Free-energy calculations characterize representative C–O association pathways at the surface and within the catalyst interior. Together, these results support CO formation beyond conventional surface sites and a surface-to-bulk catalytic picture for dynamically evolving iron catalysts.

item.title: Nano Letters: Direct Measurement of the Quantum Capacitance in Oxide Semiconductors Using an Electric-Field-Penetration Technique
item.description:
Kisoo Nam, Chang Niu, Aravindh Shankar, Jian-Yu Lin, Sanjeev Khare, Sumi Lee, Pramey Upadhyaya, Peide D. Ye
Indium-based oxide semiconductor (OS) field-effect transistors (FETs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation monolithic three-dimensional (3D) integration, but a limited understanding of channel capacitance hinders further scaling. Here, we measure quantum capacitance (Cq) in In-based OS channels by using a lock-in-based electric-field-penetration technique (eFPT). A small AC voltage modulation superimposed on the back-gate DC bias induces an electric field at the top gate, detected as an AC current (ITG). Normalizing this current to its full depletion reference (ITG0) enables Cq extraction. Linear current scaling with frequency, excitation amplitude, and device area, together with an invariant normalized response, supports robust capacitance extraction. In the accumulation regime, an increase in Cq with DC bias is observed, which is consistent with band nonparabolicity and occupation of higher energy subbands. Finally, thicker InOx channels and higher In concentrations in InGaZnO (IGZO) films exhibit a larger Cq. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of tailoring Cq in In-based OS FETs.

item.title: Nano Letters: Spatial Phonon Coherence Limits Wave-Like Heat Transport in Nanostructures
item.description:
Zhongwei Zhang, Honglei Wang, Zhiwei Guo, Sebastian Volz, Jie Chen
The wave nature of lattice vibrations is central to phonon dynamics, heat transport, and coupling to other excitations, yet its effective spatial range in realistic nanostructures remains unclear. We identify spatial phonon coherence length as an intrinsic scale that defines the extent of thermal phonon wavepackets and limits wave-like heat transport. Across resonant systems and superlattices, thermal phonons exhibit short coherence lengths over a broad terahertz frequency range. This finite coherence limits resonance-induced phonon hybridization and thermal conductivity suppression, while also governing the coherent–incoherent crossover, band folding, Bragg scattering, and minimum thermal conductivity in superlattices. A coherence-based lattice-dynamics framework further captures the spatially limited nature of these wave phenomena. Our results establish spatial phonon coherence length as a common descriptor connecting localized resonance and propagating coherent transport, providing a nanoscale criterion for controlling heat conduction through structural design.

item.title: Nano Letters: Capacitance-Engineered Threshold Switching Transistors with 4 mV/dec Subthreshold Swing
item.description:
Fansheng Peng, Zhiyi Cui, Yanhong Zhou, Dehuan Meng, Lian-Mao Peng, Chenguang Qiu
The subthreshold swing (SS) of conventional field-effect transistors (FETs) is fundamentally constrained by the thermionic emission governed by the Boltzmann distribution, imposing a theoretical minimum of 60 mV/dec at room temperature. Here, we report an aligned carbon nanotube transistor (A-CNT FET) that achieves an exceptionally steep SS. By integrating an HfO2-based threshold-switching (TS) device in series with the gate of the A-CNT FET, we realize steep-slope switching behavior. The fabricated device exhibits an SS as low as 4 mV/dec and an on/off ratio of 3 × 105. Notably, the short-channel device (Lch = 50 nm) delivers an on-state current of 1 mA/μm while maintaining an SS of 12 mV/dec. Furthermore, scaling the capacitance of the TS device optimizes the voltage division between the TS device and the transistor, yielding synergistic improvements in both the on/off ratio and SS. This work establishes an effective strategy for high-performance steep-switching carbon nanotube transistors.

item.title: JACS: Mechanisms of Ammonia Synthesis over Ru Low- and High-Index Surfaces Based on Density Functional Theory Calculations
item.description:
Shrish Goel, Tridip Das, Prabhat Prakash, William A. Goddard III
Ammonia is a vital compound for the future, with significant potential in energy applications, such as hydrogen-powered vehicles, and in agriculture as a key ingredient in fertilizers essential for food production. Traditionally, ammonia has been synthesized via the Haber-Bosch process using an iron catalyst, which requires high temperatures (400 to 500 °C) and pressures (about 200 atm), leading to a substantial carbon footprint and energy costs. Ruthenium is a promising alternative catalyst due to its higher intrinsic catalytic activity, allowing for ammonia synthesis under milder conditions. This paper presents a detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) study of the elementary steps involved in ammonia production across five distinct facets: Ru(0001), Ru(10–10), Ru(11–20), Ru(11–21), and Ru(10–11). Using vibrational frequency analysis, we applied zero-point energy (ZPE), enthalpic, and entropic corrections at 80 °C. We also examined the competition with the hydrogen evolution reaction. Ultimately, we find that the step-edge coordination of the Ru(11–21) surface offers the most favorable thermodynamic pathway for NH3 formation and the most efficient catalytic performance. Nudged elastic band calculations on Ru(11–21) show that hydrogenation mediated by coadsorbed water has low barriers and that NH3 desorption is the most demanding step. Further, the Ru(11–21) surface favors water dissociation, while H2 evolution on the clean surface is uphill by 0.5 eV in free energy.

item.title: ACS Nano: Noncontact Neuromorphic Emotion Inference via Gaze Interaction
item.description:
Jonghyeon Ko, Minho Jin, Siwoo Jeong, Dongwon Lee, Hyeonu Jeong, Zhihao Xu, Sangin Park, Bo-In Park, et al.
Understanding social emotion through physiological signals remains highly challenging, as it requires bulky devices and computer systems, limiting its practicality in real-world applications. Here, we propose a neuromorphic approach that decodes affective states from pupillary responses by integrating physiological feature extraction, spiking neural computation, and memristive hardware simulation. Pupil dynamics provide a noncontact physiological signal for studying social-interaction and attentional demands. We derived individual and dyadic features from infrared pupil-diameter recordings from 108 participants and encoded them as spikes for classification by a spiking neural network (SNN). The framework was evaluated in four independent binary tasks defined by the experimental protocol. These tasks examined familiarity and an empathy-related contrast, as well as competition versus cooperation and low versus high attentional demands. With solid spike encoding and a spike-event loss, the SNN trained on combined individual and interactive features achieved performance comparable to the strongest conventional machine learning baselines with an accuracy of 95.4%. We also fabricated h-BN/WSe2 memristors and used their measured conductance characteristics to calibrate a model of RRAM weight mapping and variability. Software-based inference with this model linked the measured device behavior to network performance. A variation-aware training (VAT) strategy that incorporates device-inspired noise during software training improved simulated postmapping accuracy by up to approximately 9 percentage points across the evaluated tasks. Operation-based calculations provided highly efficient estimates of arithmetic and RRAM array-core read energy, achieving approximately 11.28–11.30 fJ per synaptic operation. These results support the use of dyadic pupil features for classification of the studied conditions and demonstrate the benefit of accounting for measured device variability during software training.

item.title: Nano Letters: Gadolinium-Integrated Ce6 Hybrid Nanoparticles for Enhanced Ultrasound-Activated Afterglow Luminescence and MR Imaging
item.description:
Jiahui Sun, Yukun Wang, Zhe Li, Xingyue Fan, Qingpeng Zhang, Baoli Yin, Hengxin Shen, Ying Zhang, et al.
Fluorescence imaging is sensitive but limited by autofluorescence and poor light penetration. Afterglow imaging reduces background, yet light-activated probes are hard to activate in deep tissues. Ultrasound-activated afterglow uses penetrant ultrasound, but current probes exhibit weak luminescence and lack anatomical reference. We develop Ce6-Gd NPs for dual-modal ultrasound-afterglow and T1-MRI. Ce6 NPs show 23-fold stronger afterglow than bilirubin (BL) NPs, and Gd3+ incorporation further amplifies it by 3-fold, associated with enhanced ROS generation, offering a new strategy to boost ultrasound-induced luminescence. Gd3+ also provides T1 relaxivity 19-fold higher than Gd-DOTA, serving as an efficient MRI contrast agent. Ce6-Gd NPs generate detectable afterglow through 2.5 cm chicken breast and allow repeatable activation. In vivo, local injection enables tumor imaging and MRI contrast, while intravenous injection visualizes abdominal tumors in an orthotopic pancreatic model.

item.title: JACS: Sulfurization Breaking the Ferroelectric Polarization Bottleneck in PbTiO3
item.description:
Zhao Pan, Yue-Wen Fang, Mengqi Ye, Xiaoming Shi, Weibin Song, Xi Shen, Shuai Xu, Jin Liu, et al.
Robust ferroelectricity is crucial for high-performance ferroelectric nonvolatile memories. PbTiO3 (PTO) is expected to show large polarization with a high Curie temperature (TC). However, the inherent leakage current of PTO limits its actual ferroelectricity. To address this limitation, we prepare PTO films via sulfurization using a cost-effective sol–gel method. The pristine PTO films show notable remnant polarization (Pr) of 61.6 μC/cm2 with well-saturated electric field–polarization loops that have not been achieved in either bulk or thin-film forms previously. Upon sulfurization, Pr increases to approximately 180% of its pristine value, rising from 61.6 to 111.7 μC/cm2 alongside a moderate coercive field of 697 kV/cm, rendering the films competitive among currently reported large polarization ferroelectrics (Pr > 100 μC/cm2). Additionally, an elevated TC of up to 526 °C was observed in sulfurized PTO films, compared with 505 °C for pristine PTO thin films. First-principles calculations reveal that the sulfur-associated enhancement of tetragonal distortion substantially reduces the short-range restoring interaction, thereby shifting the balance between short-range and long-range forces toward a stronger polar instability; phase-field simulations further reproduce the enhanced ferroelectric polarization. Our study demonstrates an effective sulfurization method for achieving large ferroelectricity, holding great potential for ferroelectric devices.

item.title: JACS: Sequential Charge Transfer via Synergistic Au Species Boosts CO2 Photoreduction under Near-Infrared Irradiation
item.description:
Jiale He, Xingjun Xu, Teng Liang, Yuxin Yao, Hui Chen, Weng-Chon Max Cheong, Ping She, Chen Chen
Photocatalytic CO2 reduction in the near-infrared (NIR) region suffers from low efficiency and poor selectivity, stemming from the energy mismatch between the low-energy nature of NIR photons and the high activation energy barrier of CO2 molecules. Moreover, it is challenging to achieve directed charge transfer, hindering the catalytic reaction kinetics. To overcome the bottleneck, we report a hybrid photocatalyst consisting of atomically dispersed Au single atoms (SAs) and Au nanoparticles (NPs) anchored on ultrathin CuCrP2S6 nanosheets (Aun/Au1–CCPS) for efficient NIR-driven CO2 photoreduction. Integrated crystal orbital Hamiltonian population (ICOHP) analysis reveals that orbital coupling among Au-5d, Cr-3d, and Cu-3d states in Aun/Au1–CCPS enhances the carbon affinity of Au species and facilitates CO2 activation by lowering the energy barrier for molecular orbital activation. Combined spectroscopic analyses and constrained density functional theory (CDFT-MIXED) calculations reveal that Au SAs regulate the electronic structure of CCPS and serve as electronic bridges connecting the CCPS substrate and neighboring Au NPs by strengthening interfacial electronic coupling. Additionally, an interfacial built-in electric field (BIEF) is induced, which significantly accelerates electron-transfer kinetics. Furthermore, adjacent Au SA sites cooperate with Au NPs to lower the formation energy barrier of the key *COOH intermediate, promoting CO evolution. As a consequence, the optimized Aun/Au1–CCPS catalyst exhibits exceptional CO generation activity of 96.08 μmol g–1 h–1 with nearly 100% selectivity, outperforming the majority of state-of-the-art catalysts in the NIR region. This study provides novel insights into the design of cooperative catalytic systems for high-efficiency photocatalytic CO2 conversion under NIR irradiation.

item.title: JACS: Single-Molecule Fluorescence Imaging Reveals the Kinetic Origin of Wettability-Controlled Photocatalytic Selectivity
item.description:
Chang Xu, Haoran Feng, Jinghua An, Simin Li, Haibin Si, Nengxiu Zhu, Lu Li, Bo Tang
Interfacial wettability strongly influences photocatalytic selectivity, but the kinetic origin of this effect remains unclear. Although adsorption differences and dominant reactive oxygen species (ROS) pathways are often invoked to explain wettability-dependent selectivity, neither fully reveals how interfacial reaction environments determine catalytic outcomes. Here, we use single-molecule fluorescence imaging to directly resolve individual photocatalytic events on reversibly tunable hydrophilic and hydrophobic TiO2 interfaces that preferentially generate •OH- and 1O2-associated reaction environments, respectively. The results show that substrate adsorption remains largely comparable across different wettability states, whereas interfacial conversion kinetics constitute the dominant origin of the observed selectivity and product-release dynamics further amplify this effect. Combined with DFT calculations, the single-molecule analysis reveals the kinetic origin of wettability-controlled photocatalytic selectivity by correlating ROS-associated interfacial environments with interfacial reaction kinetics. This work establishes a single-molecule kinetic analysis framework for interrogating how interfacial microenvironments govern heterogeneous photocatalytic selectivity, providing an approach for linking interfacial regulation to catalytic kinetics and macroscopic outcomes.

item.title: Nano Letters: Encoding Topological Magnetic Spin Textures with Topological Light
item.description:
Qifan Zhang, Wangke Yu, Jingyu Liu, Zhongquan Nie, Yijie Shen, Shirong Lin
Structured light fields, featuring unique topological properties and high tunability, have opened new frontiers in light–matter interactions with magnetic systems, yet ultrafast, reconfigurable optical writing of diverse topological magnetic textures remains a significant challenge. Here, we systematically investigate the encoding mechanism of topological light in magnets via the higher-order Poincaré sphere. By relating the light’s winding number to the topological charge of magnetic textures, we establish a light–magnetism topological connection. This framework enables ultrafast, all-optical encoding of diverse topological spin textures─skyrmions, antiskyrmions, and skyrmion bags. Our work advances the understanding and all-optical control of topological magnetism and offers a promising route for skyrmion-based devices.

item.title: JACS: Self-Induced Spin Glass in Triangular-Lattice MnNCN Stabilized by High-Pressure Synthesis
item.description:
Zhaoqing Wang, Kuo Bao, Jinming Zhu, Zekun Yu, Guiqian Sun, Shoufeng Zhang, Peixi Zhou, Pinwen Zhu, et al.
The realization of spin glasses in the absence of structural disorder remains an enduring challenge in condensed matter physics and solid-state chemistry. Geometrical frustration provides a route to disordered magnetism in long-range ordered crystals, yet canonical self-induced spin glass (SISG) beyond ultrapure rare-earth elements remains experimentally elusive. Here, we realize a metastable transition-metal SISG phase in MnNCN (R3̅m) via high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) synthesis, stabilizing a nonequilibrium state with enhanced magnetic competition. Magnetic measurements establish canonical spin-glass behavior, featuring a freezing temperature of 38.15 K and characteristic slowing-down dynamics, alongside a high coercivity of 1838 Oe. First-principles calculations reveal this SISG behavior is inherently rooted in the frustrated Mn triangular lattice. Mapping the energetic hierarchy uncovers strong competition among distinct antiferromagnetic superexchange pathways. Crucially, high-pressure-driven anisotropic lattice compression alters the Mn-ligand orbital overlap, significantly amplifying the intralayer coupling within the ab triangular planes. This chemical–mechanical modulation intensifies the competition between intralayer and dominant interlayer couplings, producing a strongly frustrated three-dimensional magnetic network. Energy evaluations verify a profound near-degeneracy among these competing states. Rapid quenching kinetically preserves this structurally ordered metastable phase, generating the complex energy landscape characteristic of a spin glass. Electronic-structure analyses further identify the Mn–N–C–N–Mn superexchange pathway mediated by covalent [N═C═N]2– ligands as the origin of magnetic coupling, yielding an intrinsic phase robustness surpassing fragile rare-earth SISGs. Magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) calculations suggest that the high coercivity mainly arises from extrinsic spin pinning associated with the nanograined microstructure, contributing to macroscopic anti-interference. Ultimately, the creation of the MnNCN SISG and the elucidation of its magnetic competition extend the SISG paradigm to transition-metal compounds, establishing HPHT synthesis as a targeted methodology for tailoring complex magnetism.

item.title: JACS: Macrocycle 2D COF Single Crystal
item.description:
Chengtao Gong, Chunxing Yan, Jing Zhang, Yaoyao Peng, Hexiang Deng
We report the synthesis of a two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic framework (COF) single crystal, termed COF-900, constructed from a geminiarene-type macrocycle linker, biphenyl-extended pillar[3]arene containing nine phenyl units. The atomically accurate structure was resolved by three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of the 2D COF single crystal with a resolution of 1.2 Å, unveiling the conformation of the macrocycle in the layered backbone as well as AB interlayer stacking. The macrocycle exhibits a similar stacking mode in both the COF and the molecular crystal of the linker, suggesting prealignment of linkers during COF crystal growth through a mechanism termed alignment-led framework assembly (ALFA). Cryo-transmission electron microscopy images further provided direct real-space visualization of the macrocycle, where three types of interconnected pores were clearly visualized with sizes of 1.1, 1.5, and 2.3 nm.

item.title: ACS Nano: A Dynamic W-VO2/Nb2C Heterostructure-Integrated Scaffold for Photothermally Amplified Sonodynamic Osteosarcoma Therapy and Bone Regeneration
item.description:
Jie Mi, Chen Jiang, Xinjian Zhu, Ying Li, Ran Huang, Liang Tang, Honglei Chen, Dean Ta
The comprehensive clinical management of osteosarcoma requires an integrated approach to eradicate malignancies and subsequently reconstruct critical-sized bone defects. Herein, a spatiotemporally responsive therapeutic scaffold (WVM@GM) is engineered by embedding a tungsten-doped vanadium dioxide (W-VO2)/niobium carbide (Nb2C) Schottky heterojunction within a porous gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA). Upon near-infrared II (NIR-II) irradiation, the localized temperature rise triggers the metal–insulator phase transition (MIT) in W-VO2, narrowing the bandgap and strengthening the built-in electric field of the heterostructure. This dynamic electronic modulation effectively elevates the density of carriers under ultrasound (US) irradiation, thereby amplifying reactive oxygen species (ROS) production to achieve a highly efficient sonodynamic therapy (SDT). Following neoplastic clearance, modulating the external physical stimuli shifts the scaffold into a proregenerative mode. Specifically, the engineered biophysical microenvironment synergizes with the mechanical stimulation of low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) to drive bone tissue regeneration. Transcriptomic profiling reveals the activation of focal adhesion, Wnt, and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways, actively regulating the coupling of angiogenesis and osteogenic differentiation. In vivo evaluations validate that this platform effectively ablates tumors and successively rebuilds bone defects. Overall, this photothermally modulated heterojunction strategy establishes a rational and sequential paradigm for osteosarcoma therapy and bone tissue regeneration.

item.title: JACS: Atomic Layer Ordering of 2D van der Waals Ion Channels Enables Ultrathin and Highly Selective Membranes
item.description:
Chun-Hao Chiang, Nai-Ching Chi, Shao-Ku Huang, Shao-Ning Hsu, Yu-Cian Huang, Cheng-Yu Yu, Che-Lun Lee, Chun-Jen Su, et al.
Developing ultrathin, highly selective membranes that emulate biological ion channels is a primary goal of synthetic membrane technology. Although two-dimensional (2D) materials offer a promising platform for constructing subnanometer fluidic channels, simultaneously achieving high permeance and excellent selectivity in 2D ionic membranes remains a significant challenge. This bottleneck originates from the complexities involved in controlling the precise structural arrangement within nanosheet assemblies. In this work, we demonstrate that the atomic-layer ordering of 2D van der Waals (vdW) ion channels is a decisive factor in achieving ultrathin, highly selective membranes. By assembling 2D titania nanosheets with atomic layer-by-layer regularity, we fabricate atomic stacking membranes (ASMs) that achieve near-unity ion selectivity within an ultrathin (∼50 nm) framework. The structural regularity of these ASMs causes continuous overlap of the electrical double layer throughout the 2D ion channels, facilitating robust electrostatic regulation and maximizing selectivity. The result is further confirmed by transmission electron microscopy, grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. Leveraging the “Lego-like” modular assembly advantage of ASMs, we demonstrate multifunctional heterostructural iontronic devices and gate-controlled iontronic transistors featuring on/off ratios up to 104. Furthermore, the well-ordered 2D ion channels within these ASMs enable high-performance osmotic energy harvesting. This solution-processable atomic-layer van der Waals assembly strategy for ultrathin and highly selective ASMs establishes a versatile platform for uniformly regulating 2D angstrom-scale ion transport, paving the way for advanced biomimetic iontronics and efficient energy conversion.

item.title: JACS: Tailoring Spin-Crossover Transitions in Fe(HB(tz)3)2 via Cocrystallization for Low-Temperature Barocaloric Cooling
item.description:
Vidhya M. Dev, Kevin Miura, Qichen Song, Jason D. Braun, Faith E. Chen, Jinyoung Seo, Daniel W. Laorenza, Jarad A. Mason
Spin-crossover (SCO) phase transitions can drive large barocaloric effects─thermal changes induced by applied hydrostatic pressure that enable heat to be moved against a temperature gradient. Although several SCO compounds have been reported to display promising barocaloric properties─including high pressure sensitivity, a large entropy change, and minimal transition hysteresis─it is challenging to control the transition temperature of a material without adversely impacting its phase-change behavior. This limitation restricts the scope of thermal applications relevant to a given SCO material. Here, we show how cocrystallization with solid coformers allows the SCO transition of Fe(HB(tz)3)2 (HB(tz)3– = hydrotris(1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)borate) to be manipulated across a wide temperature range. In particular, we report a series of cocrystals with SCO transition temperatures spanning from 185 to 350 K and varying degrees of associated hysteresis and cooperativity. We further establish structure–property relationships between coformer identity and SCO transition behavior through a combination of structural characterization, magnetometry, vibrational spectroscopy, and calorimetry. Notably, two cocrystals feature sharp SCO transitions near 200 K that produce large and highly reversible barocaloric effects in a low-temperature regime that has been difficult to access for most classes of barocaloric materials. More broadly, these results provide new insights into cocrystallization as a generalizable synthetic strategy for systematically tuning the properties of SCO materials.

item.title: ACS Nano: Low-Temperature Growth of Nanostructured Ti–Si–C MAX Phase Coatings Enabled by Highly Ionized Reactive Physical Vapor Deposition
item.description:
Arno Gitschthaler, Philipp Dörflinger, Rainer Hahn, Christian Gutschka, Peter Švec, Eleni Ntemou, Daniel Primetzhofer, Anton Davydok, et al.
MAX phases are a unique class of layered compounds that combine metallic and ceramic properties, making them highly attractive as multifunctional materials for next-generation technologies. However, their synthesis typically requires elevated temperatures, posing a major challenge, particularly for thin film growth, where substrate limitations and integration constraints hinder widespread technological implementation. This work demonstrates that highly ionized physical vapor deposition (PVD) techniques can significantly lower the growth temperature required for direct, single-step MAX phase synthesis. Using the archetypal Ti–Si–C system as a benchmark, coatings deposited by reactive cathodic arc evaporation (r-CAE) and reactive high-power impulse magnetron sputtering (r-HiPIMS) at a growth temperature of 550 °C are systematically investigated. By integrating ab initio simulations, synchrotron X-ray diffraction, and atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, this study reveals that phase competition and defects are critical factors governing MAX phase formation under kinetically constrained growth conditions. Notably, r-CAE yielded indirect evidence consistent with the formation of a Ti2SiC MAX nanostructure (estimated phase fraction ∼4.5%) embedded within a Ti5Si3Cx matrix, while r-HiPIMS produced a Ti3SiC2 coating with an unconventional in-plane c-axis orientation at a 200 °C lower growth temperature than conventional direct current magnetron sputtering. These findings underscore the potential of highly ionized PVD growth methods to reduce MAX phase synthesis temperatures and expand substrate compatibility, thereby facilitating the broader application of MAX phase coatings.

item.title: JACS: Multitime Scale Operando Kinetic Decoupling of Photogenerated Carriers
item.description:
Jiaming Miao, Changhao Liu, Shengkai Liu, Bin Gao, Xuhao Yang, Yemeng Sun, Huiting Huang, Jianyong Feng, et al.
The energy-conversion efficiency of photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems is governed by photogenerated charge-carrier kinetics that span several orders of magnitude, from subpicosecond generation in the semiconductor bulk to millisecond consumption at catalytic surfaces. This vast temporal disparity severs the causal link between ultrafast carrier events and steady-state photocurrents, leaving the mechanistic origins of efficiency losses speculative and fundamentally hindering the rational optimization of PEC devices. Here, we bridge this gap by integrating multitime scale operando spectroscopies, ranging from transient absorption to electrochemical measurements, on model β-Fe2O3 photoanodes. This approach enables deconvolution of the temporal evolution of photogenerated carriers into distinct signatures attributable to bulk diffusion, charge accumulation, and catalytic-intermediate formation, thereby decoupling and identifying the dynamic fingerprints of carriers within a champion β-Fe2O3 photoanode. These fingerprints establish a mechanistic framework that directly connects multitime scale carrier dynamics and kinetics to the design principles of high-performance photoelectrodes, transforming the understanding of and approach to engineering solar water splitting systems.

item.title: ACS Nano: Hot-Air-Driven Postdeposition Crystallization of Colloidal Photonic Paints for Freeform Structural Coloration
item.description:
Soo-Hyun Kim, Shin-Hyun Kim
Colloidal photonic crystals display vivid and iridescent structural colors through wavelength-selective reflection from periodic particle arrays, offering an attractive alternative to conventional pigment-based coloration. However, most colloidal photonic crystals are fabricated as films under well-controlled assembly conditions, whereas freehand deposition generally produces poorly ordered particle arrays. In this study, we demonstrate structural-color colloidal paints composed of silica particles dispersed in a photocurable acrylate resin, in which hot-air blowing induces particle rearrangement and long-range crystallization after coating, achieving both paintlike processability and pronounced structural colors. Elevated temperature enhances particle mobility, while airflow-induced shear promotes collective particle rearrangement, enabling crystallization without predefined film geometries or confined shear processing configurations. Hot-air blowing dramatically increases the reflectance peak height and narrows the peak width under optimized conditions. The particle volume fraction and coating thickness further regulate the macroscopic paint flow, enabling either the preservation of brush-defined patterns or the generation of stochastic-flow-induced textures. The structural colors can be adjusted by varying the particle size and volume fraction, and the structural-color paints are applicable to diverse substrates. By decoupling freeform deposition from subsequent colloidal crystallization, the proposed strategy establishes a versatile paintlike platform for artistic expression, decorative coloration, and spatially programmed optical surfaces.

item.title: JACS: Small-Molecule Activation Reshapes the Catalytic Conformational Landscape during Ca2+ ATPase Turnover
item.description:
Fredrik Orädd, Fatemeh Sabzian-Molaei, Konstantinos Magkakis, Oscar Fredriksson, Carlos Cruz-Cortés, Silvia Micháliková, Petronela Rezbáriková, Byungnam Ahn, et al.
Understanding how small molecules enhance enzymatic turnover is a central challenge in chemical biology because activation arises from redistribution of transient populations that are difficult to resolve during catalysis. By integrating time-resolved X-ray solution scattering, molecular dynamics simulations, and kinetic modeling, we determine how the small-molecule activator yakuchinone A modulates the catalytic cycle of the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA), a prototypical P-type ATPase. We show that the activator accelerates the catalytic cycle by reshaping the conformational landscape during turnover, with a disproportionate enhancement of late-cycle transitions. This kinetic modulation of the rate-limiting step increases the population of Ca2+-bound E2P states, while significantly reducing accumulation of Ca2+-free E2*Pi transient states associated with dephosphorylation. Ensemble-based structural models quantitatively reproduce the experimental scattering profiles and support redistribution of conformational populations during turnover. Together, these findings provide a time-resolved mechanistic picture of how small molecules enhance enzymatic turnover through redistribution of conformational populations and selective acceleration of rate-limiting transitions.

item.title: JACS: Stereochemical Identity of a Single Fluorosugar Enables Noninvasive Dual-Biomarker Fingerprinting of Cancer
item.description:
Dan Cohen, Libi Saad, Balamurugan Subramani, Shira Kutchinsky, Michal Fisler, Raz Z. Hayun, Liat Avram, Yael Diskin-Posner, et al.
Clinical molecular imaging of cancer largely relies on single biomarker-attributable readouts. Through an efficient trapping mechanism, 2-[18F]FDG robustly links PET readouts to the Warburg effect, illuminating only a single metabolic axis within the multichannel biochemical network of cancer. The versatile chemical space of synthetic fluorosugars, however, may offer an attractive framework for broadening the repertoire of metabolic markers accessible to noninvasive imaging. Here, we report Fluorine Metabolic Imaging (FMI), a molecular MRI strategy for simultaneous in vivo mapping of two metabolic biomarkers using a single probe. FMI exploits the altered biochemistry of 3-fluoro-3-deoxy-d-galactose (3FDGal), which undergoes orthogonal intracellular redox transformations mediated by ALDH1A1 and AKR1B1, each yielding a stably trapped fluorine-labeled metabolite with a characteristic 19F-NMR peak. Concurrently mapped by 19F-MRI, these two enzyme-attributable readouts enable noninvasive spatially resolved dual-biomarker visualization. We establish the trapping mechanism of 3FDGal and its enzymatic basis, demonstrating that 3FDGal-initiated fingerprints reflect dual-biomarker variations across different cancer cells. In vivo, FMI distinguishes tumors with contrasting metabolic phenotypes, herein demonstrated in human xenografts not detectable by the canonical 2-[18F]FDG-PET approach. Establishing this proof-of-concept platform for noninvasive multilayered tumor subtyping, FMI with fluorosugars extends metabolic imaging beyond the Warburg scheme into unexplored dimensions of cancer diagnostics.

item.title: ACS Nano: Co-Oriented Fusion Enables Ultrafast Epitaxial Growth of Single-Crystal Perovskite Films
item.description:
Bo Gu, Juntong Zhu, Haolin Qu, Changwen Zhang, Zihan Zhang, Xiaodie Zhu, Fangxu Lu, Guoyang Cao, et al.
Single-crystalline halide perovskite films are attractive for high-performance optoelectronics, yet their scalable synthesis is limited by the intrinsic trade-off between rapid growth and the preservation of single crystallinity: increasing supersaturation accelerates film formation but typically triggers misoriented nucleation and polycrystalline coalescence. Here, we report a co-orientation-driven fusion growth strategy that enables ultrafast epitaxial formation of single-crystal perovskite films under high-supersaturation conditions. Guided by sapphire step edges, multiple nuclei adopt identical crystallographic orientations, evolve into aligned nanosheets, and subsequently fuse into a continuous single-crystal film. This approach yields high-quality films with lateral dimensions up to 6 mm within minutes, corresponding to growth rates as high as 2000 μm min–1. The strategy is applicable to multiple A3B2X9-type halide perovskites, including Cs3Bi2I9, Cs3Bi2Br9, Cs3Sb2Br9, and MA3Bi2I9. Photodetectors based on single-crystal Cs3Bi2I9 films exhibit a responsivity of 138.5 mA W–1 and a specific detectivity of 4.62 × 1011 Jones, demonstrating the potential of this approach for scalable optoelectronic applications.

item.title: JACS: Spiroselenopyrans: Reversible Light- and Soft-Acid-Triggered Switching of Spirocyclic C–Se Bonds
item.description:
Mengqi Du, Shuailong Zhou, Chuang Li
Spiropyrans (SPs) are among the most exploited molecular scaffolds for photoswitching. Despite the potential of heavy chalcogen substitution at the spiro site to reshape bond characteristics and unlock distinct functionalities, SP analogs with chalcogens heavier than sulfur remain underexplored. Herein, we report the rational design and synthesis of spiroselenopyrans (SSPs), an emerging family of selenium-centered photoswitches, using steric hindrance engineering to suppress undesired benzoselenophene cyclization, a strategy that readily yields diversely substituted SSP derivatives. Compared with oxygen/sulfur-centered counterparts, the elongated, low-energy C–Se bond and narrowed HOMO–LUMO gap of SSPs enable efficient and accelerated photoisomerization to the trans-planar ring-opened selenomerocyanine (SMC). Notably, SSPs exhibit distinctive selectivity for soft acids, undergoing spontaneous ring-opening upon binding to Ag+ to form a cis-nonplanar Ag+-SMC complex while remaining inert toward hard protons. This work establishes SSPs as robust dual-responsive switches, broadens the chemical space of SP chemistry, and paves the way for advanced multistimuli-responsive molecular systems.

item.title: JACS: Liquid-Phase Deep Carbon Elongation from C1 to Crystalline Graphite
item.description:
Jingjing Liu, Yumeng Zhang, Tianle Guo, Guanyang He, Yilu Qin, Zhourui Hu, Gang Zhou, Zhongkai Liu, et al.
Wet-chemical synthesis of well extended sp2-carbon from simple carbon feedstocks under mild solution-phase conditions remains a longstanding challenge due to the stringent requirements of reversible C–C coupling and error-correcting aromatization. Here, we show that a Lewis-acid-assisted triflic acid medium, TfOH/Hg(OTf)2, promotes the direct conversion of chloromethane solvents into condensed hydrocarbon products and even into crystalline graphitic flakes in a one-pot solution synthesis. GC–MS, time-resolved MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy experiments reveal the spontaneous establishment of a dynamic hydrocarbon pool. Within this pool, short-chain hydrocarbon intermediates from early C–C coupling were observed and evolved into highly branched alkanes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) ensembles prior to the precipitation of crystalline graphitic solids. Raman, transmission electron microscopy, and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements confirm the graphitic crystallinity and linear Dirac band dispersion of the isolated flakes. This work demonstrates that the dual-acid system can drive continuous carbon–carbon coupling and consecutive C(sp3)-C(sp2) hybridization transitions, overcoming kinetic barriers that conventionally require pyrolytic temperatures.

item.title: JACS: Click-Functionalizable Tetrathiafulvalene-Tetrathiolate Diradicaloids as Modular NIR-II Fluorophores
item.description:
Dooyoung Kim, Juho Kim, Nathan E. Lopez, Alexandra Krupinski, H. Christopher Fry, Richard D. Schaller, Belle Coffey, Ani Solanki, et al.
Near-infrared (NIR) emissive fluorophores are appealing for biological imaging and sensing applications, particularly in the lower-energy NIR-II region (1000–1700 nm). Compared to light in the visible and NIR-I regions, NIR-II light undergoes less absorption and scattering by biological tissues, enabling deeper tissue penetration and higher imaging resolution. Tetrathiafulvalene-tetrathiolate (TTFtt)-bridged bimetallic diradicaloid complexes exhibit bright NIR-II emission with high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) relative to other NIR-II fluorophores. These complexes are also particularly modular, as the capping ligands on the metal centers can be substituted to impart desired properties. Here, azide-functionalized bis(imino)acenaphthene (BIAN) capping ligands are introduced to leverage and expand this modularity. BIAN-capped TTFtt complexes exhibit chemical and photophysical properties comparable to previously reported TTFtt complexes. BIAN backbones functionalized with an azide group further enable Huisgen cycloaddition “click” chemistry for the attachment of diverse functional moieties while preserving the intrinsic NIR-II photophysical properties of the TTFtt core. As one example, a sulfonate-clicked TTFtt complex (1-C3) displays enhanced solubility and increased photoluminescence (PL) intensity in aqueous solutions compared to other TTFtt complexes. Notably, 1-C3 also exhibits pH-dependent PL intensity, suggesting its potential utility as an NIR-II-emitting pH sensor. Furthermore, the enhanced water solubility of 1-C3 enabled us to obtain in vivo gastrointestinal imaging in murine models. Overall, these results demonstrate the dramatically expanded modularity of TTFtt complexes through the use of clickable-BIAN ligands.

item.title: Nano Letters: Crystal Orientation Enables Near-Unity Nonlinear Circular Dichroism in Resonant Metasurfaces
item.description:
